Out here in Karnataka, we love avarebele, the hyacinth bean that is best harvested in this season. And the most sought after crop comes from farmlands surrounding Magadi, a town located 70 kilometres from Bengaluru, where the soil imbues a unique aroma to the bean. In this special episode, we spend a day with farmers understanding what it takes to grow the avarekai and the careful nurture it receives before it finds its way to our plates in Bengaluru. We explore this against the context of the much-awaited ‘Shree Vasavi Condiments Avarebele Mela’, which in its 25 years of existence has showcased the myriad preparations of the versatile hyacinth bean.

Hope you enjoy this special farm to table episode. And definitely find your way to the Avarebele Mela at National College Grounds, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru, from 27th December 2024 to 5th January 2025. 

Watch our previous video on the Avarebele Mela: https://youtu.be/RVbQW3VKKDA

Life changed drastically for 15-year-old Chandru in Somanahalli, Maddur when his father passed away unexpectedly. Left with no recourse but to look after his family, he took up a job selling Maddur vade on trains for others. Twenty years on, having learnt the craft of making this popular fried fritter, and more importantly, the ‘taste of customers’, he has his own shops in Kengeri, Bengaluru where he cooks and sells his version of the Maddur Vade. And going by the thousands he sells each month, Chandru has certainly come a long way from his shaky beginnings in Somanahalli.

Originally from Chikmagalur, Lijjo Joy Kasper was introduced to the world of pizzas a decade ago during a stint in an Italian kitchen. Since then, pizzas have become centrestage for this young chef, obsessing over the right mix of flour, fermentation techniques, a zesty tomato sauce that employs both Italian and naati (country) tomatoes in a sweet, spicy and sour mix, to topping combinations that are rooted in the classic but have flavourful tweaks. A year ago, his pizza passion found home in a tiny 300 s.ft. pizzeria in Koramangala, South Bengaluru where he alongside his brother and wife dish out, through a curbside store window, an impressive range of sourdough pizzas and sandwiches. I caught him by surprise one evening when I visited to taste six of Fermentation Stories’ popular pizza combinations.

64 Mutton Pulav began as a Sunday experiment five years ago for Goutham and his cousin Abhishek to cook an old-style pulav in their home kitchen to serve neighbours and friends. Enthused by the positive response of early customers to their woodfire cooked pulav, they bootstrapped an eatery in an open plot in the North Bengaluru suburb of Yelahanka. It’s been four years since and the space has evolved to evoke a rustic, airy vibe that is popular with locals. What hasn’t changed though is the brothers’ commitment to the food, preparing the dishes personally sans any hired cooks. I dropped in unannounced one afternoon to find Goutham applying the finishing touches to the mutton pulav. What impressed me also was the fact that they only serve five or six dishes; I spent time observing them and left only after tasting some of their popular fare.

Hope you enjoy this one too. Do support small enterprises like 64 Mutton Pulav for the delicious work that they do. Happy eating!

Eight years ago, two IT professionals, Vikas Subramani and Varun Timmegowda ventured out to do something on their own. A culinary enterprise wasn’t on these engineers' minds, but their limited cumulative savings ruled out most other options. And so, they ventured into the food business with a small ‘stand-and-eat’ darshini style South Indian vegetarian tiffin eatery. With no background in the space, they invested nearly a year in learning basic recipes, honing them before opening in Jayanagar, South Bengaluru. Cut to the present, and Bengaluru Café has emerged as a hugely popular neighbourhood tiffin stop. I visited them recently to see how they operate and also to taste most of their evening tiffin menu. And in the course of doing so, also learnt of their plans to open one of Bengaluru’s largest tiffin eateries shortly.

Title: This Architect Sells His Mom’s Delicious HomeMade Vada Pav Streetside! XXL VADAPAV Bengaluru
Description:
#smallbusiness #bengaluru #streetfood 

xxl vadapav, support small business, mom and son small enterprise, vada pav in bengaluru, street food, hsr layout, rayasandra, bengaluru food tour, street food in bangalore, bengaluru food trail, gourmet on the road, kripal amanna, food lovers tv, food lovers india, truth in food

Every evening Rohan leaves home in Rayasandra with a bag full of hot vada pavs cooked fresh and packed with care by his Mom, Mrs. Hema Birajdar, for a street corner in HSR Layout, South Bengaluru, where he stands patiently for four hours to sell his wares. Not your typical-sized batata (potato) vada, these are humungous therefore deserving of its moniker XXL vada pav. I visited him on a drizzly evening recently to taste a simple but tasty vadapav, which prompted a visit to his home to meet his mother and find out more about his heartening ‘Mom & Son’ enterprise. In our first tour, we visit Mysuru, a city that has always held an allure for travellers, for its majestic charm steeped in royal heritage, architecture and its proud traditions. Alongside its fabled eateries and shops that have stood the test of time, the city has also witnessed the birth of new age bakeries, cafes and food concepts. The universe conspired yet again to bring Mark Wiens and me together, this time for a supremely delicious, robustly flavoured Thai meal at his favourite restaurant in Phuket. A 30-minute drive from Phuket town, Krua Pailin is not on the typical tourist trail, but serves wholesome, honestly priced Southern Thai dishes from a menu that is replete with exotic vegetables and greens, seafood and also some game meat. If you’re looking to taste authentic flavours, this is where to go when you are in Phuket.

My original plan was to stop at this Gonikoppal institution for their much loved breakfast that features a delicious array of dishes like crisp rice pathal with mathi (sardine) curry, puttu with kadala curry, etc. But when I made my way to their kitchen, I also stumbled upon the making of an authentic Thalassery biryani, made in a unique fashion. Needless to say, I stayed for both breakfast and the biryani. Another must-visit eatery if you find yourself in this part of Coorg!

In a short span of three years, India Sweet House has emerged as a leading traditional Indian mithai brand in Karnataka with over 30 stores. What has helped its trailblazing growth is perhaps its founding philosophy that bedrocks an organic way of life. From having its own dairy farm where cows are looked after ethically to honing culinary skills that merge traditions and innovation to present a diverse range of sweets and savoury treats across their stores in Bengaluru and parts of Karnataka. In this in depth feature, I spent a couple of days across the India Sweet House universe - from a farm on the outskirts of Bengaluru to the sweet factory and a couple of stores in Bengaluru. It is rare to come across a business that is as rooted in its vision and philosophy.

I hope you enjoy this special episode that I hope will also be a delicious harbinger of the upcoming festive season. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating and stay inspired!

There are restaurants that serve great food, and then there are those rare gems that alongside delicious culinary fare also offer a fascinating insight into culture and tradition. Cuisine Papera, helmed by Rajesh Achiah and his wife, Tanuja, is a wonderful doorway to Kodava cuisine and traditions. Housed over a floor, the restaurant displays an engrossing collection of antiques from the land. And the food is top draw too. I enjoyed my outing here, including an immersive kitchen tour and a tasting of their top dishes. Bottomline, wherever you may be in Coorg, Cuisine Papera certainly deserves a visit. You will find much to keep you occupied here.

21 years ago, long before Coorg saw the number of travellers it receives these days, Mr Girish and his wife, Pushpa set up an eatery out of their home to serve the cuisine of their land. Disregarding the safe multi-cuisine approach of most highway eateries to cater to each and everyone, the couple focused only on Kodava dishes, a cuisine that not too many knew of outside Coorg back then. This gutsy gamble seems to have paid off, for today Coorg Cuisine is ‘the stop’ for its namesake cuisine for travelers (in the know) in Madikeri. I dropped in for an impromptu lunch and was pleasantly surprised to find some delicious vegetarian dishes too, like a top notch baby brinjal fry, a mellow bamboo shoot curry, in addition to the usual non veg fare - pandi curry, mutton fry, etc. that one expects to find in this part of the state.

Definitely an eatery to visit when you are in Coorg. Hope you enjoy this watch. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

As you approach Hunsur en route to Coorg, you will find many coffee stops along the state highway. But should you fancy a taste of some delicious old-world, take a minor detour to drive towards Hunsur town. There you will find Hotel Sabari Prasad, an eatery that first opened as Mangalore Cafe nearly 70 years ago, and to this day holds on to that era in its old world (read as extremely spartan and rustic!) decor and a wood fired dosa tava that dishes out the popular benne masala set and a unique jeera (cumin) dosae. And the coffee served here too is the sort that’s a befitting cup enroute to coffee country, Coorg!

On my return trip from Udupi, I stopped at this rustic eatery just outside the foothills of Agumbe and made a light breakfast of a delicious neer dosae and chutney. The most impression-able aspect of Sri Sathyanarayana hotel, Seethanadi, though is its owner Mr. Anil Kumar Shenoy, whose sincere and infectious enthusiasm lingers long beyond the fleeting minutes one spends here. Also, noteworthy are the cottage industry preparations and edible knick knacks one can carry from the store. Definitely an interesting stop to pencil into your itinerary if you find yourself on the road here.

In a small village in Kundapur taluk, sits a nondescript eatery by the wayside. If you step in, you will find Mr. Subramanya Holla hunched over a large cast iron pan, ladling batter, smearing masala, lashing streams of ghee and throwing in chunks of butter to make a special benne masala dosae. It’s a craft that he has mastered over 43 years, and he serves only the dosae and a sajjige vade alongside, that too for only four hours each evening! But such is the popularity of Guru Canteen, Halady that people don't mind changing their travel routes just to get a taste of his dosae. On my recent visit to South Kanara, I too made a 100-kilometer return trip to experience this dosae at this family-run eatery. Was it worth the effort? Well, I polished two butter laden, utterly scrumptious, flavourful dosae back to back!

I found my way to this 30-year-old home eatery on a rainy morning in Udupi,  where I was rewarded with a satisfying breakfast prepared by the lady of the house, Mrs. Sanjeevini Bhat, who also doubles up as the only cook in the kitchen. I tried a scrumptiously delicious jackfruit ‘mulaka’ that I instantly fell in love with and some more of the fare at this tiny eatery that though known to the locals is perhaps not as known (yet) to travellers yet. When in Udupi next, do check out Hotel Vanishree, and by the way, they are perhaps also the first eatery to open doors here at 615 every morning. Hope you enjoy this one as much as I did.

Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

10/10

8/10

8.5/10

Buns

avalakki 9/10, uppittu 7/10

7.5/10

When I found myself in Mangalore during the monsoon season, I was wondering what I should taste. Seafood is scarce as there’s a deep sea trawling ban in force to help the ocean regenerate its marine stock. Whatever seafood is available is either sourced from the East coast or caught locally around the harbour or in estuaries along the coastline. It was against this backdrop that I received an unexpected call from Mrs. Komal Prabhu, the livewire restaurateur and culinary force behind Maharaja Restaurant invited me to a very special lunch of seasonal delicacies that were found only during this season - forest colocasia, foraged greens, thunder mushrooms, country mango, jackfruit, pickled mackerel, dried shrimp and more. I quickly accepted and found myself relishing some truly authentic GSB delicacies, many dishes that I hadn't tasted hitherto. I hope you enjoy this special monsoon episode too.

Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

This was an invitational meal. The dishes are subject to availability and have to be pre-ordered in advance, but are definitely worth the advance planning and effort.

A native of Kodagu, Manoj Thammaiah missed the authentic meaty flavours of Coorg in Bengaluru. And so he set up a street cart to cook and sell pork based dishes in the evenings, whilst holding a job in an export firm during the day. That was seven years ago. Encouraged by the steady, encouraging response of customers over the years, he has now given up his job and expanded to a tiny shop, Coorg Style Pork Corner, in BTM 2nd Stage, Bengaluru where he and his wife cook delicious preparations to recipes from their home. Title: This Couple Serves A Tasty, Homely Biryani For Rs. 100 Only! SUBBANNAS BIRYANI Bengaluru

subbannas biryani, biryani eatery, wilson garden, near lalbagh park, bengaluru, bangalore, chicken biryani, chicken kabab, chicken fry, biryani shop, homely biryani in bangalore, cheap, value for money biryani, support small business, bengaluru food tour, bangalore food walk, bangalore food trail, karnataka food tour, support local, gourmet on the road, kripal amanna, food lovers tv, food lovers india, truth in food 

Three years ago, Subbanna and  his wife, Jamuna began a small biryani eatery in the ground floor of their home in Wilson Garden, a neighbourhood near Lalbagh in Bengaluru. In the construction business by profession, but passionate about cooking from an early age, Subbanna wanted to serve a homely chicken biryani cooked to his mother's recipe to patrons. The menu at Subbanna’s Biryani includes only a chicken kabab, chicken fry and the chicken biryani, sold at only Rs. 100 for a fairly adequate portion. Just because it is priced low doesn’t take away from the care that the couple shower upon their dishes, with the husband making the trek to the market every morning to procure the ingredients before returning to the kitchen to cook. I fell in love with the honest, homely appeal of this modest eatery, and am sure you will like it too. 

Hope you enjoy this episode, part of our special initiative to shine a bit of light on unsung eateries that are doing good work.

Venkatesh and his parents began Sri Vinayaka Condiments, a small tiffin eatery, 24 years ago. His father fell ill and they were forced to relocate to the garage of their home nine years ago to tend to him and to also run their store in whatever little manner they could. The first few years were tough, with customers far and few in their neighbourhood located in the farthest corner of Banashankari, South Bengaluru, Venkatesh says, “sales were hardly a few rupees.” However, over time the soft, melt-in-the-mouth quality of their idli, their crunchy vada and khaara bath, the only three dishes they serve here, have acquired quite a following. Title: From Losing Everything To Building 50 Restaurants! Lunch With SANGEETHA Chennai Founder, Mr. Suresh!
Description:

sangeetha veg restaurant, adyar, chennai, most popular veg restaurant in chennai, sangeetha veg, tamil nadu meals, lunch at sangeetha chennai, sangeetha veg restaurant chennai, sangeetha restaurant owner, suresh, inspiring story, kitchen tour, veg meals, best chennai food, chennai food tour, chennai food walk, chennai food trail, tamil nadu food tour, chennai food series, support local, gourmet on the road, kripal amanna, food lovers tv, food lovers india, truth in food 

45 years ago, a young lad found himself at a difficult crossroad.He was interested in photography and cinema, but the financial situation at home compelled him to give up his education and take up a job in a restaurant. Working 18 hours a day, life was tough, he spent many nights with no roof over his head. Things got better, when he and his family set up two restaurants in Chennai. Unfortunately, the restaurants failed and they had to begin all over again. This is hardly the kind of backstory one would expect to hear of Chennai’s iconic Sangeetha vegetarian chain of restaurants. But these are exactly the kind of challenges Mr. Suresh and his family endured to build 50 restaurants over the years. I caught up with him at their flagship Adyar restaurant, where I relished a delightful Tamil Nadu meal which in addition to highlighting the cuisine of the land is also accommodative enough to encompass flavours beyond the borders of the state. 

I hope you enjoy my last saapad from this Gourmet On The Road, Chennai tour. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

I spent the greater part of an afternoon exploring the kitchens here and left only after partaking of most of their popular dishes including a delicious vegetarian meal and mutton biryani. If you have a sweet tooth and find yourself in Chennai, this 108-year-old sweet shop in Zam Bazaar, Triplicane is a must visit. Especially for its dum ka roat, a delicious baked dessert of semolina, khoa and ghee that has all of Chennai flocking here. My other favourite from a quick tasting here was their ande ki mithai, a rich cake-like-texture creation that belies its core ingredient in its subtle flavour and aroma. The popularity of this Chennai institution has spawned imitators, so make sure you head to the original store in Zam Bazar, Triplicane to get your share of their iconic sweet treats.

I hope you enjoy this episode from Gourmet On The Road, Chennai. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

You know I love my dosae - watching it being made, learning what makes each version special, and savouring it with joy. Imagine my excitement then to learn of dosae history being made, right here in Namma Bengaluru. Well, that’s exactly what MTR Foods chose to do to celebrate 100 years of MTR’s iconic culinary legacy. In a move truly befitting of the time, the chefs at this food brand chose to shatter the previous Guinness record for the world’s longest dosa. The dosae is iconic and fabled here in Bengaluru, and now it stands tall, or should I say long :-), with this Guinness record - the world’s longest dosae. This iconic Chennai landmark has spawned many branches, but those in the know head to the original outpost on Mount Road that began in 1951 when its founder Mr. A. M. Buhari returned to Chennai from Colombo with his eponymous restaurant post Indian independence. Back in the day, the restaurant was associated with a number of firsts, the first espresso machine, the first jukebox, and the first eatery to serve its patrons in fine, imported bone china. Today though, Buhari is perhaps most famous as the place where the chicken 65 was invented. I tasted their creation and was surprised to find it unlike any other version that passes off as a dish. Also partook of the other popular rituals here - the bun butter jam, mutton samsa with tea, mutton biryani et al.

I’ve eaten in Kappa Chakka Kandhari, Bengaluru, and it was a great meal all right, but when I found myself in Chennai recently, I had to visit its first restaurant, which also gave me an opportunity to share a table with my dear friend, Chef Regi Mathew after 25 years. For those who don’t know him yet, this culinary doyen, a master in many cuisines, has made it his life’s work to promote regional cuisine, especially that from his homeland Kerala. The dishes that I tasted at this lunch were the sort that left an indelible impression on my palate. Made to age old home recipes, sourcing the best ingredients from God’s own country - tender jackfruit, breadfruit, chinese potatoes, pearl spot fish, mussels and more -  Chef Regi’s menu is a triumph in showcasing regional Malayalee cuisine. And has also, deservedly, earned him a recent accolade as India’s top chef.

The next time you find yourself in Chennai or Bengaluru, definitely book a table at his restaurant. Hope you enjoy this episode. Stay tuned for more from Gourmet On The Road, Chennai. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

Title: Chennai’s Popular Biryani Shop, YAA MOHAIDEEN Pallavaram Began As A Push Cart 30 Years Ago!
Description:

Chennai loves its biryani, and when it comes to the city’s most popular biryani kadai (shop), many point in the direction of Yaa Mohaideen, an enterprise that first came to life in a push cart nearly 30 years ago. Now with branches and restaurants across the city, old timers still prefer to visit its first outlet in Pallavaram, in the southern part of the city, where it is de rigueur to queue for and taste the biryani, whilst standing! We tasted both versions of the Yaa Mohaideen biryani, chicken and mutton, and also a couple of popular sides. 

Hope you enjoy this biryani episode. Stay tuned for more from Gourmet On The Road, Chennai. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

A few months ago, I featured an episode with a brave lady entrepreneur who despite facing physical hardships after a serious accident had given up an IT job to pursue her passion in food. Your response to it was amazing, and soon Veena’s Kari Dosa street food stall was thriving. Until one day when she returned to her spot to find that the entire lot had been razed to the ground!  

Left with no recourse but to begin from scratch again, this time Veena opted for the safety of a shop. Pooling her savings and borrowing some more, she has set up a small Kari Dosa shop in BTM 2nd Stage, Bengaluru. However, the going has been anything but smooth with poor sales and not enough people knowing of her delicious fare. So, she reached out to us requesting support for her enterprise. I rarely ever do this, revisit a place for an episode in less than a span of six months, but I felt this delicious initiative had to be supported. I hope you enjoy the episode and will also be motivated to support Veena’s Kari Dosa stall.

Title: Everyone Stops At Ashok Anna Hotel For Kappa Rotti! LAXMI JANARDHAN Yermal,  Mangalore Udupi Highway
Description:
#ashokannahotel #yermal #mangalorehighway
 
hotel laxmi janardhana, yermal, ashokanna hotel yermal, mangalore udupi highway, kappa rotti, mangalore udupi highway, kappa roti chicken curry, veg curry, breakfast stop, highway stop, mangalore food tour, south canara, mangalore food trail, karnataka food tour, support local, support small business, gourmet on the road, kripal amanna, food lovers tv, food lovers india, truth in food 

What began 20 years ago as a highway stop to provide breakfast sustenance to truckers has now morphed into a must-visit on the informed traveller’s itinerary for its comforting, earthy kappa rotti, a fluffy rice flatbread cooked on a clay pan minus sans any oil. The thing to do is to taste it with the thick curries, chicken or vegetarian, that are dished out by Ashok Anna and his family at this eatery, Hotel Laxmi Janardhana, located in a town called Yermal, about 30 kilometres from Mangalore. The setting is quite rustic, and the crowd an eclectic mixed lot. But it is the food that rules here, as I discovered during a busy morning here. 
Hope you enjoy this one. Take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

When I walked in for breakfast and perused the menu at this 60-year-old eatery located right opposite Ernakulam’s historic Siva temple, I couldn't help but wonder if there was a connection to Udupi. A fact that was corroborated by the owner, Mrs. Meena Mohan, whose husband’s family migrated from South Canara nearly a century ago to perform religious duties in Kochi. And Gokul Ooottupra, too, seems to cater to its patrons in the same attitude of service and tradition, I discovered over my leisurely meal here. From staple classics like the vada, dosae, kadla puttu curry, yelle adda to a few inspired creations like the peri peri idli, the vegetarian fare here is the sort that draws in customers by the hundreds each day. If you find yourself in Kochi and are craving a vegetarian meal, look no further. Hope you enjoy this watch. Take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

Drive 30 kilometres outside Shimoga, past areca nut plantations, serene forest scapes, and the roar of the mighty Tunga river, to Mandagadde, a village known for its bird sanctuary and equally popular eateries that proffer a variety of freshwater fish delicacies. In this episode, I visit Bhavani Fish Hotel, a rustic dining spot set in a home that began the Mandagadde fish tradition 27 years ago. I met the owner, Ramesh Rao and his family to learn what makes the Mandagadde fish special, and also savour some of the delicacies on offer. When in Shimoga, definitely make the trek here; the fry and curries certainly are worth the effort.

Description:

When Mrs. Geetha Shivkumar saw farmers unable to sell their stock of avarebele (hyacinth beans) 25 years ago, she co-opted them into an initiative that would make use of this delicately flavoured ingredient in a myriad of savouries, sweets and snacks. What began as a humble initiative out of her home then has today bloomed into an inspiring ‘farm to table’ movement, the Shree Vasavi Condiments Avarebele Mela that has spread awareness on this humble bean and also provided much needed livelihood to many farmers in Karnataka. 

Now in its 24th year, this festival is being staged in a large venue at the National College grounds, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru from 5th to 9th January. Hope this episode inspires you to visit this one-of-a-kind culinary festival and savour the avarebele in a variety of tasty forms. Take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

Raghavendra was employed in a bakery 33 years ago when he decided to set up a small business on his own. His original thought was to set up a stationery store requiring minimal capital, but given his interest in food, he began experimenting with all sorts of snacks and condiments and soon hit upon combinations of chaat. Thus was born Harshini Condiments in a tiny bylane of Ravindra Nagar in Shimoga. The fare here is chaat but in a healthier avatar. Think ingredients like fresh fenugreek, banana stem, cabbage, pomegranate, corn, et al tossed together with savoury elements of crunch and punchy homemade chutneys. Creations that are not only wholesome but also hit home in the flavour department. A must try for street food lovers when in Shimoga! Happy eating!

When I survey a new city for a Gourmet On The Road series, I usually invite recommendations from viewers, and post due diligence and research, these form the basis for what one eventually explores. When I called out for Shimoga, this restaurant received the most recommendations. And those in the know may not be surprised given the fact that Sri Meenakshi Bhavan has been an integral part, actually a pioneer of the city’s culinary landscape for over a century now. The space that it occupies was once the owning family’s ancestral abode and that energy also seems to permeate through the homely old-fashioned decor and the South Canara inspired fare here. The food is tasty, sumptuous and satisfying, made to traditional recipes by cooks, many who have served in the kitchens here for decades. Whilst the benne masala dosae may come as the most recommended dish, the vade, avalakki mosaru, paddu too are as rewarding as I found during a breakfast visit where I also had the opportunity to converse with the restaurant’s third generation owner, Mr Chandrashekar and his daughter, Ganavi.

If you are in Shimoga, or are making plans to visit, this is one eatery you must not miss. Hope you enjoy this breakfast episode. Take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

When it comes to chaats, every city has its own style, and Shimoga is no different. Be it the masala puri, sev puri or paani puri, each one hits differently as I discovered during this outing to DVS Circle Pani Puri, a chaat shop that has held sway over the city’s penchant for its spicy fare for nearly four decades. I was told these unique flavours were a result of Shimoga’s purveyors not being influenced by chaat traditions of the North and therefore developing a unique palate of their own. Hope you enjoy this streetfood outing; take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

And so when I recently did a tour of Shimoga, the Venkatesha Sweet House Mysore Pak was top of my list. When in Shimoga, definitely visit this 60 year culinary institution.

Over 40 years ago, Mr. Chandrashekar, originally from Sasthan in Dakshina Kannada, had to wind up his long running restaurant in Shimoga during the emergency. Forced to once again begin from scratch, he chose a spot in Birur, then a sleepy village around 240 kilometres from Bengaluru to set up an eatery. Since then Birur has grown to a bustling trading town, the spot where his venture, Preethi Canteen stands, is now a busy highway. And this tiffin restaurant has been elevated to legendary status by its many patrons for whom a halt here is a must when on the road around here. Over time, I have received many requests to taste their iconic masala dosae, and so on a recent drive to Shimoga, I stopped here and caught not just a taste of their tasty fare, but also a conversation with its second generation owner, Mr. Prakash Holla on what makes Preethi Canteen a hugely popular culinary institution.

Hope you enjoy this tiffin episode; take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

A couple of years ago when we were all stuck at home during the pandemic, I was craving for a donne biryani. That’s when I chanced upon RNR donne biryani on a delivery app. I had never heard of them before, and so Intrigued, I ordered. And was pleasantly surprised with what I tasted, so much so that I even filmed an impromptu vlog. 

Now whilst most businesses that opened during this period to cater to consumers at home were unable to make it beyond the pandemic, RNR has not only survived but scaled across multiple kitchens (at last count there were 18!) in the city and also a couple of restaurants on the back of the popularity of its donne biryani that is made to a family recipe. In this episode I visit their newest restaurant in RT Nagar, Bengaluru, where I catch up with Ramya Ravi, co-owner of the chain, who articulates that “their vision is to take Bengaluru’s donne biryani offering across the country!” And going by what I witnessed during the step by step making of their signature chicken donne biryani, and also what I tasted, they certainly seem to be on the right path to doing so.

I hope you enjoy this biryani making episode. Take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

Description:

mahalakshmi tiffin room, mltr, basavanagudi, south bengaluru, tiffin eatery, vegetarian, khaali dosae, dosa, idli, vade, sambar, carrot halwa, mangalore bajji, goli baje, coffee, must try dosa spot, bangalore food trail, bengaluru food tour, karnataka food tour, gourmet on the road, kripal amanna, food lovers tv, food lovers india, truth in food

When it comes to tiffin eateries in Bengaluru, there are those that are celebrated, even venerated, and splashed across media, both traditional and new. Nothing wrong with that. And then there are those that quietly go about their work, serving customers for decades on end, content to not bask in the limelight. A great example of the latter is Mahalakshmi Tiffin Room in Basavanagudi, South Bengaluru, though open since 1926 is still unknown to most in the city. I visited them one afternoon to meet the second and third generation owners, and to also taste an assortment of their honestly-priced fare, including a deliciously light and fluffy khali dosae and a satisfying sambar. Hope you enjoy this tiffin episode; take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

A former corporate executive, Pooja Patil realized her heart was in food, more specifically the regional specialities and dishes of her family, originally from Solapur in Maharashtra, but Bengaluru residents for decades. Honing recipes, adding her touch, she opened Maskaa, a small, cosy café in Koramangala, to serve comfort fare - from vada pav, thaalipeeth, sabudana vadas, misal pav, pav bhaji, omelets, paneer bhurji, even a couple of interesting chicken dishes, and in sync with the eatery’s name, a butter-laden bun that pairs deliciously with a masala tea, brewed with a secret blend of 17 spices prepared by her father.

I dropped in for a ‘snacky’ lunch one afternoon to chat with this enterprising lady entrepreneur, and also taste some of her dishes. Definitely check out Maskaa when in the neighbourhood and support this unique initiative. Hope you enjoy this one; take care, safe and strong. Happy eating!

Title: This 15 Rs. Thatte Idli Took Him From Street Cart To Own Shop In 2 Years! AKASH KUNIGAL THATTE IDLI
Description:
#thatteidli #streetfood #bengaluru

thatte idli, akash kunigal thatte idli, banashankari, south bangalore, bengaluru, street food, best tomato rice, masala vade, masala dosae, dosa, thatte idli in bangalore, inspiring story, support small business, must try dosa spot, bangalore food trail, karnataka food tour, gourmet on the road, kripal amanna, food lovers tv, food lovers india, truth in food

Channe Gowda moved to Bengaluru from his native place, Kunigal 10 years ago to eke out a living and supplement his family’s marginal farming income. He tried his hand at many a job and trade, barely managing to make ends meet. A couple of years ago, he set up a food cart in Banashankari, South Bengaluru on the back of non vegetarian recipes gleaned from his well wishers. This too met with limited success, it was at this point that he introduced a thatte keeping in mind the clientele in the area. And that was when things changed. His soft and spongy 15 rupee thatte idli served with butter and two delicious chutneys caught the attention of locals and demand grew to an extent that he gave up the non veg menu to only focus on the idli, vade and a single rice preparation. Unable to cope with the stream of customers, Channe Gowda eventually moved operations to a house in the area, from where he continues to serve hundreds of his now famous Kunigal thatte idli each day. 
From a street cart that would barely support him, he now provides livelihood to a team of fifteen! I set out this evening to meet this hard-working gent, and in the course of doing so, not only tasted his satisfying idlis, but also stumbled upon a flavourful tomato rice that he makes to an aromatic biryani recipe.

I hope you enjoy this inspiring tiffin thindi outing. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

Title: This Hidden Eatery Serves Delicious Family Cooked Karnataka Dishes! KUTUMBA KITCHEN

kutumba kitchen, new bel road, bangalore, karnataka cuisine, family owned restaurant, bengaluru, mysuru, hassan, local cuisine, mutton chops, mutton palav, chicken biryani, mushroom biryani, ghee roast, chicken curry, akki roti, thatte idli, badam halwa, support small business, family business, bangalore food trail, karnataka food tour, gourmet on the road, kripal amanna, food lovers tv, food lovers india, truth in food

About a year ago, I received a request from a family that had just opened a cloud kitchen to serve dishes made to family recipes handed down through generations. Much as their fare - a smorgasbord of meaty regional Karnataka delicacies seemed interesting - we couldn’t explore it further as we rarely ever cover cloud kitchens. Emboldened by the interest from customers, the family eventually set up a small eatery to seat all of 10 in the setback of a building on New Bel Road, North Bengaluru. And this of course, provided me with just the excuse to make the trek to Kutumba Kitchen, meet the family and taste some of the dishes that have earned this small enterprise quite a few fans in a short span of time.

Hope you enjoy this one, please do your best to support deserving small businesses like this. Take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

It had been a while since I had filmed a biryani making episode. And so when the opportunity arose to film the complete process of a biryani whose recipe has remained constant for over a century, I lost no time to head to Taj Hotel Shivaji Nagar, an eatery that  dates back to the early 20th century, and today churns out over 500 kilos of biryani each day. I met with the third and fourth generation of the family of the late Janab Abdur Rahman, who are committed to preserving the ancient traditions that go into the making of their biryani, including cooking it over a wood fire only.

Hope you enjoy this very special biryani making episode. Take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

Title: This Brave Lady Gave Up IT Job To Pursue Her Food Passion! Must Try KARI DOSA, Rs.10 Veg Dosa
Description:
#karidosa #streetfood #bengaluru

kari dosa, street food, kari dosae, kari dosai, kari dosa in bangalore, chicken kari dosa, prawn kari dosa, veg curry dosa, egg dosae, jp nagar, south bengaluru, lady entrepreneur, support small business, must try dosa spot, bangalore food trail, karnataka food tour, gourmet on the road, kripal amanna, food lovers tv, food lovers india, truth in food

A few weeks ago, I heard of a lady entrepreneur who despite facing physical hardships after a serious accident had given up an IT job to pursue her passion in food. Resources were limited, so she set up a small streetside stand. Extremely hardworking, Veena’s day begins at 4 in the morning when she wakes up to prepare the dosae batter, curries, thokku and kurmas that go into her delicious kari dosa. After sending her two young children to school, she arrives at her stand in JP Nagar, South Bengaluru, where customers queue up to savour her scrumptious fare that begins as low as Rs. 10 for a delightful plain dosae with spicy peanut chutney and aromatic vegetable gravy, and Rs. 30 for an egg topped version. What lends the stall its name though are the Tamil Nadu style kari dosai, chicken and my favourite, a prawn thokku topped dosae. If you love dosae, especially the non vegetarian kind, head here. And in doing so, you will also be supporting a deserving small enterprise.

Hope you enjoy this find; take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

Title: Is This India’s Oldest Running Bakery? 143 Years Old NEW IMPERIAL BAKERY, KGF KOLAR GOLD FIELDS
Description:
#indiasoldestbakery #newimperialbakery #kgf

new imperial bakery, india’s oldest bakery, 143 year old bakery, kolar gold fields, kgf, karnataka, wood fired oven, veg puff, dil pasand, muffin, coconut biscuit, spicy cookies, vanilla cookies, old fashioned bakes, plum cake, bread, karnataka food trail, kolar food tour, near bengaluru, bangalore, small business, support small business, gourmet on the road, kripal amanna, food lovers tv, food lovers india, truth in food

On a recent road drive through Kolar, we made a detour to Kolar Gold Fields, once famous across the world for its gold mines. The mines have long closed, and the town is now a pale shadow of its former glory. What has endured however is a bakery that first opened in 1880 and still continues to dispense its baked wares in an old school tradition that harks back 143 years! I met its fourth generation owner and also tasted many of the scrumptious treats on offer that are still popular with the inhabitants of this verdant town 70 kilometres from Bengaluru.

Hope you enjoy this one. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

Note: I enjoyed most of the baked treats on offer. Standouts for me though were the veg puff, muffin (dilpasand), coconut biscuit, spicy cookies and plum cake.
Biscuits are priced at Rs. 30 for 100gm, the puffs and muffins at Rs. 13, and a loaf of bread, Rs. 30.

I recently discovered this restaurant that although open at Bengaluru Airport City for a few months now, is largely unknown to food lovers in the city. Fronted by a veteran chef with a creditworthy reputation for North Indian cuisine, the food at Maa Da Dhaba certainly delivers. From punchy kebabs to silken dals and robustly flavoured curries and kadais, there is a popular selection of Sino Indian fare on the menu too. What also adds to its appeal is the pleasant drive to get here and its location - only a couple of minutes to the airport terminal but yet far removed from its bustle. Definitely check it out, and yes, at prices that are quite honest too.

Hope you enjoy this find; take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

Amongst the many culinary traditions that prevail in this state, an interesting one is that of Maratha-Karnataka fare. A cuisine that took birth a few hundred years ago when Marathas migrated to Karnataka and settled into the local culture and practices of the land. Over time, their food evolved to assimilate local produce and ingredients. Many of the ‘military’ eateries in and around Bengaluru trace their roots to this style of cooking, although the offerings of some have morphed beyond recognition. To find examples of this unique fare that is comparatively true to its origin, one has to travel a bit out of the city. Like this 70-year-old eating house that we discovered in Malur, a town located 50 kilometres from Bengaluru. Where rustic meaty preparations are cooked with home made masalas over wood-fired stoves.

Hope you enjoy this lunch at Venkob Rao Mess. Take Care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

It was wonderful to meet tennis ace, our very own Bengaluru boy, Rohan Bopanna, soon after his return from Wimbledon and being recently ranked World No. 7 for the second time in a decade. However, his constant travel on the circuit has meant that there are aspects of namma ooru that he hasn’t been able to explore yet, including Mavalli Tiffin Rooms in Lalbagh. And so we took it upon ourselves to introduce this icon to a Bengaluru tiffin legend over a leisurely, indulgent-breakfast conversation where we also caught a glimpse of his passion for coffee, and his role as the ambassador for the World Coffee Conference, to be held in India for the first time in our city in September.

Hope you enjoy this tiffin talk. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

Title: Tried The Famous HOSKOTE KABAB & Hoskote Chicken Biryani For First Time! RAVI KABAB CENTER
Description:
#ravikabab #hoskotekabab #hoskotebiryani

ravi kabab center, ravi kabab hoskote, hosakote, chicken kabab, fried chicken, egg rice, chicken biryani, quail fry, fish fry, non vegetarian restaurant, hoskote kabab, hoskote biryani, ravi kabab centre, hidden gem in hoskote, hoskote food trail, hoskote food tour, near bengaluru, bangalore, must try street food, gourmet on the road, kripal amanna, food lovers tv, food lovers india, truth in food

Almost everyone has heard about and many have tasted the early morning biryani at Hoskote, a pre-sunrise ritual 40 kilometers from Bengaluru. However, few visitors seem to know about a fried kabab evening tradition that is hugely popular with locals. On a drive back from Kolar a few weeks ago, we took a detour into this highway town to savour a quick meal of chicken kabab, egg rice, and a chicken biryani too. The last wasn’t on our plan, but then, we were in biryani country after all. Definitely check out Ravi Kabab Center when in the area, and be prepared to jostle with the crowd to get your share of bisi bisi (hot) kababs.

Hope you enjoy this one. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

I had heard much about this tiny eatery located in a bylane of old Mysuru, especially of its biryani that back in the day would be cooked over a wood-fired stove. And so when I received recommendations in response to a recent “where should I lunch in Mysuru” post, I lost no time in making tracks to Nasheman. The place is drab, and that’s putting it mildly, a handful of tables sit cheek by jowl in a modestly-sized room, and the service is industrial at best. But it is the mutton biryani here and other meaty delicacies, especially a delicious twice cooked mutton phaal that draw customers to this 50-year-old restaurant. In this outing, I tasted most of what was on offer for lunch, after an insightful kitchen tour.

Title: HOTEL ADITYA Super Naati Non Veg Oota In Classy Ambience! Tasty Mutton, Chicken Fry, Biryanis & More
Description:
#hoteladitya #mahalaxmipuram #bangalore

hotel aditya, mahalaxmipuram, hotel aditya non veg, naati oota in classy setting, non vegetarian restaurant, chicken biryani, mutton biryani, mutton nalli fry, brain pepper dry, kaal soup, chicken fry, chicken kabab, bengaluru, bangalore, food tour bengaluru, must try restaurant in bangalore, bangalore food tour, bengaluru food trail, support local, gourmet on the road, kripal amanna, food lovers tv, food lovers india, truth in food

Over the last few months, I had received numerous requests from our viewers to visit Hotel Aditya in Mahalaxmipuram, a eatery that in just over 12 years has managed to create for its local non vegetarian fare the sort of fan loyalty that some of Bengaluru’s revered culinary institutions have taken multiple decades to garner. The people behind the eatery are extremely low profile, preferring to let their food do the talking, and therefore reluctant to let cameras in. Which is also why you may not have seen a single in depth video or feature on the place thus far. 

We managed to get our cameras not only into the restaurant, but also deep in the kitchen where we took an in-depth look at the making of some of their iconic dishes, from the meaty curries to the terrific biryanis and fries. The best part we found at Hotel Aditya, not only is the food great, but so is the ambience that it is served in. Making it one of the very few local style non vegetarian restaurants where you can savour your meal in peace and air conditioned comfort too.

If you've been putting off tasting some great naati oota because of concerns of ambience and crowd, Hotel Aditya is certainly the place to dive into local non veg cuisine. Hope you enjoy this watch. Take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

Title: Lost His Job And Created A Delicious Fruit & Sugarcane Drink! AMBAARI JUICE, Must Try In MYSURU

ambaari juice centre, mysuru, mysore, ambaari sugarcane and fruit juice, healthy juice, season fruits, small business, smart business, inspiring business, must try juice in mysuru, fresh fruit, mysore food tour, bengaluru food, must try street food, gourmet on the road, kripal amanna, food lovers tv, food lovers india, truth in food

Jayaramu was working in the food and beverage department of a hotel in Mysuru when he lost his job during the pandemic. Left with no recourse to earn a living, he began a sugarcane juice stall, but with a twist. Given his experience in mixing cocktails and mocktails in his previous job, he tried crushing seasonal, fresh fruits and herbs in the cane to create an interesting, healthy yet refreshingly delicious take on the humble sugarcane juice. I visited Ambaari Juice stall a few weeks ago and tasted a bevy of his offerings - malabar plum, mango, mixed fruit, pomegranate, muskmelon, et al - in sugar cane juice. Definitely something to try when you are in the palace city next.

Do support enterprising small entrepreneurs like Jayaramu who in the course of earning a livelihood are also bringing something deliciously different. Hope you enjoy this episode. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating.

Note: plain sugarcane juice with mint, lime, ginger is priced at Rs. 30, the fresh fruit and sugarcane juices are priced Rs. 60 upwards. My top picks were plain, jamun and mango amongst others.

A Gourmet On The Road episode that’s dearest to me is the one where I shared a meal with ‘namma priyaru’, Karnataka Ratna Puneeth Rajkumar. How one wishes things had turned out differently, but alas! He wore Karnataka on his sleeve, and part of his vision was to promote young talent in Kannada cinema, a role that is now being bravely carried forward by his wife, Ashwini Puneeth Rajkumar. And when I recently received a call from her inviting me to a conversation on Aachar & Co., a film made by a near-all-women-team led by Sindhu Sreenivasa Murthy, somewhere, I felt this would be an apt continuation of my conversation with Appu Sir. 
We met over a delicious South Canara lunch at New Modern Hotel, an appropriate venue given the film’s setting in Bengaluru of the sixties. We discussed the film, which promises to be a witty family entertainer, rich in its cinematic value, food, pickles, family, a lot more… and also basked in the warming memory of our dearest Appu, Puneeth Rajkumar.

I am looking forward to watching the film, you should too. Hope you enjoy this special conversation. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

My meal at Sarposh was an eye opener into the traditions of true Kashmiri cuisine that restaurateur Azmat Ali Mir seeks to showcase. In ingredients that she procures from the valley, to the brigade of wazas (cooks) from Srinagar who have made Bengaluru their home! To enjoy a meal here, park aside all notions you may have of the cuisine based on the odd so-called Kashmiri dish you may have tasted on a menu here and there. For the fare here is anything but that.
I opted for the maaz traem, a traditional celebratory meal and what followed was a procession of 12 dishes. From the initial methi maaz, soft and velvety tripe, served on a bed of rice, to a ghee-fried tabak maaz (ribs), dani phol (stewed lamb shanks) and a finely minced seekh kebab, to the hearty mains, rogan josh, the subtly flavoured sort you have never eaten before, rista (juicy meatballs), a comforting palak and razmah dal, creamy nadur (lotus stem) yakhni, marchewangan korma, the only searingly spicy dish of the lot, and gushtaba (meatballs stewed in yoghurt and dried mint), each preparation I found exquisite and subtly distinct in its flavour and taste. 
If you’re looking to try wazwan fare true to its roots, far removed from the ginger-garlic-chilli-cream infused heavy dishes that get passed off as Kashmiri elsewhere, definitely check out Sarposh restaurant and tea room in Bengaluru. 

Hope you enjoy part two of my Sarposh outing. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

When Azmat Ali Mir moved from Srinagar to Bengaluru after marriage, she yearned for authentic Kashmiri food, but “there was none to be found”, she says. A casual idea of staging a Kashmiri pop-up for a few friends ‘avalanched’ into a dinner for 1000 guests, compelling her to fly in wazas (Kashmiri cooks) to prepare the meal. Encouraged by the response, and her husband Azeem Syed, she embarked on setting up a space that sought to not only celebrate true Kashmiri cuisine, but also its culture and traditions. Thus was born Sarposh restaurant and tea room in Indiranagar, Bengaluru. Needless to say, the cooks (wazas) stayed back. I visited her for lunch one afternoon and was blown away by the sheer depth of cuisine and culture that this young entrepreneur seeks to showcase in her cozy dining space, which also offers a fascinating insight into the traditions of her land in its decor and artifacts. What was intended as a typical review lunch turned into an engrossing conversation with Azmat and her team, thereby resulting in this rare two-part Gourmet On The Road episode. Hope you enjoy part one.

Run by Ravi Shetty, an affable native of Kundapura who has been cooking since the age of 17, Karavali Lunch Home offers a delicious smorgasbord of coastal flavours from Dakshina Kannada featuring unique dishes like the country chicken uppu koli, that has earned it loyal patrons in its 15 years of existence. Sumathi was content being a homemaker, when her husband Charles, a software engineer, encouraged her to open a small eatery given her passion for cooking. She began one and ran it for a few months, when tragedy struck, and her husband was no more. Left with no recourse to fend for her three children and herself, Sumathi Charles ploughed her entire savings into setting up a modest eatery serving Tamil Nadu style vegetarian tiffin and meals. I visit The Madhras Kitchen early one evening and leave thoroughly impressed with most of the dishes I taste. I have no doubt that if this eatery remains true to its cuisine philosophy, it will certainly emerge as a must-eat-at place on Bengaluru’s culinary trail. Located in the heart of Bengaluru on Castle Street, this clean, hygienic eatery is certainly worthy of more than one visit. Do taste their delicious fare, and in doing so, support yet another deserving small business.

Title: Lucknowi Biryani & Kebabs At Bengaluru’s Smallest Biryani Shop Run By A Brave Lady! BIRYANI DELICACY
Description:
#biryanidelicacy #lucknowibiryani #bangalore 

biryani delicacy, biryani shop, lucknowi biryani, awadhi biryani, galouti kebab, seekh kebab, chapli kebab, shami kebab, goat meat biryani, non vegetarian, akshayanagar, south bengaluru, bangalore, inspiring story, lady entrepreneur, small business, bengaluru, bangalore, support small business, gourmet on the road, kripal amanna, food lovers tv, food lovers india, truth in food

The pandemic was a difficult time for Mahi and her husband Majeed. Their little son fell seriously ill and to nurse him back to health, this young couple had to borrow a fair bit of money. However soon thereafter Mahi lost her job. Left with no recourse, she turned to her love for cooking and opened a small shop near her home in Akshayanagar, a distant suburb in South Bengaluru, where she serves Lucknowi biryani and kebabs made to her grandmother’s recipe at home. There’s only a table to seat four and a few regulars in the area who order takeaways. But business has been tough, and the young couple have been having a tough time trying to make ends meet and repay their loans. I received an appeal from Mahi, and after making discreet enquiries, visited them for a meal. While the tiny size of the shop, it’s no more than a kiosk, with a table outside to seat four, did surprise me, what floored me completely was the taste of the fare that is served out of Biryani Delicacy. I will definitely return for the biryani and the kebabs. And needless to say, you should visit too. To savour a unique Lucknow style biryani that has been tweaked a bit to suit Bengaluru’s palate, and to also support a deserving small enterprise.

Hope you enjoy this episode. Tackle care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

It was inspiring to watch this one-man-army go about his work serving the community when I dropped in unannounced at his small store one evening.

Ranganatha was only in the fifth grade when he began assisting his brother-in-law at his chat cart after school. Soon, his interest in making chaat overtook any academic inclinations and after completing seventh grade, he gave up school. Soon, his family joined in too, his father giving up his profession as an automotive mechanic, his mother, and much later, his wife, assisting in preparing the masalas, chutneys, etc. at home. Over the last two decades or so, the cart has made way to a tiny shop and Sri Ranganatha Chats Corner has emerged as a favourite chaat spot in the neighbourhood, not only for their homestyle, simple preparations, but also the friendliness with which they interact with customers, many who have been tasting their fare over years.

When Narasimha Murthy’s livelihood as a masala salesman was disrupted owing to covid, he set up a tiny eatery serving seafood. Thrice, but each one failed. As a last resort, he approached Karnataka Fisheries Development Corporation, and they suggested he explore the model of a seafood mobile canteen that he set up a couple of years ago. Murthy still keeps his day job, selling spice mix packets throughout Bengaluru whilst his wife, Sunanda cleans the fish and prepares the masala throughout the day. And in the evening, they drive their seafood fry truck to Rajajinagar, where this hard working couple cook, and serve the neighbourhood. The fish that they serve is fresh, sourced from KFDC each day, and their fries, delicious as I discovered when I paid them an impromptu visit a few weeks ago.

I salute their work ethic, and hope many of you will be inspired to support this small enterprise. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

I first discovered The Vintage in Chikmagalur a couple of years ago when Sree and I, having emerged from the pandemic, were looking to take a break in a safe environment. This villa homestay set in an orchard came recommended. Since then, we have returned twice again to the endearing hospitality of its owner, Charles Baptist, who personally leaves no stone unturned to ensure his guests enjoy a refreshing Chikmaglur experience. On this visit to film a Gourmet On The Road series in coffee town, we camped here and left only after partaking a delicious Malenadu brunch, highlights of which included a tender jackfruit curry, tasty Malnad chicken, kadak fish fry and a surprising bottle gourd payasa. Definitely a spot to consider when you’re planning your next weekend break.

When Vani, a dietician, and her husband, Harsha, a IT professional, chanced upon an ice cream churner at an exhibition in Bengaluru, they saw in it an opportunity bring to fruition their plans of creating 100% natural ice creams, made only with fresh fruits and nuts, sans any artificial flavours, colours or additives. A trip to Italy to learn the art of making gelato, low fat ice creams, followed by months of honing recipes at home, led to the birth of their ice cream parlour, Churn in a leafy bylane of RMV 2nd Stage. The ice creams here are made fresh everyday using only seasonal ingredients. Although Churn has its share of loyal patrons in and around the neighbourhood, their ice creams are perhaps unknown to most of Bengaluru. I visit Churn to meet the friendly couple, learn the art of making gelato and taste every flavour that’s in the store.

Title: Ultimate Chikmagalur Coffee Tasting Experience! WORLD OF COFFEE | Brew Filter Kaapi To Civet Coffee!
Description:
#worldofcoffee #coffeeexperience #chikkamagaluru

world of coffee, chikmagalur, chikkamagaluru, coffee experience zone, coffee shop, filter coffee, artisan coffees, coffee tours, coffee roasting, coffee estate, 4d coffee, coffee tour, coffee tasting, civet coffee, karnataka food tour, gourmet on the road, kripal amanna, food lovers tv, food lovers india, truth in food


It is said that coffee first found its way into India through a Sufi saint, Baba Budan who, having smuggled seven coffee beans from Arabia in his beard, planted these in the hills around Chikkamagaluru in the late 17th century. Fitting therefore that this coffee town is also home to a unique coffee store that offers customers an immersive walk through the history, brewing and experiential tasting of coffee. I visited World Of Coffee on a recent trip and tasted a host of coffee - new age artisan varieties like pineapple fermented, honey infused, foraged civet coffees, and traditional filter coffee. When in Chikmagalur, you must explore coffee and this store is a great place to start.

Hope you enjoy this heady brew of an episode. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

Tasting:
Each of the coffees tasted left a mark. My favourites though, in descending order of preference - civet coffee, filter coffee, cold brew, fruit and honey infused coffee. And to taste coffee in a dessert form, the panna cotta is highly recommended.

The coffee panna cotta is priced at Rs. 170, and the artisan coffees around Rs. 170.

This isn’t a typical Gourmet On The Road episode. What appealed to me most about Director, Santhosh Ananddram’s upcoming film, Raghavendra Stores, set in a fictional eatery in Malenadu, wasn’t just its earthy, realistic portrayal of culinary traditions, but also its message. That tackled headlong the social challenges faced by those in the food trade, the protagonist in this film unable to find a bride due to his profession as a cook or ‘adige bhatta’. In this fun conversation, I catch up with Santhosh Ananddram, and actors, Navarasa Nayaka Jaggesh and Shwetha Srivatsav over a delicious tiffin thindi at a Malleswaram icon, Sri Raghavendra Stores.

Long before the current Mangalore highway was built, travellers from Bengaluru enroute to Hassan, Coastal Karnataka and beyond took the state highway that would meander through towns along the way. Kunigal was an important stop back then, and I remember pit stops for breakfast here in the nineties when quality eateries were hard to find, barring places like Hotel Parimala that first opened doors over four decades ago. Since then, a new highway has emerged that bypasses most such places. On a recent road trip to Chikmagalur though, I decided to stop at Hotel Parimala and rediscovered for myself a culinary institution that takes great pride in its age-old traditions that places great emphasis on serving quality fare to customers at prices that also seem to be an honest echo to the past.

I hope you enjoy this episode enough to revisit old eateries like Hotel Parimala that have been bypassed by modern highways. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

My last visit to Udupi Sri Krishna Bhavan in Balepete for an early tiffin coincided with the conclusion of their lunch service. I watched some of the lunch crowd relishing their thali meals, and made a note to return for the same someday. And so when on a recent visit to Chickpete, a lunch opportunity suddenly opened up, I lost no time in heading to this near-100-year-old eatery to taste their South Canara lunch. It’s a simple affair - couple of vegetable preparations, lentils, rasam, poori and rice, even a sweet - quite homely in its taste and sumptuous enough to fill one’s belly for a very affordable Rs. 110 only. And consumed in the restaurant’s heritage setting, it is also the sort of meal that transports one back to ‘good ole yesteryear’! Definitely plan a lunch here when in the area.

A farmer by profession, Mr. Rangaswamy opened a small thatched eatery on his property abutting the highway in Gowdagere, near Channarayapatna, 15 years ago to serve tea and snacks to travellers on the Bengaluru Hassan route. As the eatery became popular, his family also introduced their unique village style biryani along with other meaty preparations like the mutton sambar, thale kaalu and chops. He has since passed on, but his family continues his culinary traditions at SLR Biryani. Notwithstanding the recent construction of a flyover that bypasses this humble home eatery and has impacted business here, it still manages to hold on to its loyal patrons. The popularity of their wood-fire-cooked biryani is such that it runs out in a few hours each morning, after which it is the mutton dishes served with ragi mudde, plain rice or khushka that occupy centrestage. I dropped in impromptu for lunch one afternoon and was elated to find, through a tremendous stroke of luck, the biryani that was prepared for a special order.

When Mr. and Mrs. M. Mahadev Rao moved to Peenya on the outskirts of Bengaluru, this area was a remote industrial outpost where a few factories lay scattered amongst fields. With a family of seven children to feed and educate, this couple rented a shed to run a small tiffin shop that fueled workers and staff in the manufacturing units around. Over time, the popularity of their homely vegetarian tiffin fare and meals grew, also earning for the humble eatery the moniker ‘Bhatru Hotel’, as the couple were constantly cooking and feeding customers. 34 years on Gurukrupa Bhats Canteen stands strong as a cornerstone in this now bustling suburb, a daily ritual for many of its patrons, for whom a day is incomplete without coffee, tiffin or a meal here. Now in his nineties, Mr Rao has left the running of the eatery to his sons who are involved in every aspect of the operation - from the cooking to the serving and speaking a kind word or two with their customers, many who share decades-old relationships with the place. I dropped in for a quick tiffin, but felt compelled to linger on and savour many of the dishes on offer.

Prabhakar Hegde moved from his native Sirsi in Uttara Kannada to Bengaluru in the nineties to earn a livelihood. He found employment at the iconic Veena Stores in Malleshwaram, and after a few years of working there decided that cooking and serving tiffin was his calling. He went on to open a tiny store in Vidyaranyapura, a far flung locality in North Bengaluru, 23 years ago, a place so remote that back then only a handful of buses would ply there each day. However today, the area has grown into a bustling suburb, and so has Hegde’s Fast Food which is now a cornerstone of the neighbourhood for its idli, vade and a couple of other thindi items. Having received a bunch of recommendations in support of this shop, I visited Hegde impromptu for a chat one evening with him, and also with the locals who have monikered this place as the Veena Stores of Vidyaranyapura.

Please do your best to support tiny small businesses like these that need all the help that they can get for the delicious work they do. Hope you enjoy this one; take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

When Mr Mohan Rao couldn’t find a job in Bengaluru after completing his engineering degree, he hired a cook from Nellore and began a restaurant in 1981. Over time Hotel Navayuga became popular amongst its patrons for the biryanis, kebabs and fries. Its patrons include not just with the common man and hordes of travelers given its location in Gandhinagar, but its fare has also endeared itself to luminaries of Karnataka, most noteworthy being the Dr Rajkumar parivar. 

I was told about this place by Karnataka Ratna, Dr. Puneeth Rajkumar, Appu Sir, and more recently shared a meal with his nephew, Vinay Rajkumar and Anushree when I tasted some of Dr Puneeth Rajkumar’s most favourite dishes here. In this Gourmet On The Road episode, I return to taste some of the delicacies that have transformed Hotel Navayuga from an eatery that was born out of the need for a livelihood to a Bengaluru culinary icon.

I hope you enjoy this very special episode, also catch part one where I visit the kitchens of Navayuga to explore what makes their iconic biryani special, in addition to watching the making of the other favourites here like the chicken kebab, fish fry and more.

I was first introduced to Hotel Navayuga during the course of my most memorable meal, with Karnataka Ratna, Dr Puneeth Rajkumar, Appu Sir. We were relishing a traditional jolada rotti oota, but somewhere our conversation veered to tasting a biryani during our next meal. Alas, that wasn’t meant to be, but deep down I feel that if it would have been at Hotel Navayuga, a 40-year-old eatery that Appu Sir spoke about quite fondly. I did make a visit to the eatery later, to record a tribute episode to commemorate his last film over a meal with his nephew, Vinay Rajkumar and Anchor Anushree. It was also during the course of this meal that I decided I must return to film a full-fledged Gourmet On Episode.

I hope you enjoy part one of this episode, where I visit the kitchens of Navayuga to explore what makes their iconic biryani special, in addition to watching the making of their other favourites like the chicken kebab, fish fry and more.

Title: Softest, Fluffiest SRI LAKSHMI BHAVAN TIFFIN ROOM Khaali Dosae Making & Tasting! 68 Year Recipe!

Over the last couple of years, I have received innumerable requests from our viewers to taste the khaali dosae at Chitradurga’s popular Sri Lakshmi Bhavan Tiffin Room. And so, on a recent drive through the area, I stopped at this 68-year old institution where I enjoyed my short conversation with the humble second-generation proprietor, Mr Mahabala, and also caught the making of what is perhaps one of the fluffiest khaali dosae that I’ve eaten. Khaali means ‘empty’ in kannada, there is no oil deployed in the dosae’s cooking, but ironically the tradition here is to serve it with some tuppa (ghee), and palya (potato stuffing) to make for an enjoyable, filling thindi. And they say, you shouldn't leave here without tasting their soft gulab jamun, which is what i savoured too in addition to a lovely idli sambar.

Hope you enjoy this tiffin watch, definitely pencil the place into your travel plans when in and around Chitradurga. Happy eating.

Not enjoying his vocation as a public works contractor, Satyanarayana Reddy converted a part of his home into a rustic eatery in Chitradurga, seeking to serve non vegetarian delicacies made to his wife’s recipes. The eatery had no signboard for many years, but gained immense popularity amongst locals for its unique mutton and chicken dishes. However, it is still largely undiscovered to most travellers which is ironic given its location just off the highway. The atmosphere of this 31-year-old eatery is rather rudimentary, but the fare served here is the sort that will have you reminiscing its robust flavours well into your journey.

Hope you enjoy this delicious find; take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

The pandemic was tough on the hospitality industry and the people who worked in it, many who found themselves out of employment. My good friend, Chef Amit Wadhawan however saw in this adversity an opportunity to convert an interest, that of bottling traditional and modern expressions of flavours in a hand crafted range of jams, chutneys, pickles and preserves, into a small business. When Mr. Chandrappa moved to Mathikere, then a remote corner of Bengaluru nearly half a century ago, he set up a vegetarian eatery to cater to the local populace. This met with limited success, however things clicked when he added in the non vegetarian dishes that he and his wife would cook at home. Eventually, his sons joined in to support this family enterprise that in a span of 46 years has come to be the de facto eatery for naati (local style) non-vegetarian oota in the area. However, there are still many outside the immediate area who are yet to discover the homely taste of the fare here. I was one of them, until I paid a surprise visit one afternoon. In our last Old Delhi outing this season, we stumbled upon the best biryani that we tasted in the walled city. Getting to Taufiq Dilpasand Biryani Point requires some effort given its location in the inner recesses of Galli Haveli Azam Khan, a bit of a walk from Jama Masjid. The shop itself is a little more than a window, but the biryani that emerges from the copper pots here has endeared itself to biryani lovers in the know for a quarter of a century now. They call Haji Mohd Hussain’s fried chicken the KFC of Old Delhi, a moniker well earned by the hard working septuagenarian for his single minded focus to making his version of a double fried, crisp and juicy, spicy chicken. Speaking of one-dish eateries, further down the road, one also finds Shabrati Nahari Shop that has been making a slow-braised eight-hour nahari twice a day each day since 1954. And in between the fried chicken and nahari, I also gulped down a few glasses of mohabbat ka sharbat, a delightful refreshing concoction that I instantly fell in love with.

Park aside whatever notions you may have of the butter chicken, for Purani Dilli’s most famous Aslam Butter Chicken is anything but that. Made to a seemingly simple recipe with secret masalas, this roasted and charcoal grilled chicken bathed in copious amounts of molten butter has built for this Jama Masjid eatery an iconic status over a span of 25 years. We catch the making of this indulgent chicken tikka, but before that take respite in the reinvigorating offerings of a tea stall that goes back seven or eight decades.

What began as Mrs. Geetha Shivakumar’s home cooking initiative 23 years ago to bridge with farmers and bring a seasonal produce to Bengaluru’s consumers in a myriad range of savoury and sweet delicacies is now a culinary institution called the Avarebele Mela. Farmers congregate from Magadi, Karnataka bringing the pick of their crops and the cooks from Shree Vasavi Condiments cook up a host of preparations, each one featuring the avarebele. I was recently invited to open this festival with a host of other dignitaries including Mrs. Sudha Murthy, Sihi Kahi Chandru Sir and others. Hope you enjoy this vlog account of my experience there. The mela runs through 9th January 2023 at National College Grounds, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru.

This is followed by a piquant introduction to Old Delhi’s famous Lotan Chole Kulche. Authentic Maharashtrian Food at Suryawanshi Restaurant, Bengaluru, Bangalore, Kolhapuri Mutton, Mutton Thali, Pune Vegetarian Food, Pandra Rasa, Tamba Rasa, Misal pav, Vada Pav, Sabudana Vada, Whitefield, Bangalore, Prawn Fry, Pomfret Fry, Malvan Fish Curry, eating out in bengaluru, bangalore,  food trail, must try restaurant 

When Kailash Suryawanshi moved from Kolhapur to Bengaluru with his family nearly a decade ago, the one cuisine he couldn’t get any of was his own. Such was his yearning for food from his land, that this entrepreneur decided to take upon himself the onerous task of introducing Bengaluru to authentic Marathi fare. After months of travel through the hinterlands of Maharashtra, gleaning recipes and cooks, Suryawanshi was born, a restaurant where conversations in Marathi waft through the dining room, as if in endorsement of the food served here.

Zain’s Hotel Kozhikode stands testament to Mrs Zainabi Noor’s firm resolve to showcase the Mappila cuisine of her family. Kozhikode’s first lady restaurateur, she began her culinary enterprise 32 years ago as a small tea stall dispensing evening snacks. Spurred by the love she received from her customers, Zain’s today stands tall in Calicut as the address for homestyle Malabar cuisine.

In this throwback episode, I visit  this cosy restaurant set in a home and meets the mother-daughter duo of Zainabi Noor and Shireen Mustafa who oversee every detail of the operation. Title: Tasting The Mumbai PAV BHAJI At SHIV SAGAR Bengaluru! Throwback
Description:
#shivsagar #pavbhaji #bangalore

shiv sagar, mumbai pav bhaji, bengaluru, pav bhaji making, vegetarian restaurant, eating out in bangalore, bengaluru food trail, vegetarian, popular restaurant

A dish that finds its origins in leftover vegetables tossed by street vendors into an inexpensive but tasty mash and served with local bakery bread as cheap sustenance to Bombay’s mill workers at the turn of the last century, the pav bhaji evolved to its buttery, cheesy, somewhat indulgent avatar courtesy savvy restaurateurs in the seventies and eighties. My memories of a Mumbai pav bhaji go back to Shiv Sagar, Juhu and Vile Parle, a hop and a skip away from college, where I relished many a plate. So when a craving for the Mumbai style pav bhaji hit me one cold evening, I found my way to the Bengaluru outpost of Shiv Sagar, where brothers Ram and Shyam, second generation restaurateurs trained in the Mumbai restaurant, dish up this quintessential Mumbai fast food that is quite close to the real deal. 

Hope you enjoy this throwback episode. Take care, stay safe and strong. Happy eating!

47 years ago, Janab Ahmed Basha Sahib set up a modest eatery in Vaniyambadi, a town in Tirupattur district of Tamil Nadu, famous for its leather industry. The fare at Ahmedia Hotel was mostly Mughlai,  inspired by the culinary traditions of erstwhile North Arcot principality. Over decades the kitchens here have perfected time-honored recipes, amongst them a wood-fire-cooked biryani that, unusual for Tamil Nadu, favours the basmati over seeraga samba rice. I discovered Ahmedia three years ago on a #gourmetontheroad tour through the region when I met the founder and his enterprising sons. Janab Ahmed Basha has passed on since, but his sons seem determined to build on their father’s legacy. And have now opened a massive 25,000 sq. ft., 250-seat Ahmedia branch on the Bengaluru Chennai highway with the conveniences required to cater to travellers. I visited them on a recent trip to Chennai, where I tasted most of my favourite dishes here, including the biryani that has put Vaniyambadi on the culinary map.

I recently received an invitation that compelled me to drive 350 kilometres to visit the Adyar Ananda Bhavan Sweets & Snacks Factory in Ambattur, Chennai. A2B, as the group is popularly known, is now perhaps South India’s most recognised restaurant, sweets and snacks brand, with over 150 outlets across Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and overseas, however its origins are rather humble and trace an agricultural family’s inspiring 60-year journey through Rajapalyam, Bengaluru, Chennai and beyond. As I learnt from the second and third generation of the Adyar Ananda Bhavan family when I visited their facility that can produce over 40,000 kilos of savouries and 10,000 kilos of sweets evry single day! 

What is heartening though is the family’s commitment to sourcing quality ingredients, even making their own ghee to ensure 100% purity, and fostering an environment where the skill and craft involved in making artisanal handmade sweets is also encouraged alongside automated production lines to meet the burgeoning demand for their sweets and savouries. I hope you enjoy the first part of this very special episode this Deepavali weekend.

Title: Nearly 100 Years, UDUPI SRI KRISHNA BHAVAN Is Bengaluru’s Best Kept Secret! Sagu Dosae, Best Sambar
Description:
#udupisrikrishnabhavan #balepete #bangalore

pure vegetarian restaurant, oldest restaurant, bengaluru, south canara cuisine, sambar, rava idli, vada, vade, sagu dosae, masala dosa, south indian tiffin, dumrot, badam halwa, gulab jamun, filter coffee, popular bengaluru restaurants, balepet, chickpet, must try restaurant, historical restaurant, heritage eatery, bangalore food tour, eating out in bengaluru, vegetarian, eateries in bangalore, support local

Although established at its present location in 1926, its culinary provenance dates back to the early 1900s. One of Bengaluru’s oldest eateries, Udupi Sri Krishna Bhavan has not received the kind of recognition other eateries of its ilk have perhaps due to its location amidst the hustle and bustle of Balepete. The food here is prepared the old-fashioned way, not the sort that swims in rivers of ghee or is buried under mounds of butter, khoa, or other such dairy decadence. Which is good, especially if you want to indulge, sans any guilt, in its tasty South Canara fare, like many of its regular patrons, some who have been visiting for 50 years! I soak in some charming old-world vibe as I make a tasty meal of some of their must-try dishes including a scrumptious, very popular sagu dosae and perhaps the most impressionable sambar you will find in this city. A sambar that we also watched the making of.

I chanced upon this small shop tucked in a by-lane of Indiranagar, serving the hitherto unseen (in Bengaluru) flavours of Benares, Uttar Pradesh. In this quick evening stop, I made quick work of some of the must-try dishes on their menu, scrumptious samosas, a weighty, comforting dal and methi (fenugreek) poori, aloo mangodi, fresh ghee jalebis, an utterly 'khasta' kachori and more. If you love the vegetarian flavours of the North, especially UP, Panditji Ras Bana Rahe is a must-visit. Hope you enjoy this episode. Take care; stay safe and strong. Happy eating!
