Takeaway Meal, Lockdown, Royanna Military Canteen, Karnataka Meal, Military Style Food, Chicken Kebab, Chicken Liver Fry, Mutton Fry, Curry Leaf Chicken, Chicken Pepper Fry, Chicken Pulav, Mutton Pulav, Pulav, Pulao, Non Veg Meals, Bangalore, Bengaluru

Just over a year old, Royanna Military Canteen seeks inspiration from the decades-old traditions of military hotels in the South, in its meaty menu that serves up naati (local) dishes. But in a format that the restaurant says is “sanitised and one that makes military-style fare convenient to families eating out.” The important question, though, does the food deliver the tasty punch that one has come to expect of military hotels that have stood the test of time? Well, I visit the restaurant and grab a takeaway of most of their dishes to find my answer. Hope you enjoy this episode. Take care and stay safe.

Chicken Kebab
Not as crispy as a kebab would be when tasted at the restaurant, but the chicken is moist, juicy and flavourful. The chicken is cooked perfectly and peels off the bone. 
Rs. 150 (usd 2) 
8/10

Curry Leaf Chicken
The rich masala exudes the toasty herbaceousness of curry leaf, however its flavours have not penetrated the meat as one would have desired. 
Rs. 200 (usd 2.6) 
6.5/10

Chicken Pepper Fry
The chicken is moist and napped in a flavourful masala rich in onions, tomatoes, coriander and curry leaf. The onions have been roasted to a deep brown. Definitely a dish to savour at Royanna.
Rs. 150 (usd 2) 
8.5/10

Mutton Fry
The meat has a bit of a bite, after all one is eating local, military-style dishes. The buttery, unctuous flavour of the fat that straddles the meat makes for a lush mouthfeel. The spicing is gentle and warming as opposed to the fiery chilli hit one sometimes encounters when dining local style. 
Rs. 280 (usd 3.7) 
8.5/10

Chicken Liver Fry
The chicken is perfectly cooked to a creamy texture, its deep flavours complemented by the pepper laced green masala. 
Rs. 150 (usd 2) 
9/10

Palav
Cooked with chicken, but served minus the meat, the khaali palav is a spicy, military hotel tradition. The palav here though is mild on the palate, if you like to pick up the flavours, combine it with the sherva, the spicy broth that’s served with the palav.
Rs. 120 (usd 1.6) 
7/10

Chicken Palav
If you are looking for a bold, military-style pulav, this is not it. But if you’re looking for something mellow in flavour, this would be a good pulav to taste. The chicken benefits when tasted with the rice, the latter lending its spice notes. The pulav comes alive when combined with the spicy sherva.
Rs. 160 (usd 2.1)
8/10

Mutton Palav
The palav is deeper in its flavours helped by the character of the red meat and also the fat that’s clinging on to it. One needs to work though, to pry some meat from the bone, and also to chew on it. One of those rare occasions when I preferred the chicken palav to mutton. 
Rs. 180 (usd 2.4)
7/10

Title: A Taste of Dindigul in Bangalore | DINDIGUL THALAPPAKATTI BIRYANI Making | Mutton, Chicken & More...
Description:
#DindigulThalappakatti #Biryani #Bengaluru 

Takeaway Meal, Lockdown, Dindigul Thalappakatti Restaurant, Dindigul Thalappakatti Biryani, Mutton, Chicken, Vegetable, Biryani, Mutton Chukka, Mutton Kuchi, Chicken Kodaikanal, Chicken Peri Peri, Kola Urundai,  Kuzhambu, Biryani, Bangalore, Bengaluru

In the year 1957, Nagasamy Naidu set out to sell a biryani made to his wife’s unique recipe in the then sleepy town of Dindigul in Tamil Nadu. Seated at the counter, always with a turban tied on his head, led to the eatery being popularly referred to as the Thalappakatti (thalappa - turban; katti - tied) biryani shop as opposed to its original name, Anandha Vilas, and thus was born an establishment that today owns (yes owns, not franchises) nearly 70 outposts of Dindigul Thalappakatti across the world. I visit the kitchen here to watch the cooking of their famed biryani made with small-grained seeraga samba rice, and also visit one of their eight restaurants in Bengaluru to get a takeaway bundle of their signature dishes. Hope you enjoy this episode. Happy eating and stay safe! 

Kola Urundai
Spiced roundels of mutton mince, it’s unassuming form doesn't reveal the flavourful rush of spices it delivers on the palate. 
Rs. 137 (usd 1.8) 
7.5/10

Mutton Chukka
Tiny morsels of meat, soft and yielding, with a springy bite. You can taste the grainy crunch of the coconut and the pepper hit, the perfect snack to accompany an evening tipple.
Rs. 253 (usd 3.1) 
9/10

Peri Peri Chicken Chops
The smokey, spiciness of the peri peri masala certainly perks things up on the palate alongside a zing of acidity, perhaps from some vinegar. The mayo helps assuage the spicy assault of the peri peri chicken. 
Rs. 300 (usd 4) 
8/10

Kuchi Mutton
Tender goat ribs, braised in a deep-roasted masala. The meat is soft and tender, encased in a thin veil of fat which adds to the flavour. The parotta makes for a handy bread to mop up the masala, this is a dish that epitomises the way in which DT cooks its mutton! A must-have!
Rs. 288 (usd 3.8) 
9/10

Kodaikanal Chicken Kozhambu
The chicken is moist and calming in its flavours, the spicing is mellow and cradled in creamy coconut milk. You bite into flecks of coconut as you savour this kozhambu.
Rs. 265 (usd 3.5) 
8/10

Vegetable Biryani
The seeraga samba rice heroes the Dindigul biryani powder that makes for the masala, the vegetables, beans, carrots and cauliflower, have been roasted in the masala thus imbuing in them the flavour of the biryani.
Rs. 210 (usd 2.8) 
7.5/10

Chicken Biryani
The rice is flavoursome and the chicken definitely benefits when savoured in its company. Taste it with the biryani gravy and its endearing tomato-acidity if you like to moisten things up on the palate. The boiled egg helps stretch the protein component on the plate.
Rs. 240 (usd 3.2) 
8/10

Thalappakatti Boneless Mutton Biryani
This is the biryani that’s synonymous with Dindigul Thalappakatti, and therefore it is no surprise that they do it extremely well. The seeraga samba has not just trapped the flavour of the spices, but also the smoky aromas of the meat. The meat is soft, tender and moist. This is the sort of deep-flavoured, satisfying biryani that needs no accompaniment, either the gravy or the raitha. A must-order if you’re a biryani buff.
Rs. 299 (usd 4) 
10/10

Title: Make This AUTHENTIC MANGALOREAN FISH CURRY | Spicy Surmai, Pomfret, Rawas, Kane, Prawns Curry RECIPE
Description:
#Mangalorean #FishCurry #Recipe

Easy Fish Curry, Mangalorean Fish Curry, Fish Curry Rice, Indian Fish Curry, Seer Fish Curry, Pomfret Curry, Prawn Curry, Mangalore, Seafood, Kudla, Easy Recipe

The Mangalorean fish curry is the perfect balance of spice, heat and sour. In this recipe episode, we cook up a seer fish curry from scratch, including a vivacious masala that lends itself well to any mild-flavoured fish like pomfret, kingfish, ladyfish, or even prawns. Its beautiful bright reddish-orange hue comes from the combination of Kashmiri & Guntur chillies I prefer to use in this traditional preparation from namma Kudla. Traditionally, the curry is prepared atleast a couple of hours ahead of meal time, thereby allowing the fish to soak up the flavoursome masala. Served with steaming hot rice, this is a curry that pleases the soul! Enjoy!

Link to Rooster Masala episode https://youtu.be/3RXHj32sToQ

Ingredients to make Mangalorean Fish Curry
Serves 3 to 4

500 gm fish, marinated in ½ tsp each of turmeric and salt.

15 red chillies (I use a combination of Kashmiri & Guntur in the ratio 9:6)
1 tbsp coriander seeds
1 tsp cumin seeds
10 to 12 peppercorns 
¼ tsp mustard seeds
12 to 15 fenugreek seeds I USED 15
A pinch of carom seeds (ajwain)
½ tsp turmeric powder
1 large onion, roughly chopped 
10 cloves of garlic
½ inch ginger, roughl chopped
Tamarind, lime sized ball 
5 tbsp grated coconut
400 ml water 
Salt to taste

For the seasoning
½ medium sized onion
20 to 25 curry leaves
Coconut oil

Since then, this wholesome Madhwa Brahmin dessert, made of Bengal Gram, jaggery and nuts mostly, continues to be offered as prasadam and is relished especially during festivals. The Mangalorean Prawn Pulao is unlike any seafood pulao. At its heart is an aromatic coriander-mint masala that complements the sweetness of fresh shrimps, and lends this rice dish an appealing greenish hue and a unique fulsome flavour. One of my favourite food memories growing up, this was a pulao cooked by my Mom on special occasions like birthdays,  with plenty of medium-sized prawns, thereby ensuring a taste of the crustacean in every mouthful. And she would also find in this pulao the perfect medium to include finely chopped carrots and beans to feed veggies to her fussy kids. ;-) This pulao recipe is truly special to me, I hope you find it special enough to cook too. Take care and stay safe. Enjoy! 

Mangalorean Prawn Pulao
Serves 4

Ingredients:

500 gm medium-sized prawns (roughly around 40 to 50 prawns) 
2 large onions, finely chopped
2 carrots, finely chopped
10 beans, finely chopped
1 cup peas
8 cloves
5 to 6 green cardamoms
1 inch cinnamon
Oil/ ghee to cook
Salt to taste

For the masala
1 big bunch of coriander and stalk,
1 cup of mint leaves 
Ensure coriander and mint are in a 60:40 ratio.
8 to 9 green chillies
1 inch of ginger, peeled and sliced
10 to 12 pods of garlic
1 tsp of turmeric powder
1 tsp salt

Title: Make The Parsi Delicacy, AKURI | Best ANDA SUBZI | Spiced SCRAMBLED EGGS | ORIGINAL Mumbai Recipe
Description:
#Eggs #ScrambledEggs #EasyRecipe  

Akuri, Parsi Scrambled Eggs, Spicy Scrambled Eggs, Desi Eggs, Parsi Dish, Parsi Cuisine, Irani Restaurant Breakfast, Breakfast. Eggs, Eggs Recipe, Easy Recipe, Parsi Sambar Masala, Authentic Recipe, Mumbai, Parsi Dish, Bombay

In this lockdown recipe episode, we celebrate the humble ‘anda’ in the making of an Akuri, the spicy Parsi version of scrambled eggs. Some confuse this dish with the Mumbai street food staple, ‘anda bhurji’, but the Parsi Akuri is a different dish altogether, from its nuanced spice notes, its depth of flavour, and its texture, comparable to a savoury custard. Growing up in Mumbai, this was a dish I would savour in Irani restaurants with some kadak brun pav, or in Parsi homes. I dig deep into my food memories to cook this comforting ‘eggy’ dish, perfect for breakfast or a lazy lunch. Enjoy, stay safe and happy cooking.

Ingredients

Serves 2

3 eggs
1 tbsp ghee, you could use refined oil as well.
Knob of cold butter butter for finishing
2 medium sized onions, chopped finely (roughly ½ onion per egg) 
2 medium sized tomatoes, chopped finely (roughly ½ tomato per egg)
4 to 6 garlic cloves, finely chopped
2 to 3 green chillies, finely chopped
¾ 1 tsp red chilli powder
½ tsp turmeric powder
1 tsp Parsi sambar masala (optional) The Parsi sambar masala is that special touch that adds depth of flavour to the dish. It is a concoction of chilli powder, turmeric, asafoetida, fenugreek seeds, mustard seeds, peppercorn, star anise, cloves and cinnamon, ground together, and then combined with heated sesame oil). If you don’t have this, you can use any garam masala to add flavour depth.
2 to 3 tbsp coriander, chopped
Salt to taste

#gourmetontheroad #gotrraw #athome #foodloverstv 

Subz-e-Biryani
The vegetables consisted of peas, carrots, potatoes and cauliflowers, mushy for the most part, and slathered in a rich masala. The rice though was cooked perfectly, each grain blossomed to its fullest. Rs. 286 (usd 3.7) 
6/10

Lazeez Bhuna Murg Biryani
With tonnes of masala, this isn't a biryani that will endear itself if you’re looking for something delicate. The rice is cooked well, garnished with slivers of almonds, but suspiciously tastes just like the rice in the vegetable biryani. The chicken is firm, not juicy and succulent.
Rs. 314 (usd 4.1)
5/10

Dum Gosht Biryani
With three or five juicy pieces of meat slathered in masala, this is a biryani that could feed two. The meat is soft and moist, cooked perfectly. Taste with plenty of mint raita to wash down the warmth of the spices in the masala. 
Rs. 448 (usd 5.9)
7/10

Title: Best TANDOORI CRAB, BOMBIL (BOMBAY DUCK) FRY, FISH CURRY & More At GAJALEE Seafood Restaurant MUMBAI
Description:
#BestSeafood #Mumbai #GourmetOnTheRoad

Gajalee, Mumbai’s Favourite, Most Popular Seafood Restaurant, Best Bombay Duck Mumbai, Best Seafood Mumbai, Most Popular Seafood Mumbai, Best Tandoori Crab Mumbai, Best Seafood Restaurant In Mumbai Stuffed Bombil Fry, Bombil Fry, Bombay Duck Fry, Randoori Crab, Indian Salmon Rawas Curry, Fresh Seafood, Bombay, Seafood, Lunch, Dinner

Gajalee is perhaps Mumbai’s most popular seafood destination. When here, its fresh seafood offerings, from the signature stuffed bombil fry, prawns koliwada, plain bombil fry, rawas curry to the splurge worthy tandoori crab are a ritual for many of its regulars. I make the most of a quick visit to Mumbai to catch an indulgent seafood feast here and film this GOTR Raw episode. Enjoy!

PRAWNS KOLIWADA
These sea prawns are fresh, well seasoned and encrusted in a crunch rice flour batter. Smother it with the ginger garlic chutney if you like it spicy.
Rs. 425 (USD 5.6)
8.5/10

STUFFED BOMBIL FRY
If you were to try only one dish at Gajalee, this would be it. The delicate, watery bombay duck is rolled around a spicy shrimp mixture, dipped in a batter and fried. The fish retains its moistness despite being fried and the shrimp adds flavour.
Rs. 400 (USD 5.3)
10/10

Bombil Fry
The Bombay Duck is simply seasoned, dredged through a rice batter and fried. Yet another dish to try here. You can quite literally taste the ocean in this preparation.
Rs. 325 (USD 4.3)
9/10

TANDOORI CRAB
It’s a bit of a splurge, but you definitely get the ‘meatiest’ bang for your buck! The crab was fresh and plump in its meat. I was worried that the tandoori masala would overpower the flavour of the crab, but that wasn’t the case. You could taste the sweetness in the flesh, and the gentle edge of the tandoori marinade.  
Rs. 2957 (USD 39)for a one kilo crab
10/10

Rawas Curry
A creamy Malwan style curry, flavoured with the sour twang of kokum. The rawas or Indian salmon was soft and had absorbed the flavour of the curry. Best eaten with the ghavne, lacy pancakes made with a runny rice batter. 
Rs. 425 (USD 5.7)
8/10

Title: Cilantro Veggies, Mexican Rice, Citrus Salsa, Cilantro Fish | Tasty & Easy Recipe To Cook At Home
Description:
Easy Vegetarian Recipe, Easy Fish Recipe, Cook restaurant Style Food At Home, Mexican Recipe, Cilantro Vegetables, Cilantro Fish, Salsa, Mexican Rice

Cilantro Fish/ Cilantro Vegetables 
With Citrus Salsa and Corn On The Cob
Serves 2
Recipe by Chef Vikas Seth, Sanchez, Bengaluru

For the Cilantro Marinade
Ingredients:       
Cilantro, chopped   100g
Green Chilli, chopped   3 pcs
Garlic, cloves   1tbsp
Onion     quarter of an onion
Jalapeno     1 tsp 
Oil      1 tbsp
Lemon juice    1 tbsp
Salt      to taste
Water     1 tbsp or as required
Method:
1. Prepare the marination by blending all the ingredients together in a food processor or a mixer.

For the Cilantro Fish
Ingredients:       
Boneless Fish, cut into cubes   300g
Cilantro marinade    4 tbsp
Mustard                     1 tbsp
Salt                      to taste
Black Pepper crushed    a pinch
Lemon juice             1 tbsp
Oil                      1 tbsp
Orange zest              ½ tsp
Method:
1. Marinate the fish with the above ingredients and leave aside for 20minutes.
2. Grill it on both sides to cook it perfectly, and it will take 5 to 7 minutes, depending upon the thickness of the fish filet.
3. Serve it on the plate as done.

For the Cilantro Vegetables
Ingredients:       
Broccoli, thick slices     50g
Cauliflower, thick slices    50g 
Green Beans, batons, blanched   20g
Carrot, thick slices, blanched   20g
Red/Yellow/Green Peppers, 
thick batons                                                 60g
Cilantro marinade     4 tbsp
Mustard                      1 tbsp
Salt                       to taste
Black Pepper crushed     a pinch
Lemon juice              1 tbsp
Oil                       1 tbsp
Orange zest              ½ tsp
Method:
1. Marinate the vegetable with all the above ingredients and leave aside for 20minutes.
2. Grill on a medium high heat, flip it once or twice to cook it perfectly on both sides.
3. Serve it on the plate as done

For the Fresh Tomato Garlic Paste
Ingredients:     
Tomato Red                                                             1 Whole
Garlic Cloves                                                            5 cloves
Onion                                                                         Half onion
Method:
1. Cut tomato into quarters, add garlic cloves & onion in a Mixer. Blend into a smooth paste.

For the Mexican Rice
Ingredients:  
Long Grain Rice/basmati rice   100g
Refined oil                      20g
Carrot, small cube            20g
Green peas                      20g
Tomato puree            1 tbsp
Fresh Tomato garlic paste**    2 tbsp
Vegetable stock                   180ml
Coriander Stem                    15g
Salt                              to taste
Lemon Juice                    1 tbsp
Method:
1. Heat oil in a saucepan over medium heat; add in rice and sauté till all the grains are lightly golden brown in color.
2. Add in the carrot cubes, tomato puree, fresh tomato garlic paste stirring constantly, now add in the vegetable stock, salt, green peas and bring to a boil. Add in the coriander stems at this time. 
3. Reduce heat to low, cover and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes until done. 
4. Remove the cover and the coriander stems out from the cooked rice. 
5. Squeeze lemon juice on top and fluff the rice with a fork.

 
Mexican Corn on the Cob
Ingredients:
Fresh Corn ears    1pcs
Lemon Juice     1 tbsp
Butter      10g
Salt              to taste
Black Pepper, crushed  a pinch
Method:
1. Remove the husk and strings from the corn. Cut into three or four pics.
Boil it in salted water for half an hour.
2. Grill it with a little butter, salt, crushed black pepper and lemon juice.

Citrus Salsa
Ingredients:
Grapefruit, cubes    4 tbsp
Orange , cubes    4 tbsp
Onion Chopped    1 tbsp
Green Chili, chopped    1 tsp
Cilantro             1 tsp
Salt               to taste 
Lemon juice     1 tbsp
Olive oil              1 tbsp
Green Pumpkin seeds   1 tsp
White Pumpkin seeds   1 tsp
Method:
1. Cut grapefruit and orange segments into medium sized cubes.
2. Add chopped onion, cilantro, green chilli, salt, lemon juice and olive oil and mix lightly
4. Serve chilled with a sprinkle of green and white pumpkin seeds.

Title: HYGIENIC, TASTY & AFFORDABLE! Tiffin At TAAZA THINDI | Most Popular SOUTH INDIAN SNACK Destination
Description:
#VegetarianBreakfast #Bangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad

Taaza Thindi, must-visit for its tasty south indian tiffin, hygienically prepared and affordable! Vegetarian, Masala Dosa, Plain Dose, Masala Dose, Plain Dose, Idli, Vada, Khara Baath, Kesari Baath, Chowchow Baath, Coffee, Filter Coffee, Bengaluru, Bangalore, Jayanagar, Breakfast in Bngalore

Tasty food made using quality ingredients in a kitchen that rivals the best in terms of its hygiene standards and at prices that make it affordable for everyone, these are three tenets religiously adhered to by Taaza Thindi, that have made it one of Bengaluru’s most popular South Indian tiffin destinations in a short span of only six years in a culinary landscape that’s dominated by institutions that have been around for decades. 

Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna savours a delicious tiffin comprising of all five dishes on the menu here, but not before a detailed walk-through of this eatery that has no door separating the restaurant from the kitchen in its belief that customers should be able to see how their food is prepared. Enjoy!

Idli Vada
The idli is grainy and porous in texture allowing for the ‘runny’ chutney to seep through and imbue it with its spicy fervour. The vada exudes a near ‘biscuity’ crunch and is simple and clean in its flavours. 
Rs. 10 (usd) per idli/ vada
8.5/10

Chowchow baath
Made with bansi wheat rava, the khara baath is porridge-like in its consistency. On the palate, it exudes savoury, spicy flavours tinged with the tartness of tomato. The kesari bath is rich, in ghee, toasted cashew, raisins, and also incorporates the fruit of the season, and the spicy tinge of cloves.
Rs. 25 (usd)
8.5/10

 
Plain Dose
The dose here is not kadak (extremely crisp) but exudes a whisper of a crunch and is soft inside. Although the ghee and oil is quite evident on the fingers, its compact size renders it manageable. The dose seeks the company of the coconut chutney.
Rs. 20 (usd) 
8/10

Masala Dose 
Its golden brown crust glistens with the ghee that’s ladled over, the kempu chutney reveals itself from within. Crunch (well, almost) into this dose to taste the savoury onion flavour in the creamy potato palya, the warm tinge of of the kempu chutney. 
Rs. 25
9/10

Coffee
The perfect close to a tiffin here!
Rs. 10
8/10

Title: Juicy LAHM (Mutton) MANDI, 14-Dish PRAWN CURRY MEAL, KERALA | WHITE HOUSE RESTAURANT Wayanad
Description:
#PopularHighwayRestaurants #Wayanad #GourmetOnTheRoad

Restaurants On Wayanad - Calicut Road. Popular Restaurants In Wayanad. White House Restaurant. Making Of Mutton Mandi. Pidi Kozhi Porichatu. White House Restaurant Wayanad Road, Puduppadi, Kozhikode Road

Although a relatively recent eatery, White House Restaurant located in Puduppadi has turned into a dining hotspot for travellers on the Wayanad-Kozhikode route. Lured by its enticing offerings that include traditional Keralan dishes cooked on wood-fired stoves and much loved Arabian dishes like the Mandi, prepared in deep rubber wood-fired brick pits, we had to stop here for a meal enroute to Kozhikode. 

Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna relishes a 14-dish Prawn Curry Meal, a juicy Pidi Kozhi Porichathu, the Mutton Mandi of course, and a Ayakora or King Fish Fry.

TAWA FISH 
The kingfish has been cocooned in a masala with coconut milk as its base and hence the spicicing is quite gentle in its warmth. I like the crunch of the coconut flakes in the masala. 
Rs. 300 (usd 4.2)
8/10

PRAWN CURRY MEALS 
I was expecting a bowl of prawn curry and rice, but instead it came in a procession of 14 dishes packed into tiny bowls. The prawns were fresh and cooked with the head, which is where the flavour pop is! A nice touch were the drumsticks in the curry. Also enjoyed the crunch of the beans poriyal, the bitter gourd, the fish pickle and the red chilli chutney with a touch of sweetness. The paruppu payasam is the perfect end to the meal here.
Rs. 140 (usd 2)
10/10

PIDHI KOZHI PORICHATHU
A juicy bird despite its scrawny size, and served with a mutta (egg). The fried curry leaves makes for a toasty relish. One of the signature dishes here, loved the crunch of the masala that this chicken is covered in before being deep fried. 
Rs. 200 (usd 2.8)
9/10

MUTTON MANDI 
cooked the traditional way in a brick-lined pit oven. The meat peels away effortlessly from the bone with a thin flavourful veil of fat. The rice is scented with the meat juices and hit of saffron. The mandi is served with a smattering of chutneys, but I preferred savouring the delicate flavours of the dish sans any condiment. 
Rs. 550 (usd 7.7) 
9/10

Title: Unusual SALEM IDLI, ONION DOSE | DOSE MANJANNA, A Son’s Tribute, Father’s 48-Year Street Cart Legacy
Description:
#Bangalore #IdliDosa #GourmetOnTheRoad

Dose Manjanna, Must Try Salem Idli, Butter Idli, Onion Open Dosa, Mysore Masala Dosa, Jayanagar, Bengaluru, Vegetarian, Street Food


Manjanna ran a popular street cart for 48 years in the South Bengaluru suburb of Jayanagar selling only three or four dishes, dose, idli and vada, earning him the moniker, Dose Manjanna. His son, Ganesh, seeks to keep alive his late father’s legacy in a tiny shop, aptly named Dose Manjanna, serving a smattering of traditional and some accidentally inspired creations, like the buttery, spicy Salem Idli. Concocted on a cold, rainy night, when his store had run out of hot idlis, in a bid to acquiesce to a customer’s demand for hot food just prior to the latter’s boarding a bus for Salem. 

In this #gourmetontheroad episode, Food Lovers’ editor, Kripal Amanna tastes the Salem Idli, a scrumptious ghee onion dose and a couple of other tiffin treats that has Jayanagar’s denizens crowding this eatery at all times. Hope you enjoy this episode.

SALEM IDLI
This Idli roasted in butter, sings the flavour of the butter with the spicy, grainy crunch of the podi. Eat it piping hot, just off the tawa. When it cools down, pair it with the spicy hurigadale (fried gram) chutney.
Rs. 20 (usd 0.3)
8.5/10

Butter Idli 
Thatte idli roasted on a hot tawa over melted butter, with lashings of butter and served with a dollop of butter, this is sheer decadence. The idli loses some its fervour as it begins to cool, and that’s when you taste its slight tartness.
Rs. 20 (usd 0.3)
8/10

Open Onion Dose
Served folded, this crisp, kadak dose was the highlight for me. Dripping with ghee and butter, smeared with chutney podi, a generous sprinkling of moist, crunchy onions, this dose is flavourful enough to be eaten on its own. The chutneys served alongside play a distant second fiddle to this open onion dose. 
Rs. 40 (usd 0.6)
9/10

Mysore Masale Dose
The masale is smeared into a paste with chutney podi, butter and onions as the dose is roasted on the tava. I expected it to be robust in its flavours, however the potatoes seem to tone down the aggression of the chutney podi, making this a gently-spiced bite. Mix together the gram chutney, chutney podi and butter that’s served alongside, and combine with the dose to savour a spicy mouthful. 
Rs. 40 (usd 0.6)
8/10

Shavige Baath 
The shavige baath here is light, fluffy and springy, tossed in a chitranna or lemon rice masala. Studded liberally with peanuts, fried lentils, flecks of green chilli and roasted curry leaves, it makes a gentle yet persuasive impression on the palate. If you like it spicy, enjoy it with the smokey tomato-red chilli-roasted gram chutney.
Rs. 30 (usd 0.4)
8.5

Title: TASTY VEGETARIAN TWIST | Parmesan KHICHDI, Avocado PAPDI, HALWA Mousse, Coffee MALAI| STREET STORYSS
Description:
#Vegetarian #Bangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad

Street Storyss, Vegetarian Street Food With A Twist, Vegetarian Restaurant in Bengaluru, Bangalore, Indiranagar, World Cuisine, Indian Cuisine, Burmese Cuisine, Asian Cuisine, Tibetan Cuisine, Italian Cuisine,  Chef Nishant Choubey
 
Street Storyss caters to the discerning vegetarian palate with its playful adaptations of ‘street flavours’ from the world. Chef Nishant Choubey, curator of the cuisine here says they seek to take popular fare and add a unique dimension that elevates the original dish.

Intrigued, Food Lovers’ editor, Kripal Amanna, takes up the chef’s invitation to visit this popular eatery in Indiranagar, Bengaluru, and taste a smorgasbord of creations - Rajma Ghee Khichdi, Tibetan Laping Roll, Soba Khow Suey, Mushroom Salad, Thai Corn Cake, Coconut Pancakes... some a delightful confluence of flavours and textures, some rather unexpected, but all vegetarian! Enjoy!

Avocado Mousse
A papdi with Western aspirations, the desi yoghurt makes way for the creamy avocado mousse. The chutneys are replaced by piquant raw mango salsa and a refreshing tomato salsa.
Rs. 295 (usd 4.1)
8/10

Curried Cauliflower & Beetroot Soup
A vegan offering at Street Storyss, the warming spiced cauliflower broth combines with the sweet and sour beetroot puree in a lively jig on the palate. 
Price na
8.5/10

Pomegranate Kombucha 
A refreshing mocktail of fermented kombucha and fresh pomegranate.
Rs. 250 (usd 3.5)
7/10

Tibetan Laping Roll
These translucent noodle rolls deliver batons of pickled cucumber and watermelon in a chilled sweet and sour crunch, swathed with the nuttiness of sesame soy and the warming heat of ginger. 
Rs. 325 (usd 4.5)
9/10

Thai Corn Cake
Corn pureed and coaxed into a cake before being cubed and fried. The result is a lush, creamy appetiser, topped with toasted garlic and chilli. 
Rs. 325 (usd 4.5)
8.5/10

Bangkok Stir Fry 
This is a dish that seems atypical for an eggplant preparation. Bite into its deep-fried crunchy texture to savour its soft and mushy insides. Tossed in a chilli garlic sauce, this is certainly a dish that’s made for the spice-loving palate.
Rs. 325 (usd 4.5)
9/10

Warm Mushroom Salad
A dish with banging umami flavours, the shiitake has been poached with aromats rendering it soft and gentle on the bite. The cooked watermelon provides a fruity contrast to the star anise scented notes of the mushrooms.
Rs. 395 (usd 5.5)
9/10

Burmese Khow Suey
Soba noodles, placed atop a creamy yellow curry that’s rich in coconut flavour and the fragrant notes of fresh turmeric.  
Rs. 425 (usd 5.9)
8.5/10

Nasi Goreng
The black bean lends its fermented salty punch to the Nasi Goreng, but I found the preparation a tad dry and unappealing.
Rs. 325 (usd 4.5)
6/10

Rajma Ghee Khichdi
Far removed from the humble khichdi, this version is topped with crunchy khakra and slivers of parmesan. 
Rs. 425 (usd 5.9)
8/10

Coconut Pancake with Besan Halwa Mousse
Inspired by the Bengali patishapta, the pancakes are topped with a near-cloyingly sweet besan halwa mousse. The pancakes help rein in some of the sweetness, the banana chips help in this effort too.
Rs. 325 (usd 4.5)
8/10


Frozen Coffee Malai
This is the dessert to try if you like a milky dessert and coffee. Smooth in its consistency, its flavour harks back to a cardamom-scented kulfi or rabri, condensed milk.
Rs. 295 (usd 4.1)
9/10

Title: CTR - SHRI SAGAR | Bangalore’s Most Popular BENNE MASALA DOSA, GOLI BAJJI, IDLI & More | Malleswaram
Description:
#Vegetarian #CTR #GourmetOnTheRoad

Central Tiffin Room, CTR Malleswaram, Shri Sagar, Bangalore’s Most Famous Benne Masala Dose, Goli Bajji, Mangalore Bajji, Kesari Bath, Masala Dosa, Maddur Vade, Rava Idli, Ordinary Masala Dosa, Filter Coffee

When it comes to the Benne Masala Dosa, all roads lead to CTR - Shri Sagar or Central Tiffin Room in Bengaluru. The city’s love for this butter drenched dose goes back a few decades when the present owners took charge of this 70-year old establishment that served as the only eatery in the historic Malleswaram area.

Food Lovers’ editor, Kripal Amanna catches up with Sandesh Pujari, third generation owner of this landmark eatery and explores what makes the benne dose special, before indulging in a tiffin treat that includes not just their most loved offering, but other equally popular snacks like the Mangalore bajji, Maddur Vade and more. Enjoy!

Rava Idli
The soft rava idli makes for a wholesome, comforting tiffin, bathe it in the kai (coconut) chutney or savour it with the vegetable sagu that is packed with nutrition and flavour.
Rs. 29 (usd 0.4)
8.5/10

Goli Bajji
Scrumptious with a bit of a stretchy pull on the bite, and served steaming hot, the goli bajji is a must-have when you are at CTR for an evening snack. Relish it just by itself, with its slight hint of sweetness, or dunk it into the chutney to make for a spirited mouthful.
Rs. 35 (usd 0.5)
9/10

Maddur Vade
This vade has the texture of a scrumptiously flakey cookie. On the palate, one tastes the deep savoury notes of the fried onion. Relish it while at CTR, or also carry some home, it makes for a great snack on the go
Rs. 29 (usd 0.4)
8/10

Ordinary Masala Dosa 
The dose is roasted kadak (crisp), and smeared with a generous amount of kempu (red) coconut chutney inside that lends a tinge of heat. The creamy masale, potato palya, barely whispers its flavours, but lends a great supporting act to the dose that takes centerstage with every bite.
Rs. 52 (usd 0.7)
8.5/10

Benne Masala Dosa
This butter-drenched gold-hued dose is blessed with the perfect gentle crackle. On the palate, one tastes the lushness of the homemade butter that envelopes every bite of the dose, the palya and the chutney with its delicious veil. If you need one reason to visit CTR, this would be it.
Rs. 57 (usd 0.8)
10/10

Kesari Bath 
Dripping in ghee and topped with toasted cashews and raisins, the grainy kesari bath almost melts away when placed in the mouth. The cashew provides an element of nuttiness and the raisin, pops of sweetness to this semolina preparation.
Rs. 29 (usd 0.4)
9/10

Coffee 
A fitting end to a meal here.
Rs. 15 (usd 0.2)
8/10

Title: Tasting HOT & SPICY DARJEELING STYLE MOMOS | Chicken, Paneer, Vegetarian | STEAMED, FRIED & SZECHUAN
Description:
#Momos #StreetFood #GourmetOnTheRoad

Hot Momos, Unique Momos, Darjeeling Style, Indian Street Food, Bengaluru, Bangalore, Steamed Dumplings, Steamed Vegetable Momo, Steamed Paneer Mom, Steamed Chicken Momo, Fried Chicken Momos, Fried Chicken Momos in Szechuan Sauce, Street Food, Momos, Bengaluru Street Food, Veg Momos, Veg Momos Indian Style, Veg Momo Recipe, Chicken Momo, Fried 

This tiny dim sum shop serves momos with a difference, says its owner, Dawa Lepcha, a migrant from Darjeeling into Bengaluru, “they are steamed fresh with the filling raw, which makes them juicier than other momos.” I put his claim to the test as I taste an assortment of momos - steamed, fried and sauced, spicy, in this snacky Gourmet On The Road outing. Enjoy! 

Steamed Vegetable Momo
Stuffed with a cabbage, carrot, bean and capsicum filling that’s enlivened with a ginger-garlic and green chilli paste, this is a savoury momo, quite flavourful for a veggie option.  If you like it spicy, go for the chilli sauce. 
Rs. 60 (usd 0.8) for 8 pieces
7.5/10

Steamed Paneer Momo
I was quite cynical of this momo before I tasted it. But one bite and I changed my mind! If I were a vegetarian, I would be quite happy with this momo stuffed with soft paneer and slivers of green chilli. Flavourful enough to be eaten on its own minus the chutney.
Rs. 70 (usd 1) for 8 pieces
7.5/10

Steamed Chicken Momo
The chicken momo had spent a bit longer in the steamer than necessary, and therefore weak in the strength of the dumpling wrap. The chicken stuffing is the consistency of a soft paste, and though flavourful, a bit shy in asserting itself on the palate. I wish this momo was served hot though.
Rs. 70 (usd 1) for 8 pieces
7/10

Fried Chicken Momos
These deep-fried momos are crispy and crunchy outside and doughy inside. An interesting contrast of textures that makes for an interesting bite. Though I wasn’t a fan of its chatpata taste with the chaat masala that’s sprinkled quite liberally on the momo..
Rs. 80 (usd 1.1) for 8 pieces
7/10

Fried Chicken Momos in Szechuan Sauce
The Szechuan style spicy momo tops the ‘fiery’ chart here and is certainly not for the faint-hearted. All that you taste here is tonnes of chilli spice, the momo ends up being just a dumpling that has surrendered to the assault of the spicy sauce.
Rs. 100 (usd 1.4) for 8 pieces
6/10

Title: Spicy KONGUNADU VILLAGE STYLE Tamil Food | KOTHANUR KITCHEN Bangalore |MUTTON URUNDAI, NETHLI KURUMA
Description:
#TamilCuisine #NonVegetarian #GourmetOnTheRoad

Kothanur Kitchen, Authentic Kongunadu Cuisine, Tamil Cuisine, Village Style Salem Food, Kothanur, Bengaluru, Bangalore, Kothu Parotta, Mutton Kola Urundai, Egg Boti Fry, Naatu Kozhi Fry, Nethili Kuzhambu, Naati Kozhi Kuruma, Chicken Biryani, Mutton Biryani, Non Vegetarian 

This village style eatery in the North Bengaluru suburbs of Kothanur draws inspiration from Kongunadu cuisine and the streets of Salem in its hearty non vegetarian Tamil fare. Kothanur Kitchen favours cooking over wood fire and a strict no-refrigeration policy, ensuring that everything that is served is cooked with fresh ingredients for the day. 

Food Lovers’ Editor visits the restaurant to savour some of the most popular dishes served here, from a Mutton Kola Urundai to Egg Boti Fry, a vivacious Netholi Curry and more. Enjoy! 

Kothu Parotta
Robust in its spicing, this parotta that has soaked up the egg masala and chicken sherva will transport you to the street stalls of Salem. 
Rs. 80 (usd 1.1)
8/10

Mutton Kola Urundai
Love the texture of these spiced mutton mince balls, it's got a bit of a crunch as you bite into it but is yielding inside. The meat hasn’t been ground to a paste, and the spicing is gentle, leaves behind a happy warmth on the palate. 
Rs. 200 (usd 2.8)
9/10

Egg Boti Fry 
The boti is prepped and cooked rather well too. There is none of the raw ‘animal’ scent that one smells if offal meat isn't cleaned well. 
Rs. 150 (usd 2.1)
8/10

Naatu Kozhi Fry 
At first bite, I felt the meat was a bit too tough, although I enjoyed the flavours of the fry - the tartness of the tomato, the mild sweetness of the onions and the savouriness of the Salem masala. However, as you chew on the chicken, it releases the flavours of the masala it has been cooked in. 
Rs. 200 (usd 2.8)
8.5/10

Nethli Kozhambu
This Sunday special fish curry  at Kothanur Kitchen combines the humble nethili fish with the puckeringly sour raw mango in a curry pot that’s cooked slowly over a wood fire. 
Rs. 150 (usd 2.1)
9/10


Naati Kozhi Kuruma 
The chicken is cooked with the skin, which lends a fulsome flavour to the kuruma. The kuruma in itself is rather delicately flavoured, allowing one to savour the flavour of the meat and the lingering warmth of the spices.
Rs. 200 (usd 2.8)
8.5/10

Mutton Kuruma 
The fat flavour in this kuruma is quite pronounced, I also found the meat a tad chewy. On a positive note, the gravy benefits from the richness of the fat on the meat. 
Rs. 180 (usd 2.5)
7/10

Chicken Biryani 
The rice is quite flavourful once you get past its slight stickiness. On the palate you taste the freshness of the mint and coriander, the acidity of the tomatoes amidst the spices.  
Rs. 130 (usd 1.8)
8/10

Mutton Biryani 
The mutton biryani is restrained in its spice notes and spotlights the flavour of the meat. The rice is cooked perfectly in this naati, country style biryani, with the fat lending its deep savoury unctuousness.
Rs. 200 (usd 2.8)
8.5/10

Kalaki 
In case you haven’t had enough of the meaty preparations here, the custardy goodness of the kalaki, an egg and chicken curry mix that's cooked to the point where the egg begins to coagulate, provides the perfect end to a Kongunadu meal.  
Rs. 30 (usd 0.4)
7.5/10


ADDRESS -  Kothanur Kitchen, Sy. No. 28/3 & 28/4, K Narayanapura Road, Kothanur, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560077; tel +91 95358 11681

Title: Rare BENGALURU ACREY IDLI Served By A 30-year-old FAMILY-RUN Eating House, SSP REFRESHMENTS | Pulav
Description:
#VegetarianBreakfast #AuthenticBreakfast #GourmetOnTheRoad

SSP Refreshments, also known as Mudanna Hotel, Mixing Hotel, Jayanagar, Bangalore, serves rare Bangalore Idli, Acrey Idli, Acre idli, Ikrey Idli, Pulav, Vegetable Pulav, Palav, Chitranna, Vada, Uppitu, Mosaru Anna, Vegetarian Breakfast, Bangalore, Breakfast, Idli, Chutney, Mudanna Pulav

With recipes gleaned from his father-in-law, Devaraju and his wife began a small venture out of their home nearly 30 years ago, serving what is now a rare Bangalore breakfast delicacy, the Acrey Idli. Since then, SSP Refreshment House has amassed a formidable reputation for its limited menu, an aromatic vegetable pulav, chitranna and a couple of other dishes, that run out not too long from the time they open doors to their home at 7 am.

Food Lovers’ editor, Kripal Amanna savours some of the dishes and also peeps into the kitchen to chat with the family and catch the making of the now-largely-lost Bengaluru Acrey Idli. Enjoy! 

Acrey Idli 
The idli is soft and unbelievably pliable, melts in the mouth when hot. You can smell the gentle sweet aroma of the batter which is perfectly fermented rendering a springy fluffiness to the idli. The thick, spicy lentil chutney with flecks of dry coconut makes for a great accompaniment.
Rs. 20 (usd 0.3)
9/10

Chitranna 30/ 20
You can taste the gentle tartness of the lemon, the flavour of cumin and pointed notes of green chilli on the palate, the lentils in the seasoning make for a nice bite.
Rs. 20/30 (usd 0.3/ 0.4) for half/ full portion
7/10

Pulav 
A flavourful pulav with the lingering warmth that comes from spices such as cinnamon and cloves, this is what draws customers to SSP. There’s the spicy kick of green chilli, but juxtaposed against the other ingredients, its hit is not the sort that obliterates your tastebuds. The seasoned chutney served alongside adds a layer of pleasing nuttiness. 
Rs. 20/30 (usd 0.3/0.4) for half/ full portion
8.5/10

Mosaru Anna  
Gentle on the palate, this provides cooling respite if one has overindulged in the spicy pulav and chutney.
Rs. 20/30 (usd 0.3/ 0.4) for half/ full portion
7.5/10

Title: Breakfast at SHIVAJI MILITARY HOTEL | Most Popular CHICKEN DONNE BIRYANI Making Revealed! BANGALORE
Description:
#ShivajiMilitaryHotel #DonneBiryani #GourmetOnTheRoad

Bengaluru's most popular Shivaji Military Hotel, Chicken Donne Biryani, Mutton Donne Biryani, Breakfast, Bengaluru's Top Restaurants, Biryani

What begins as a visit by Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna, to check out this iconic restaurant’s breakfast soon turns into a never-seen-before-on-video demonstration on the making of Bengaluru’s most famous chicken biryani, the Donne Biryani at Shivaji Military Hotel, a restaurant that has stood tall for over eight decades for its local-influenced Maratha fare.

Needless to say, he also catches a full military-style breakfast that includes a nourishing paaya soup, chicken leg masala, chops, mutton liver, khaali dose and steaming hot donne biryani. 

Lunch at Shivaji Military Hotel video - https://youtu.be/XxatALJz0Ro

Leg Soup
The gelatine has rendered well into the broth and glistens on the surface, you taste the flavour of the fat in the broth and the spicing too, especially the green chilli. The trotter is the sort that melts in your mouth. 
Rs. 160 (usd 2.2) for 2 legs.
8.5/10

Chicken Chops 
A rich, spicy green masala of coriander, mint and onions, studded with green peas. The juicy chicken pieces tame the salty savoury punch of the gravy. The khali dose makes for the perfect companion to taste the chicken chops masala. 
Rs. 190 (usd 2.6)
9/10

Chicken Leg Piece
Plump chicken legs cooked nice and juicy down to the bone. Definitely not a dish for the faint-hearted, you can taste the searing heat of the red chilli powder in this gravy. The onions,  tomatoes and lime provide a mildly sweet-tart counterpoint to the chilli heat though. 
Rs. 160 (usd 2.2) for 2 pieces.
8.5/10

Mutton Liver 
The mutton liver is cooked to perfection in a green masala, has a springy bite and is soft and creamy inside. Absolutely delicious, the intense earthiness of the liver goes well with the salty savouriness of the gravy.
Rs. 150 (usd 2.1)
10/10

Mutton Dry
The fat bits in the meat pieces add flavour. I tasted this piping hot off the stove, but I wish the meat had rested in the masala for a bit post cooking for me to better savour this peppery preparation. 
Rs. 190 (usd 2.6)
8/10

Chicken Donne Biryani 
You can taste the ingredients that have gone into Shivaji Military Hotel’s iconic donne biryani the moment you place the intensely flavourful rice in your mouth. The sweetness of the spices, the star anise, the mild astringency of the cloves, the fresh bite of the herbs, the pointed pungency from the green chillies, the tartness of tomato and the lime. The ghee coats the rice with a film of lushness, you can smell the smokiness from the dum. The chicken is delicate in its flavour, and not as effusive. Savour it with the rice to enjoy the complete range of flavours in this dish. 
Rs. 190 (usd 2.6)
9/10

Title: Bangalore’s ‘Oldest’ SEAFOOD Spot, HOTEL FISHLAND | KONKANI, MANGALOREAN Fish, Prawn FRY, Crab CURRY
Description:
#Seafood #Bengaluru #GourmetOnTheRoad

Hotel Fishland, 38-year-old seafood restaurant in Bengaluru, specialising in Konkani and South Canara coastal cuisine. Opened in 1982. hotel fishland, gandhinagar, bengaluru, fishland bangalore, fishland gandhinagar bangalore, seafood thaali, seafood thali, special seafood thaali, banged fry, mackerel fry, kana curry, ladyfish curry, prawns fry, crab curry, denji curry, clams, marvai sukka, mangalorean cuisine, konkani cuisine, saraswat cuisine

Established in 1982, Hotel Fishland in Gandhinagar, Bengaluru is one of the city’s oldest dining spots to cater to a seafood craving. Specialising in Konkani and coastal Mangalorean cuisine, the most popular item here is the seafood thaali.

Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits revisits this establishment and savours not just the special ‘limited’ seafood thaali, but a host of other delicacies like the crab curry, bangude (mackerel) fry and prawns masala amongst others. Enjoy!

Special Limited Fish Thaali 
This thaali, complete with a fish curry, fish fry, vegetable of the day, rice, buttermilk and yoghurt had the potential to be a rather satisfying fish meal, especially given the fulsome flavours of the kaane curry. However, it was let down by the kingfish fry that although swathed in a spirited masala and crumb-fried, wasn't the epitome of freshness. Next time, I would order either a fish curry or the limited thaali that arrives minus the fry, but offers terrific value at at Rs. 180, and a fish fry separately.
Rs. 320 (usd 5.3)
7/10

Bangude Fry 
This is what a fish fry should be all about. The mackerel was fresh, plump and juicy. Fried such that the masala formed a thick crust. You can taste the heat of the chilli and the tang of the tamarind in the masala, this combination of spicy and sour made for the perfect complement to the oily flavours of the mackerel. 
Rs. 160 (usd 2.2)
10/10

Prawns Fry
You can taste the sweetness of the sea prawns notwithstanding the robust masala. The prawns are fresh, springy to the bite and the masala coating this crustacean is fried to a delightful crust. Order these for sure.
Rs. 295 (usd 4.1)
9/10

Marvai Sukka 
The clams are wanting in their flavour. All that you taste is the masala, the clams barely make their presence felt. 
Rs. 160 (usd 2.2)
6/10

Crab Masala 
The crab is delicious, plump with briny-sweet flavoured flesh. Chew on the crab shell unabashedly to lap up every ounce of its goodness that also carries the flavour of the curry. The curry too has tones of the crab ‘sweetness’. Another winner here at Fishland.
Rs. 275 (usd 3.8)
9.5/10

Title: Exploring BANGALORE’S  Tasty AVAREBELE FESTIVAL| VV PURAM FOOD STREET |Avarebele Vada, Dosa, Jilebi!
Description:
#AvarebeleMela #Bengaluru #GourmetOnTheRoad

Bengaluru’s Annual Avarebele Mela at Sri Vasavi Vaisistha THindi, VV Puram Food Street, Farm to Food, Hyacinth Beans, Hithkabele Masala Vade, Hithkabele Bonda, Avarebele Dose - Hithkabele Saru, Hithkabele Akki Rotti, Avarebele Mosaru Kodubale, Hithkabele Holige, Hithkabele Honey Jalebi, Payasa, Ellavare, Street Food

Now in its 20th year, Bengaluru’s annual Avarebele Mela that celebrates the Bengaluru bean in an array of ‘snacky’ preparations, goes back to a time when farmers from in and around Bengaluru would congregate in VV Puram to sell their harvest of Avarekai. Given the bean’s short shelf life, any unsold produce would be thrown away. Which prompted Mrs Geetha Shivakumar, owner of Sri Vasavi Vasisitha Mane Thindi to put together a food festival that would make use of the Avarebele. And thus began a unique collaboration between farmers and a food entrepreneur that now has Bangalore’s food lovers congregating here for their share of deliciousness.

Food Lovers’ Editor visits the mela and tasted a delicious smorgasbord of preparations, from vade to bonda to dose to hollige to rotti to jalebi to payasa to pootharekulu, with one ingredient in common, the avarebele. Enjoy!

Hithkabele Masala Vade
A top draw at the mela, and also all year around, one can taste the freshness of coriander and dill in this spicy hithabele masala vade. 
Rs. 20 (usd 0.3) for 2 nos.
9/10

Hithkabele Bonda
A tad mellow in flavour, the bonda benefits from the weight of the avarekalu. It’s a pleasing snack, but fails to make as impactful an impression on the palate as the masala vade. 
Rs. 20 (usd  0.3) for 2 nos.
7/10

Avarebele Dose - Hithkabele Saru
The most popular item at the mela, this dosa is topped with a spirited mix of avarebele, coriander, dil and onions. 
Rs. 60 (usd 0.8)
9.5/10

Hithkabele Akki Rotti
The akki roti is toasted nice and thin, and crispened around the edges making for a delightful crunch. 
Rs. 50 (usd 0.7)
8.5/10

Avarebele Mosaru Kodubale
Crisp and crunchy on the bite, but chewy as you linger on this bangle-shaped jeera and ajwain flavoured treat made of steamed rice flour, yoghurt and avarebele.
Rs. 30 (usd 0.4) for 4 nos.
8/10

Hithkabele Holige
Dripping with ghee and stuffed with tuvar dal, jaggery and hithkabele, one can taste the lingering aroma of cardamom on the palate. 
Rs. 30 (usd 0.4)
8.5/10

Hithkabele Honey Jalebi
The jalebi are a light pista green in colour from the avarebele which lends its strength to the fermented batter and renders the jalebis cripier and also lends it a tart edge.  
Rs. 20 (usd 0.3) for 4 nos.
8.5/10

Payasa
The avarebele payasa is smokey in its flavour. Although made with gas gase, poppy seeds, one does not taste the nuttiness of the ingredient. 
Rs. 30 (usd 0.3)
6.5/10

Ellavare
Sesame seeds, coconut milk, avarebele and jaggery come together in this thick dessert. I quite enjoyed the crunch of the fresh coconut and the earthy sweetness of the jaggery.
Rs. 30 (usd 0.3)
7/10

Putharekulu
The avarebele makes its way into the putharekulu as well. However, I’m tasting more of the wrap in this version as compared to the filling and that takes away from the enjoyment of what is otherwise an interesting sweet.
Rs. 30 (usd 0.3)
6/10

Title: IYENGAR HOMESTYLE Breakfast At TKS IYENGAR’s |UNIQUE DISHES! Nuchinna Unde, BaleEle Idli, Hayagreeva
Description:
#VegetarianBreakfast #AuthenticBreakfast #GourmetOnTheRoad

TKS Iyengar’s must-visit for authentic Iyengar dishes. Three Generations Family Recipes, Vegetarian, No Garlic, Unique Homestyle Dishes, bale elle idli, thatte idli, classic idli, nuchinna unde, puliyogare, ottu shavige, god halubai, hayagreeva, sweet pongal, bangalore, breakfast

This recent entrant to Bengaluru’s vegetarian dining landscape located in the suburb of Basaveshwaranagar serves up Iyengar homestyle fare. Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits this eatery for a late breakfast where he tastes an array of dishes, some hitherto unseen in restaurants, such as the Nuchinna Unde, Halubai, Hayagreeva (originally prepared as a temple offering), Ottu Shavige and more. He also meets the three generations of the TKS Iyengar family that is seeking to share its interesting culinary traditions with the people of Bengaluru though this endearing enterprise. Enjoy!

Bale Elle Idli 
The Bale Elle Idli carries with it the subtle aroma of the banana leaf in which it is steamed. The leaf also imbues the idli with a light colouring. You bite into the crunch of coconut and the lentils as you taste the idli, savour it with the sambar that’s perfect in its sour-sweet balance and the spirited chutney. Rs. 30 (usd 0.4) for 2 pcs
9/10

Thatte Idli
A deliciously delicate thatte idli, springy like it should be. Acts as the perfect canvas of sorts to soak up the flavours of the chutney and sambar.
Rs. 30 (usd 0.4) for 2 pcs
8.5/10

Classic Idli
Grainy in texture and porous, but pales in comparison to the bale elle and thatte idli served here.
Rs. 12 (usd 0.2)
7/10

Nuchinna Unde
If you need only one reason to visit TKS Iyengar, these steamed dumplings made of four lentil varieties would be it. A traditional Iyengar recipe wouldn’t use onions, but these are added here due to the wants of running a commercial establishment, which lends it a delightful crunch alongside the lentils. Rs. 30 (usd 0.4) for 2 pcs
10/10

Puliyogare
Cooked and cooled rice, flavoured with spicy tamarind paste and fortified with the crunch of lentils and ground lentils, this is a Iyengar classic with the perfect balance of flavours - touch of sweet that gives into sour and the warmth of  the spices. The puliyogare here is made with red rajamudi rice from Hassan. 
Rs. 50 (usd 0.7)
9/10

Ottu Shavige
This sweet and ‘khaara’ combo is served with ella pudi (a powder made of sesame seeds, peanuts and jaggery) gasgase (poppy seed) payasa and a nutty, spicy chutney, enlivened with mustard oil and red chillies.  
Rs. 60 (usd 0.8)
9/10

Godhi Halubai
Made with puree of wheat, coconut milk and jaggery, this wobbly pudding like dessert magically disappears into sweet ‘nothingness’ when you place a piece in your mouth.
Rs. 10 (usd 0.15)
8/10

Hayagreeva 
Taste the creaminess of lentils and the bite of dried coconut and cashew nuts in this decadently sweet dessert that was originally made as an offering to Lord Hayagreeva. 
Rs. 50 (usd 0.7)
8.5/10

Sweet Pongal
The whiff of edible camphor that greets you on the palate disappears quickly into the background, leaving you to relish the milky richness of this rice and lentil dessert.
Rs. 50 (usd 0.7)
8/10

Coffee 
Nice way to end things after an indulgent meal here.
Rs. 10 (usd 0.15)
7/10

Title: FULL BENGALI LUNCH | Esplanade | Shukto, BHAJA, Bhetki PATURI, Katla JHOL, Kosha Mangsho, Mishti DOI
Description:
#BengaliFood #Bangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad 

Esplanade, Authentic Bengali Restaurant, Indiranagar, Bengaluru. Recipes from Chef Subhankar Dhar’s Mother. Best Bengali Restaurant in Bangalore, shuktoni, begun bhaja, bhetki paturi, daab chingri, katla jhol, kasha mangsho, mishit doi, rosogolla

Esplanade has been catering to Bengali palates in Bengaluru for the last 12 years. Helmed by Chef Subhankar Dhar, a native of Kolkata, it is the destination to savour an authentic Bengali meal experience in an elegant setting.

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor catches up with Chef Dhar before settling down to a sumptuous meal that covers the entire spectrum of a Bengali lunch - from shukto to dal to bhaja to paturi, jhol, mangsho and chutney before ending with mishti, desserts. Enjoy! 

SHUKTONI 
The traditional way to start a Bengali lunch, the Shuktoni, made with cow’s milk, sun dried lentil dumplings and flavoured with wild celery seeds, radhuni, is rich in vegetables. 
Rs. 195 (usd 2.7)
9/10

BHAJA MUNGER DAL
This is a comforting lentil dish, mellow in its flavours, embellished with fresh peas and hint of cumin in its ghee seasoning. 
Rs. 185 (usd 2.6)
8/10

BEGUN BHAJA 
Thick, fleshy slices of eggplant, roasted on a tawa. The pulpy ‘begun’ has a sweetish edge contrasted by the slightly bitter tones of its skin. A
Rs. 175 (usd 2.5) for 4 pcs
9/10

JHUE JHUREE ALOO BHAJA 
Rs. 155 (usd 2.2)
7/10

DHOKAR DALNA 
Lentil, gram flour cakes simmered in a spicy tomato onion gravy. The stodgy texture of the dhokar is lifted by the spirited flavours of the spicy gravy, dalna. 
Rs. 235 (usd 3.3)
8/10

BHETKI PATURI
This dish is an ode to the Bengali palate’s fascination with mustard. The Kolkata bhetki is swathed in a paste of mustard, coconut and green chillies, wrapped in a banana leaf and roasted, rendering the fish firm to the touch but moist inside. Rs. 475 (usd 6.7)

9/10

DAAB CHINGRI 
The sweetness of the coconut milk and tender coconut, the punch of mustard, the grainy texture of poppy seeds and the heat from green chillies come together to make this flavourful curry.  
Rs. 595 (usd 8.3)
8.5/10

KATLA JHOL
The plump piece of katla, a pond fish, is fried first before being introduced to the curry which has a lilt of fennel in its flavours. The fish is earthy in its aroma, has a bit of a bite around the edges and its soft and fleshy texture is the perfect medium to soak up the flavours of the jhol. 
Rs. 395 (usd 5.5)
10/10

KASHA MANGSHO 
A slow cooked dish of onions and meat in equal measure, braised over four hours, the kasha mangsho epitomises ‘meaty indulgence’! The fat, gelatin and marrow of the meat lend to the savoury, unctuous character of the dark, braised onions. Rs. 495 (usd 7)
10/10

TOMATO KHEJUR CHUTNEY
Rs. 95 (usd 1.3)
8/10

MISHTI DOI 
Flavoured with seasonal, nolen or nutan, meaning ‘new’, gur, jaggery tapped from the date palm, this is a lush, sweet end to the meal at Esplanade. 
Rs. 145 (usd 2)
9/10

BAKED ROSOGOLLA 
Rosogolla made with nolen gur, soaked in a sugar-nolen gur syrup, topped with a nolen gur enriched reduced milk before being baked, this mishti screams decadent indulgence. 
Rs. 195 (usd 2.7)
8/10

Title: TOP 9 CHAATS At Bangalore’s Oldest Chaat Shop GANGOTREE | KING OF Tasty KOLKATA, North INDIAN CHAATS
Description:
#BangaloreStreetFood #Chaats #GourmetOnTheRoad 

Gangotree Chaats and Sweets, Bangalore’s oldest and favourite chaat shop for Kolkata and North Indian style chaats, since 1986. Paani Puri, Jhal Mudi, Aloo Tikki Chola, Masala Cola, Rasagoola Chaat, Masala Puri, Dahi Samosa, Sev Puri, Channa Moth Chaat, Malai Ladoo

One of Bengaluru’s earliest chaat destinations, Gangotree has been satisfying chaat cravings since 1986 with its Kolkata and North Indian chaat offerings. In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers editor, Kripal catches up with second generation owner, Raj Sethia over an indulgent chaat outing where he tastes over 9 of the eatery’s palate-teasing combinations. If you’re a chaat lover, this is for you! Enjoy! 

PAANI PURI
Super crunchy puri that holds together the spiced potato and bengal gram mix topped with the sweet, tangy paani, just long enough to unburden the delicious snack in your mouth. A riot of flavours and textures, this Kolkata style paani puri is a must-eat here.
rs. 40 (usd 0.6)
9/10

JHAL MUDI
True to its Kolkata roots, mustard oil is the hero in this concoction of puffed rice, potatoes, onions and peanuts. Served in a paper bag, this is the perfect fast food on the go for chaat lovers.
rs. 60 (usd 0.8)
8/10

ALOO TIKKI CHOLA
The aloo tikki, stuffed with green peas and grated coconut, has a nice crust. Topped with the hot chickpea gravy, this makes for a comforting snack. 
rs. 60 (usd 0.8)
8.5/10

MASALA COLA
A concoction of Indian cola served up with spices, it's the perfect thirst quencher to refresh the palate in between ‘chatpata’ plates of chaat.
rs. 50 (usd 0.7)
7/10

RASAGOOLA CHAAT
A unique creation here, the ‘dissolve-in-the-mouth’ rasagoola chaat appears quite bewildering. But the mild sweetness of the rasagoola seems to work with the sweet and spicy hit of chutneys, yoghurt and the crispy texture of sev. If you want to try something different, this is it.
Rs. 70 (usd 1)
8.5/10

MASALA PURI
Karnataka’s favourite chaat, I found it to be a bit mellow as compared to the pointed flavours of the other concoctions here. 
rs. 60 (usd 0.8)
7/10

DAHI SAMOSA
The crisp texture and robust flavours of the samosa have been tamed by the yoghurt. There’s the gentle aroma and flavour of fennel seeds in the samosa. Personally, I like the samosa just by itself.
rs. 60 (usd 0.8)
7/10

SEV PURI
The sev puri here plays ode to Mumbai’s streetfood with its perfect play of textures and tastes. There’s the crisp crunch of the papdi, the juicy crunch of onions and the cold creaminess of potatoes. The spicing is just perfect making every bite super-satisfying!
rs. 60 (usd 0.8)
9/10

CHANNA MOTH CHAAT
Made sans any fried ingredients, you need to specify this when you order, the channa moth chaat is a chatpata indulgence for the health conscious. This is what happens when chaat and salad come together. 
rs. 60 (usd 0.8)
8.5

MALAI LADOO
Rasagoola topped with reduced milk and saffron, this is a rich and indulgent dessert. 
rs. 30 (usd 0.4)
8/10

Title: ULTIMATE Calicut FISH CURRY, PAROTTA & CHICKEN FRY At Local Favourite HOTEL SAGAR | KERALA PRAWN FRY
Description:
#KeralaFood #CalicutFoodTrail #GourmetOnTheRoad 

Hotel Sagar, Calicut’s famous restaurant for fish curry, spring chicken fry, parotta, irani kebab, prawn dry fry, meen molagathu curry, pidhi kozhi porichathu, chicken biryani

A spot in Calicut that does not require too much of an introduction. Located at Mavoor Road, near the KSRTC Bus Stand, 45-year old Hotel Sagar serves a variety of food items from 6 am till late night at 2 am on all days of the week. So, depending on what you wish to have you can come here at any convenient time of the day. Meals, Parotta and Meen Curry, Pidi kozhi fry, Meen Porichathu, Chicken Biryani available here are an all-time hit among its customers.

Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna tastes some of the must-haves at this popular Kozhikoden eatery.
 
IRANI KEBAB
this dish is Hotel Sagar’s ode to the Middle Eastern region. Not a dish I would return for, but a tasty dish nonetheless.
rs. 240 (usd 3.3 )
6.5/10

PRAWN DRY FRY
the prawns are medium-sized and pack flavour. A tad excessive on salt, but nothing that a squeeze of lime can’t fix. I love the spicy-sweet bite of the prawn and toasty notes of coconut oil in which it has been fried. the sort of dish that will make a prawn lover happy. 
rs. 268 (usd 3.7)
8.5/10

AVOLI FISH FRY
The white pomfret is almost crunchy to the bite, the skin is fried to the perfect crisp and soft inside. If you like the flavour of your fish fry to be robust, eat it with a generous measure of the spicy coconut mix that’s garnishing the fish. 
rs. 375 (usd 5.2)
8.5/10

PIDI KOZHI PORICHATHU
it's a spring chicken, so there's tiny bones to work around to get to the meat. But once you get to the meat, it’s moist and delicious, swathed in a zesty coconut mixture. A must have dish at Hotel Sagar.
rs. 190 (usd 2.6 )
9/10

MEEN MOLAGATHU CURRY 
a hugely popular dish here, the fish has soaked up the spicy-sour flavours of the curry to the point where it almost disintegrates in your mouth sans any effort. The curry has a chilli kick that’s balanced by the acidity that comes from tamarind and tomatoes. The light rice pathiri and the layered parotta, both make for an ideal companion to mop up this tantalisingly tasty fish curry.
rs. 140 (usd 1.9)
10/10

CHICKEN BIRYANI
Kozhikoden style dum biryani made with kaima rice. the flavours in the biryani are well rounded, I definitely taste the prominent notes of cinnamon. The leghorn chicken is cooked to perfection and straddles the flavourful masala. 
rs. 172 (usd 2.4)
8.5/10

Mavoor Road Near KSRTC Bus Stand, Mavoor Road Junction, Kozhikode, Kerala 673001; tel: +91 495 272 0152

Title: MOST POPULAR Bangalore BREAKFAST At MAVALLI TIFFIN ROOMS | Making BEST Rava Idli | TASTING 11 ITEMS
Description:
#VegetarianBreakfast #BestRestaurantsInBangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad

Full Breakfast at MTR (Mavalli Tiffin Rooms) Restaurant, Lalbagh Road, Bengaluru, nearly 100-Years Old Eatery, Vegetarian Food, Bengaluru’s Most Popular Restaurant, Bengaluru's Most Popular Breakfast Spot, Rice Idli, Medu Vada, Rava Idli, Masala Dosa, Kesari Bath, Khara Bath, Chandrahara, Damroot, Dumrot, Badam Halwa,

This nearly-100-year-old establishment is chock full with customers every hour of the day when they are open. With a loyal fan following that values its adherence to age-old recipes and traditions to serve up consistent, wholesome South Indian fare, Mavalli Tiffin Rooms on Lalbagh Road is perhaps Bengaluru’s most popular breakfast destination.  

Food Lovers’ editor, Kripal Amanna drops in for a full breakfast and tastes 11 must-try dishes from this timeless eatery’s repertoire. He begins with a kitchen tour with VIkram Maiya, Managing Partner, MTR before sitting down to a sumptuous meal that includes amongst others, a dessert creation that’s the restaurant founder’s ode to French pastry. Enjoy!

RICE IDLI
The idlis are soft and a hot, buttery treat when had with the ghee. The coriander in the idli adds to its flavour. The idli dissolves in the mouth when immersed in the nourishingly thick sambar.
rs. 33 (usd 0.5)
8.5 

MEDU VADA
The vada exhibits a textbook crunch as it yields to the bite! Delicious with the sambar and comes alive with the spicy kick of the chutney. 
Rs. 44 (usd 0.6)
8

RAVA IDLI
Made of roasted semolina, yoghurt and speckled with fresh coriander, toasted cashews, and lentils, the rava idli makes for a hearty breakfast. The creamy potato sagu is a flavourful accompaniment to the rava idli.
Rs. 60 (usd 0.8)
10

KHARA BATH 
Fortified with carrots, slivers of green chilli and crested with a tomato slice, the khara bath is soft and crumbly, yet holds itself together. The pudina chutney helps tone down the tart notes of the lime and tomato. 
Rs. 62 (usd 0.9)
8

KESARI BATH
This breakfast treat glistens with the lushness of ghee. Embellished with toasted raisins and nuts, the kesari bath here is rich in its texture owing to the shavige (rice vermicelli) and semolina mix. 
Rs. 57 (usd 0.8)
9

MASALA DOSA
The dosa here is iconic and never disappoints. Made with a blend of three rice varieties, including two red rice varieties that lend a toasty colour tone, the dose is crisp outside and soft within. The palya is seasoned just right. Rs. 90 (usd 1.3)
10

PUDI DOSA
It’s soft, fluffy and big on flavours. You can taste the grainy crunch of lentils, the sharp, spicy notes of the chilli and the undertones of asafoetida. Tame its aggression with the palya and coconut chutney. 
Rs. 95 (usd 1.3)
8

DAMROOT 
Made of shredded pumpkin, semolina, raisins, nuts and tonnes of ghee, this MTR sweet is scented with cardamom. 
Rs. 47 (usd 0.6)
8.5

BADAM HALWA
You can ‘almost’ drink this lush, buttery, silken almond halwa enriched with ghee and flecks of saffron. 
Rs. 60 (usd 0.8)
10

CHANDRAHARA 
MTR’s ode to French pastry, this ‘sugary-sweet’ pastry is fried in pure ghee, garnished with almond slivers and doused with a khova (milk solids) syrup. 
Rs. 67 (usd 0.9)
8

Title: LOCAL Chef Prepares His FAMILY'S FAVE Kerala FISH CURRY + GreenPepper Mackerel Fry| The Raviz Kadavu
Description:
#FishCurryRecipe #FishCurry #GourmetOnTheRoad 

Traditional Kerala Fish Curry Recipe, Black Pomfret Curry, Spicy Curry, Avoli VaruthaRacha Curry, Green Pepper Mackerel Fry, Ayala Valli Kurumulagu, Poricha Pathiri, The Raviz Kadavu, Kozhikode, Chef Arun Ramanunni Nair

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers Editor, Kripal Amanna goes fish shopping with Chef Arun Ramanunni Nair of The Raviz Kozhikode, after which he watches the chef cook up a delicious sour and spicy fish curry with black pomfret. This Avoli Varutharacha curry is then savoured with a scrumptious Poricha Pathiri and boiled rice.

Chef Nair also serves up a unique mackerel fry, Ayala Valli Kurumulagu, flavoured with strings of green pepper pearls at Garam restaurant in the lush settings of The Raviz Kadavu, a stunning resort nestled on the banks of the legendary Chaliyar River just outside Kozhikode.

AYALA VALLI KURUMULAGU
This delightful twice-cooked fish is moist and flavoursome.  I've never tasted mackerel prepared like this before. you taste the tartness of the lime, the whisper of the cheriya pepper, sweetness of the shallots and the flavour of the fish  that rounds off everything. Eat with the pumpkin leaves if you're looking to get some fiber into your system.

AVOLI VARUTHARACHA CURRY
The fish has soaked up the robust flavours of roasted, hand-ground masala, you can taste the toasty, creamy notes of the coconut, the earthy flavours of the coriander and the sharp edge of the tamarind. The poricha pathiri makes for a scrumptious accompaniment to this delicious fish curry, as would some local boiled rice.

RECIPE FOR AVOLI VARUTHARACHA CURRY
Serves 4
 
For the fish marinade:
Black pomfret 500 gms (after cleaning)
Rock salt 1 ½ tsp 
Tamarind water 100 ml
 
For the ground masala:
Coconut oil 30 ml
Shallots 50 gms
Garlic 25 gms
Desiccated coconut 200 gms
Coriander seeds 40 gms
Whole dried red chilli 4 nos.
Curry leaves 10 gms
Turmeric powder 1 tsp
Coriander powder 2 tsp
Chilli powder 1 tsp
 
For the fish curry:
Coconut milk (50ml) at the finish to balance the dish.
Tomatoes, 2 nos.
Curry leaves 5 gms
 
For tempering:
Coconut oil 30 ml
Mustard seeds 10 gms
Fenugreek seeds 5 gms
Thin slices of shallots 30 gms
Bits of coconut 25 gms
Curry leaves 10 gms
Whole red chilli 2 nos.
 
Method of preparation:
Marinate the fish with rock salt and tamarind water. Keep aside for 30 minutes.
Saute the ingredients for ground masala till golden brown. Add turmeric, red chilli and coriander powder into the mix.
Remove masala mixture from fire and allow it to cool down. 
Make a fine paste, mix this masala into the marinated fish. Add two whole tomatoes, quartered into mix it well add curry leaves.
Put back on fire and allow it to simmer on a medium flame.
Occasionally, gently stir the curry until the fish is cooked.
Finish the preparation by adding coconut milk to balance the flavours. 
Make a tempering with the ingredients and ladle over the curry. Serve with hot rice or pathiri.

Title: This TEA SHOP Serves Up AMAZING Local Flavours With A DELICIOUS TWIST! ADAMINTE CHAYAKKADA Calicut
Description:
#KeralaFood #CalicutFoodTrail #GourmetOnTheRoad 

Adaminde Chayakkada, must visit destination for Malabari Food served with a twist, Kidilan Prawns Fry, Kozhi Porichathu, Kallumakaya Nirachathu, Kunzhi Kozhi Nirachathu, Elaneer Chicken, Mapranam Fish Curry, Chatti Choru, Parotta Kizhi, Avil Milk

A relatively new entrant to Kozhikode’s vibrant food scene, Adaminte Chayakkada or Adam’s tea shop is the brainchild of investment banker turned restaurateur, Aneez Adam. A self-confessed food lover, Aneez sought to showcase the culinary traditions of his Mappila community but in a format that seemed relevant to current times. And thus was born ACKD, as it is known in local parlance, a tea shop that celebrates quirk in its decor and innovation in some of the fare on the menu, a formula that seems to have helped position it firmly on Kozhikode’s dining map.

Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits Adaminte Chayakkada to chat with Aneez Adam and also taste some signatures on the menu, both traditional and dishes served up with the ACKD spin.

KIDILAN CHEMEEN FRY
Served quirkily in an old-fashioned iron box, these tiger prawns cooked in the skin are juicy and moist despite being charred. The prawns certainly hold their own against spicy assault of the red chilli aided by the toasty notes of coconut oil.
rs. 300 (usd 4.2)
9/10

KITABILEY KOZHI PORICHATHU
A chicken dish that will certainly hold your attention with its hot and spicy kick, If you’re faint-hearted, you may want to tame the chilli in this satay with a squeeze of lime.
rs. 235 (usd 3.3)
8.5/10

KALLUMAKAYA NIRACHATHU
A popular Kozhikoden snack, this dish of mussels stuffed with rice flour and then deep-fried with spices is a fixture on almost every restaurant menu. rs. 25 (usd 0.4) per piece
7.5/1

KUNZHI KOZHI NIRACHATHU
This roasted spring chicken, stuffed with mutta (egg) and masala made of loads of onions, thick coconut milk and cashew paste, makes for a rich bite, one that’s worthy of being served as a traditional first breakfast to a groom after the wedding. rs. 235 (usd 3.3)
10/10

ELANEER CHICKEN
Thickened with tender coconut and garnished with slivers of fresh coconut, this chicken stew is an ode to the versatility of the fruit of the cocos nucifera. There’s a gentle sweetness to this velvety stew and the gentle warmth of ginger and green chilli. 
rs. 294 (usd 4.1)
9/10

MAPRANAM FISH CURRY
A vivacious curry that reflects typical toddy shop fare. The sour notes of the kokum dominate this ayakora or kingfish curry, followed by the heat of red chillies and the pungency of garlic. Savour this with boiled rice.
rs. 500 (usd 6.9) price varies, depending on the size of fish.
9/10 

CHATTI CHORU
Basically, the equivalent of a sadhya served in a claypot (chatti). Work the choru (rice) with the smorgasbord of dishes in the chatti, be it the dry shrimp chutney, the fried fish, aviyal or the fish thiyal, or coriander fish curry. rs. 80 (usd 1.1)
8/10

PAROTTA KIZHI
A weighty dish of three parottas drenched in coconut milk and wrapped around chicken masala and steamed in a banana leaf bundle. A sumptuous one-dish meal. 
rs. 190 (usd 2.6)
8/10

AVIL MILK (CALICUT FALOODA)
AC’s spin on the Malabar staple, avil milk, is loaded with calories but sinfully delicious!
rs. 80 (usd 1.1)
9/10

CHILLI HORLICKS
Sweet Horlicks spiked with chilli flakes and pepper! Perfect for a cold night, if ever Kozhikode has one. 
rs. 55 (usd 0.8)
7/10

Title: HYDERABADI Chef Cooks MOST FAMOUS Hyderabad Vegetarian Dish | NIZAMI HANDI Recipe| Novotel Hyderabad
Description:
#HyderabadiCuisine #HyderabadFoodTrail #GourmetOnTheRoad

How to make Nizami Handi, Vegetarian Nizami Handi Recipe. Easy Vegetarian Recipes.

Although Hyderabadi cuisine is known for its richly flavoured meat dishes and kebabs, there are also delicious vegetarian recipes like this Nizami Handi, a mixed vegetable curry enriched with cashew paste, cream and gently flavoured with whole spices. The velvety gravy, and medley of veggies makes this dish a stiff competition to every non-vegetarian counterpart.

Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna joins Chef Iqbal at Novotel Hyderabad Convention Center as he makes this rich, aromatic, and gently spiced vegetarian dish made in the ‘Handi’, a traditional wide, heavy-bottomed pot used in Indian cooking. Hence the name of this royal dish!

Indicative recipe for Nizami Handi:
Serves Four
Ingredients: 
1 pinch of ajwain or caraway seeds
1 pinch of jeera or cumin seeds
3 onions, chopped
3 tomatoes, chopped 
1 tablespoon ginger garlic paste 
1 small bunch of spinach, chopped 
1 carrot, diced 
1 small cauliflower, cut into florets
6 pieces of baby corn, diced
50g of green peas 
200g of cashewnut paste 
200g of tomato puree
50ml cooking oil 
1 teaspoon chilli powder 
1 tsp jeera or cumin powder
1 tsp garam masala 
1 large pinch of kasuri methi powder (dry fenugreek leaves)
50ml cooking cream 
A small handful of chopped coriander to garnish. 

Method:
1. Heat the oil in a pan.
2. Add ajwain and whole jeera and stir till fragrant.
3. Add onions and cook until they are translucent.
4. Add the tomatoes.
5. Once the tomatoes are cooked through and the raw flavour is gone, add ginger garlic paste.
6. Once the paste has cooked through, add chilli powder and cumin powder and saute. 
7. Add the cashew nut gravy as well as the tomato puree. 
8. Add your vegetables along with enough water to submerge them. 
9. Let the mixture cook over medium flame until vegetables are tender (10-15 minutes) 
10. Finish with fresh cream, kasuri methi powder,and fresh coriander leaves 
11. Serve hot with roti or rice.

Title: Popular MALABAR Snacks At 70-Year-Old BOMBAY HOTEL Calicut | UNAKAYA, ELANCHI, ELADA, BIRYANI CHAI..
Description:
#MalabarSnacks #CalicutFoodTrail #GourmetOnTheRoad 

Best Malabar Snacks. Bombay Hotel Kozhikode. Calicut Bombay Hotel, Kozhikode Street Food, Moplah Snacks At Bombay Hotel Calicut. Elanchi. Unakaya. Mutton Cutlet. Biryani Chai. Chemmeen Cake.

A landmark on Silk Street, Kozhikode, Bombay Hotel has stood the test of time for 70 years and is still going strong, dishing out over 20 varieties of Moplah snacks come tea time every day! 

The spot to savour some Malabari snack classics and this is exactly what Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna does in this episode of Gourmet On The Road. He treats himself to the elanchi (thin crepes stuffed with a mix of bananas, coconut, sugar and raisins), a custardy savoury chemmeen or prawn cake, a biryani chai and much more! 

BIRYANI CHAI
A fancy name for this gimmicky tea poured skilfully into a glass such that the milk and tea liquor hold their own in a dancing swirl! Fancy name aside, and there are no biryani spices in this, the tea makes for a punchy companion to the loaded desserts and savouries here. 
rs. 22 (usd 0.3) 
8/10

CHICKEN PUFF
Not so pleasing to the eye, the chicken puff is flavourful. A deep-fried maida puff stuffed with chicken, onions green chillies and turmeric, this snack makes for a delicious accompaniment to some hot chai!
rs. 22 (usd 0.3) 
8/10

MUTTON CUTLET
A filling cutlet of meat and onions flavoured with ginger. I was expecting a more meaty flavour, but you taste mostly the onions and some flour that’s gone in as a binder in this snack. 
rs. 20 (usd 0.3) 
7/10

ERACHI PATHIRI
This stuffed pathiri is generous on the onions, but a trifle sparing on the meat, which in itself has a bit of a bite. Prepare to spend some time chewing on this.
rs. 35 (usd 0.5) 
7/10

CHEMEEN CAKE
a cake with a difference, this savoury steamed cake comprises of spiced shrimp sandwiched between layers of the soft cake. On the palate, I detect a hint of sweetness which contrasts with the mildly spicy shrimp. You can definitely taste the shrimp flavour in this! 
rs. 28 (usd 0.4) 
8.5/10

ELANCHI
A moist wobbly pancake that’s stuffed with ripe banana, fresh coconut, sugar and nuts. The tart sweetness of the banana combined with the juicy bite of the coconut is endearing, clearly a dessert that’s a must-try here.
rs. 17 (usd 0.2) 
10/10

MUTTAPOLA
They love eggs in desserts at Bombay Hotel, and this egg white and ripe banana steamed cake is a taste to be acquired. 
rs. 19 (usd 0.3) 
7/10

SP UNNAKAYA
A sticky maida fritter with a coconut, banana and egg filling. I was bracing to taste some ‘egginess’, but thankfully you don’t. One tastes the sweet tartness of the banana and the flavour of the coconut. Certainly a snack that grows on you.
rs. 17 (usd 0.2) 
8.5/10

ELADA
A gooey steamed rice cake stuffed with coconut, banana, some lentils and jaggery, best eaten with a spoon. The rice casing is slightly mushy in texture, but the hero of this treat is certainly the banana. 
rs. 20 (usd 0.3) 
7/10

LEMON TEA
the lemon tea helps reset your palate and appetite if you want to dive back into some of the delicacies at bombay hotel. 
rs. 10 (usd 0.1) 
8/10
