Title: MAKING of CHICKEN BIRYANI at KERALA’s Most Popular PARAGON RESTAURANT, Kozhikode | Tasting 11 DISHES
Description:
#MostPopularRestaurantInKerala #ParagonHotelKozhikode #GourmetOnTheRoad

Most Popular Restaurant In Kerala. Paragon Restaurant Kozhikode. Paragon Chicken Biryani recipe, Chicken Dum Biryani, Crab Bhumika, Meen Moilee, Mango Fish Curry, Mutton Varthiyathu.

A Keralan culinary institution that people are familiar with not just in the state but beyond its borders, Paragon Restaurant, is perhaps the oldest and by large the most popular restaurant in the city of Kozhikode. Established in way back in 1939, Paragon has built an empire across the world with restaurants in various parts of Kerala and the Middle East. 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits the iconic restaurant on Kannur Road, where Paragon was born to meet Sumesh, third-generation owner. He then visits the kitchen to watch their revered Paragon Chicken Biriyani being made from scratch. He then sits down to savour some of the most ordered dishes on the menu.

PRAWN DRY FRY
You taste the sweetness of the fresh prawns and the fragrance of the coconut oil in which this crustacean is fried. The prawn is perfectly seasoned and cooked textbook perfect to a yielding crunch and succulent inside.
rs. 315 (usd4.4) 
10/10

PAN FRIED MUSSELS
The mussels are cooked supple in a savoury mix of onions, curry leaves and green chillies. A play of flavours and textures, one tastes the toasty lilt of the curry leaves, the bite of the onions and gentle heat of the pepper.
rs. 331 (usd4.7) 
9/10

PAN FRIED SQUID
The squid, though cooked to a pleasing springy bite is quite neutral in its flavour and needs to be cocooned in the masala for it to make an impression on the palate.
rs. 273 (usd3.8) 
7.5/10

TAMARIND FISH
This Paragon creation teases the senses with its medley of flavours. You taste the sourness that comes from the vinegar, the sweetness of jaggery and the lingering warmth of ginger in the sauce in which the fried kingfish is tossed. 
rs. 336 (usd4.7) 
9/10

CRAB BHUMIKA
I love the size of these juicy sea crabs, they're soft and one can bite into them whole to relish the flavours of the dish. You taste the sweetness of the crab meat, the freshness of the ingredients, coriander, green chillies, ginger, garlic and the sour twang of lime.  
rs. 231 (usd3.2) 
9/10

AVOLI MOILEE
The delicate white pomfret is the perfect accomplice to the mellow, soothing flavours of this creamy coconut stew, punctuated with the notes of kokum, curry leaves and green chilli. Enjoy this with a lacey appam.
rs. 452 (usd6.3) 
9/10

MANGO FISH CURRY
Another popular dish here, the ayakora or kingfish has imbibed the sour notes of the raw mango. The shallots add a robust bite and the heat from slivers of ginger contrasts with the slightly sour notes of this curry.
rs. 273 (usd3.8) 
10/10

MUTTON VARTIYATHU
A mutton preparation that’s rich in flavour and texture. The meat, onions, tomatoes and spices have been slow-cooked for a few hours to come together in a lush gravy. 
rs. 254 (usd3.6) 
9.5/10

CHICKEN BIRIYANI
The biriyani here is plated in a layered mound, milky white grains of the mildly aromatic kaima rice or jeerakasala rice sit at the crest, followed by a layer of masala-stained rice, a savoury ribbon of masala and fried onions separating the two. 
rs. 168 (usd 2.4) 
10/10

Title: Making & Tasting KOZHIKODE'S Famous RAHMATH HOTEL BIRYANI | Mutton, Chicken| ft@VolpeWhereAreYou
Description:
#Rahmath Hotel #Gourmet On The Road #Kozhikode

Kozhikode’s Famous Rahmath Hotel Biryani, Chicken, Mutton and Beef Biryani, Mutton Stew, Surprise Collab with Venezuelan-American blogger, Volpe Where Are You

A much-loved biryani destination in Kozhikode is Rahmath Hotel, famous for its meaty biryani, led by beef and mutton. Although they offer many varieties of biryani including chicken, fish, prawns, mussels and squid, it’s the meat biryanis that draw in serpentine queues of people especially on weekends.

Food Lovers’ editor, Kripal Amanna meets Mohammed Suhail, 2nd generation owner of Rahmath Hotel and explores the making of the biryani before sitting down to a sumptuous biryani meal and a surprise collab with Carlos Volpe, a visiting Venezuelan blogger from Miami who produces insightful destination stories that make for an interesting watch. Do follow his travel vlogs on his channel, Volpe Where Are You https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCcPVzEbEIv1GUl_c4owKuhg


Mutton stew 
An aromatic stew, the meat has soaked up the lush creaminess of the coconut milk and the savouriness of the onions which also lend a gentle bite. the potatoes in the stew also add to the body of this dish. The meat pieces are tender and thoughtfully sized small, make this a dish that’s convenient to share. Enjoy this with soft, puffy, rice pathiris. 
rs. 140 (usd 1.8); pathri rs. 9 (usd 0.1 ) for each
8.5/10

Kallumakaya Fry
Cooked in a thick gravy made of onions, tomatoes, green chillies, the kallumakaya or mussels are cooked to the perfect texture that results in a juicy, yielding bite of this mollusc. This preparation displays a harmonious balance of savoury, sweet, sour, the warmth that comes from slivers of ginger, and is perfect to be mopped up with the rice pathiri.
rs. 155 (usd 2.0) 
10/10

Chicken Biryani
A steaming hot biryani, served with lemon and dates pickle, raita and salad, as typical to the region. The white leghorn chicken is cooked twice, first in the masala and next, as the biryani simmers on dum. The bird is juicy and moist. The flavour of the biryani is quite gentle, if you like it spicy, you can always perk things up with the lemon date and chilli pickle.
rs. 155 (usd 2.0 ) 
8.5/10

Mutton Biryani
This one-dish meal is a happy celebration of flavours. the meat, coated in a robust masala, is cooked to perfect doneness and is a juicy pink inside. the tomatoes lend a gentle acidity, thereby a unique to the biryani. you can never tire of a good biryani and this is definitely one of those.
rs. 230 (usd 2.9) 
10/10

Beef Biryani
A flavourful biryani that jolts your senses awake. you can savour the hearty presence of the meat in the rice. the meat is tender, has a salty savouriness that complements the spices in the masala. you definitely taste the fulsome meat broth in every grain of rice. 
rs. 110 (usd 1.4) 
10/10

Title: Must-Try KALANTHAN'S Sharjah Milkshake, KUMARI Banana Chips, BHASKARETTAN Milk Sarbath | Kozhikode
Description:
#Kalanthans #BhaskarettanMilkShake #KumariBananaChips

Kozhikode Street Food & Treats, Kalanthan’s Milkshakes, Bhaskarettans Milk Sarbath, Kumari Banana 

Given Kozhikode’s hot and humid weather, it comes as no surprise that the people here love their cool, refreshing drinks. And what rules their craving for an icy cold thirst quencher are the thick, satisfying milkshakes at Kalanthan’s and Bhaskarettans satisfying milk sarbath. 

When it comes to a ‘snacky’ bite, the banana chip is what’s on every Kozhikoden’s mind. And the best specimens of these are found at Kumari Banana Chips where these scrumptious treats are made fresh through the day. 

Food Lovers’ editor, Kripal Amanna spends a day savouring these, guided ably by Chef Arun Ramanunni Nair, Regional Executive Chef of Raviz Hotels & Resorts.   

SHARJAH SHAKE 
you don't drink this shake you eat it! it's as thick as that. you taste the flavour of the mildly sweet banana that is integrated into the frozen milk and the subtle undertones of cocoa. Disregard the sugar and this could be an incredibly nutritious milkshake.
rs 40. (usd 0.6) 
8.5/10

STRAWBERRY MILKSHAKE 
tart, sweet and lusciously thick, this strawberry shake is delicious. 
rs 60. (usd 0.8) 
8/10

CUSTARD APPLE MILKSHAKE 
My favourite shake here, you taste the ripe sweetness of the custard apple and its grainy bite. A glass of this would make for a refreshing meal substitute. 
rs 60. (usd 0.8) 
9/10

AVOCADO MILKSHAKE 
the sweet, buttery mouthfeel of the avocado, albeit with a slightly bitter edge, is a tasty way to get your superfood fix for the day. 
rs 60. (usd 0.8) 
8/10

BHASKARETTAN’S MILK SARBATH (MS) 
This popular kozhikoden thirst quencher tastes quite similar to a melted vanilla ice cream laced the earthy tones of the sasparilla root extract. delicious! 
rs 20. (usd 0.3)
8/10

KUMARI BANANA CHIPS 
The banana chips are made fresh. you can watch these seriously addictive chips being made from the raw banana in a matter of minutes, seasoned just right with the perfect crispness and seasoning. 
rs 350. (usd 4.9) per kilo
10/10

Title: Most Popular FISH FRY in Kozhikode| Amma Hotel | Kingfish, Red Snapper,Fish Meals| Calicut Food Tour
Description:
#AmmaHotel #Kozhikode #GourmetOnTheRoad

Most Popular Fish Fry and Fish Meal Restaurant in Kozhikode, Amma Hotel, Ayakora (Kingfish) Fry, Chembali (Red Snapper) Fry, Fish Meal

Come lunchtime and locals in Kozhikode (Calicut) flock to this eatery set in a home in the tiny bylanes of Puthiyara. What draws the crowd here is their Ayakora or Kingfish fry and their satisfying fish meal served on a banana leaf.

Food Lovers’ editor, Kripal Amanna visits this fish fry icon and after a tour of the kitchen where fish are slathered with a secret masala, lashings of coconut oil and fried over a rubber wood fire, sits down for a sumptuous meal.   

AYAKORA (KINGFISH) FRY
a much loved fish in the city, found in almost every eatery. Served here with a thick layer of a spirited masala slathered on a thick slice of kingfish, the bite of the masala has almost tamed the flavour of the fish. Slightly salty and redolent with the aroma of coconut oil, the fish fry masala is also a great accompaniment to be savoured with the rice and lentil curry. 
rs 160. (usd 2.2)
9.5/10

CHEMBALI (RED SNAPPER) FRY
a plump piece of red snapper naped with the Amma Hotel masala. Since this is a meatier fish than the ayakora, the masala doesn’t penetrate all the way in. if you like your fish fry robustly flavoured the ayakora is for you. but if you like it spicy and still want to enjoy the flavour of the fish the red snapper is what you should be trying. 
rs 150. (usd 2.1)
9/10


FISH MEALS
The swollen grains of kuruva rice are the perfect medium to carry the flavours of a tasty vegetable paruppu curry and also tame the aggression of the spices in the fish fry masala. For a mere 50 rupees, this unlimited meal that includes a simple choora (tuna) curry, valakaya (raw banana) upperi and rasam, is a meal that provides nourishment, satisfaction and taste!
rs 50. (usd 0.7)
8.5/10

Title: Authentic, BEST Mappila Meal | ZAIN’S HOTEL| Kozhikode |Cooking CHICKEN BIRYANI… Mutton Stew|Calicut
Description:
#MappilaCuisine #Kozhikode #GourmetOnTheRoad

Authentic Moplah Cuisine in Kozhikode at Zain’s Hotel, Calicut, Mappila Cuisine, Chatti Pathiri, Kallumakaya, Mutton Stew, Chicken Biryani, Ghee Rice, Chicken Masala

Zain’s Hotel Kozhikode stands testament to Mrs Zainabi Noor’s firm resolve to showcase the Mappila cuisine of her family. Kozhikode’s first lady restaurateur, she began her culinary enterprise 29 years ago as a small tea stall dispensing evening snacks. Spurred by the love she received from her customers, Zain’s today stands tall in Calicut as the address for homestyle Malabar cuisine.

Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits this cosy restaurant set in a home and meets the mother-daughter duo of Zainabi Noor and Shireen Mustafa who oversee every detail of the operation. He also looks at the making of their popular chicken biryani, ghee rice and chicken masala in their kitchen ‘manned’ only by lady cooks, before sitting down to a generous lunch.

CHATTI PATHIRI 
A 12-layered baked pancake interspersed with eggs, poppy seeds and raisins, each bite is a delicious crunch followed by luscious overtones of the ghee, caramelised sugar and the textural play of nuts. This is one dessert that’s a must-have here.
rs 25. (usd 0.4)
8.5/10

KALLUMAKAYA NIRACHATHU
Twice cooked, first the mussels are steamed in a rice cake with spices and then fried, the kallumakaya niracathu is a speciality at Zain’s. Peel the shell away to reveal the mussel, the rice cake is a tad crunchy to the bite and yet moist within, the flavour of the masala has seeped into the rice dumpling. 
rs 29. (usd 0.4) per piece
10/10

FISH FRY
Lightly coated with a masala that plays second fiddle to the flavours of the plump ayakora or kingfish, this fry snares the moist flakey-ness of the fish in a light crunch. The turmeric lends it a delightful golden-orange hue. 
rs 200. (usd 2.8) per piece
8.5/10

MUTTON STEW
Rich in coconut milk, this creamy stew carries within itself juicy chunks of meat that is yielding and flavourful. The tingling sensation of green chillies on the palate is balanced by the ripe acidity of the tomatoes. Best savoured with the ghee rice.
rs 250. (usd 3.5) per piece
10/10

GHEE RICE AND CHICKEN MASALA
The rich chicken masala makes for the perfect companion to the aromatic ghee rice. Rounding up the rich tones of the onions, tomatoes and curry leaves is the coconut oil that floats to the top of this dish, absorbing the flavours of the vivacious masala along the way. 
Chicken masala rs 150. (usd 2.1), ghee rice rs 60 (usd 0.8) 
8.5/10

CHICKEN BIRYANI
This isn't a biryani that jostles your tastebuds, it embraces your palate gently with light flavours of the fried onions and spices. The chicken is moist, having absorbed the flavours of the marinade as it cooks slowly over dum for an hour. The biryani exudes a hint of smokiness, and is almost buttery on the palate thanks to the ghee, oil and vanaspati that goes into the cooking of this biryani.
rs 150. (usd 2.1)
9/10

Title: Visiting JAI BHUVANESHWARI Miltry Hotel For A MEATY BREAKFAST | Srirangapatna | MUTTON CHOPS| KHEEMA
Description:
#PopularRestaurantsOnTheBangaloreMysoreHighway #BreakfastInKarnataka #GourmetOnTheRoad

Popular Military Hotels In Karnataka. Jai Bhuvaneshwari Military Hotel, Srirangapatna, Bangalore-Mysore Highway. Non-Vegetarian Breakfast. Mutton Chops. Kheema Unde. Thatte Idli. 
 
If you are setting out on a road trip en route to Mysore, Jai Bhuvaneshwari Miltry Hotel, a seemingly nondescript eatery with a legacy of 40 years int Srirangapatna is one place you should definitely make stop at for a robust, meaty, village-style breakfast meal. Set in an orange coloured home, look out for a signboard screaming the hotel’s name in Kannada and English. The eatery opens for breakfast as early as 7:30 am, dishing out carnivore favourites.

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna stops over for a hearty ‘miltry’ style breakfast tasting three crowd favourites here, the Kheema Unde, Mutton Chops in a masala-rich gravy and Paya Soup savouring these with some steaming hot Thatte Idli. 

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATINGS
THATTE IDLI
on the bangalore-mysore highway, the thatte idli rules and i had to order some to savour with my meaty sides! the idli served steaming hot is super soft. with the mutton chops gravy it just melts in the mouth. no chewing at all, it just disintegrates leaving behind the savouriness of the spices and meaty flavour. . 
rs 30 for two. (usd 0.4)
8/10

MUTTON CHOPS 
this mutton chops is a thick gravy preparation that comes with a generous piece of bannur mutton. the meat is pink encased in a thin sheath of fat and cooked to soft juicy perfection. you taste the robust meaty flavours in the gravy and the green chilli heat that slowly creeps up on you. don't forget to suck on the bone for a generous slurp of the marrow. 
rs 120. (usd 1.7)
9/10

KHEEMA UNDE
as you break into these, you notice only the tender pink of the meat. the mutton in this unde is coarsely ground giving it a delicious texture. this meatball is all about the meat and the warm spices in the gravy.
rs 120. (usd 1.7)
9/10


LEG SOUP
the gelatin in the trotter has rendered well into the nourishing soup, lending it a gamey savouriness that’s offset by the spices in this soup. this dish will definitely warm you up from within!
rs 120. (usd1.7)
8/10

Title: Making & Tasting Of The Famous AMBUR BIRYANI in Ambur | RAHAMANIYA BRIYANI HOTEL | Mutton, Chicken
Description:
#Biryani #Ambur #TamilNadu #Mutton #GourmetOnTheRoad

Rahamaniya Briyani Hotel, Home of the legendary Ambur Briyani, Making of Ambur Mutton Biryani, serving the biryani since 1890 in Ambur, Tamil Nadu

With a culinary legacy that spans 130 years and four generations, Rahamaniya Briyani Hotel is considered to be the home of the Ambur Briyani. Spelt Briyani by the denizens of this bustling town, this dish has spawned many a biryani shop across the region.

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna meets three generations of the Ahmed family and gets exclusive insider access to the kitchens of Rahamania Briyani Hotel to watch the making of an Ambur mutton briyani from scratch.

He also tastes the briyani and a moist Naatu Kozhi briyani in addtion to a couple of meaty sides.


GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATINGS

MUTTON BRIYANI
this biryani is seductively subtle in its aroma. you taste the luscious flavours of the aqhni in every grain of the flavourful jeera samba rice. The juicy meat pieces are small, allowing you to savour its meaty goodness in almost every mouthful of the briyani. If you like your briyani a little spirited and slightly spicy, taste it with the eggplant salan. I personally love this 'briyani' just by itself.
rs 200.
10/10

NAATU KOZHI BRIYANI
prepared in the same fashion as the mutton version, the flavour of the rice is very similar to the mutton briyani sans the flavour of the fat in the latter. The flavourful country chicken has a bit of a bite, typical of its character. If you love your naatu kozhi, you will love this briyani too. 
rs 210.
9/10

CHICKEN LEG PIECE
Marinated deep-fried leg of chicken, fried to the perfect crisp outside yet retains its juicy moistness within. relish it with the toasty, herbaceous flavours of the curry leaves that are fried alongside the chicken.
rs 40. 
8/10

VANJARAM FRY
Encased in a robust masala that’s rich in its fenugreek flavour notes, the seer fish fry is a tasty distraction from the legendary briyani here. The savouriness of the curry leaves and the acidity of the lime definitely perks up the flavours of the fish. 
The skin has been fried to a crisp 
rs 160. 
8/10

Title: Delicious NORTH KARNATAKA Jolada Rotti Meals & Snacks At HOTEL NALAPAKA In Bangalore
Description:
#NorthKaranatakaMeals #RestaurantsInBengaluru #GourmetOnTheRoad

North Karnataka Food, Bangalore. Vegetarian Meals. Hotel Nalapaka Rajajinagar. Jolada Rotti Meals. Davanagere Benne Dosa. Girmit. Mirchi Bajji. Biranji.

An eatery located in the western suburbs of Bengaluru, Hotel Nalapaka’s rustic Karnataka meals are an experience one must definitely devour! Ms Kavitha Lingayya who hails from North Karnataka, set up the restaurant 20 years ago with the motive of sharing her beloved cuisine with the city. She first begun serving food out of a car shed, moving to catering to office-goers and then finally moving to a bigger space, Hotel Nalapaka.

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers Editor, Kripal Amanna visits the eatery after it came much-recommended by viewers, to savours a North Karnataka-style meal for lunch. He meets with Ms Kavitha, visits her kitchen and also takes a look at how their famous jolada rottis are made the traditional way. He then sits down to a meal, and makes a beginning with tasting the popular snacks on offer, namely the Girmit, Mirchi Bajji and Davanagere Benne Dose. He then tastes the Thursday special Biranji meals, served with toasty jowar rotis topped with a big dollop of butter, he wolfs these down with a creamy brinjal curry, lentil preparations and chutneys!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATINGS

GIRMIT
often considered north karnataka’s take on a bhel puri, this snack is nothing like one! the addition of an onion tempering and gram flour to a mixture of turmeric stained puffed rice, raw onions and coriander is what makes the girmit different. make sure to chase a bite down with the fried chilli which perks up the flavours of this dish.
rs 36. (0.50 usd)
8/10

DAVANAGERE BUTTER DOSA
the perfect lacey and crisp texture of this dosa makes you want to dive straight into eating it! served with a lightly tempered potato palya and coconut chutney. the crunch in every bite followed by the lush butter that coats the palate is what makes this a superb dosa! rs 57. (0.80 usd)
8.5/10

MIRCHI BAJJI
love the way they make the chilli bajji here. the lightly spiced batter encases the chilli but not all the way through. you can see the spicy green chilli. you taste the spice of the chilli despite the thick casing. rs 21. (0.30 usd)
8/10

JOLADA ROTTI MEAL WITH BIRANJI 
this jolada rotti meal is wholesome in every sense! the rottis are light, fluffy and have a nutty flavour. when eaten with that lush butter and chutneys (the shenga or peanut chutney was my favourite) they are all the more delicious! the badnekayi is tangy and cream,  while the thick dal is fortified with fresh methi and the madike kalu is cooked to that perfect crunch. rs 192. (2.70 usd)
9/10

BIRANJI RICE
this aromatic rice quite similar in appearance to a pulav is a popular rice dish in the town of ranebennur, north karnataka. it is served only on thursdays as part of the jolada rotti meals at Nalapakka. the spices, cloves, cardamom, are reminiscent of a pulav but the addition of the lightly toasted garlic takes it in a new direction. every grain of rice is also speckled with that special biranji masala. the toasted cashew and butter makes this a rich preparation. 
8.5/10

not the softest idli you will come across, this one borders on being slightly firm. you taste the tart fermented edge of the batter. the idli is best enjoyed with the chutneys. the coriander chutney has a fresh flavour while the mint chutney makes for a zesty bite. my favourite accompaniment is the nourishing sambar fortified with lentils. the texture of the idli makes it perfect to be dunked in the sambar. 
rs 20. (0.30 usd)
7.5/10

GHEE PODI IDLI
this idli is a lot more softer and has a certain springiness to it. Slathered with ghee and doused in a spirited, spicy podi, its texture is a lot more pleasing to the palate. the heat of the podi is tamed when eaten with the creamy lentils in the sambar. this is a delicious idli!
rs 32. (0.45 usd)
9/10

SPECIAL SWEET PONGAL 
this dish is laden with ghee, so much so that it feels like you aren’t just eating the pongal but the ghee too! the dish isn’t cloying sweet, the amount of jaggery used is just right. the addition of toasted cashews gives it a nice bite and also helps cut through that dairy richness of the ghee. 
rs 58. (0.80 usd)
8/10

GHEE MASALA DOSA
the dosa is crisp and translucent. you can hear it go crunch as you break into it. the potato filling is creamy, almost pate-like. a bit excessive on the salt but flavourful nonetheless. the dosa batter in no way interferes with the flavours of this soft mash. the dosa surprisingly manages to retain its crunch despite being dunked into the sambar. it's almost like biting into a puff pastry, that's how delicately crunchy this dosa is!
rs 108. (1.50 usd)
9/10

ONION UTHAPPAM
love the way this uthappam is loaded with onions! the onion has been roasted to a deep brown. you taste the delicious caramelised notes of the almost burnt onion on the top layer followed by the sweet crunch of the lightly sauteed onions below it. the thick uthappam just cradles all these delicious textures and flavours! the chutney provides for a nice break, if it gets too onion-y.
rs 89. (1.25 usd)
8.5/10

JIGARTHANDA
literally translating to ‘cool the heart’ the jigarthanda is a very popular cooler on the menu here. the orange flavoured ice cream made in-house has a texture that’s somewhere in between a gelato and sorbet. the jelly has almond essence in it, you can also taste the dairy from the basundi. if you like something cooling and refreshing, settle for this drink.
rs 70. (1 usd)
7/10

FILTER COFFEE
my choice of drink after a south indian breakfast! the sweet bitterness of the filter coffee is the right way to end a slightly over indulgent breakfast here at murugan idli shop. 
rs 32. (0.45 usd)
8/10

Title: Tasting BHEEMA'S Most Popular ANDHRA VEG MEALS | MUTTON BIRYANI | Chilli Chicken | KITCHEN TOUR!
Description:
#AndhraCuisine #RestaurantsInBangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad

Best Restaurant For An Andhra Meal In Bangalore. Andhra Restaurants In Bangalore. Andhra Style Biryani. Andhra Meals.

A popular name when it comes to Andhra cuisine in Bengaluru is Bheema's, an iconic restaurant located in the heart of CBD, at Church Street. Although the street has witnessed a resurgence over the years, this over 20-year-old establishment has stood still, turning into a favourite spot for lunch, when in the area.

The simple yet satisfying vegetarian Andhra meal served on a plantain leaf and the Nellore-style Biryani is what patrons usually flock to the restaurant for, not forgetting their signature side, the Bheema's Chicken!

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers' Editor, Kripal Amanna visits the restaurant after a decade to revive memories of a meal here. He meets with second generation owner, Vijaykumar and explores the kitchen. He discover the evolution in the method of cooking traditional Andhra fare Bheema's has adopted and also visits the restaurants' nursery!

He then sits down to indulge in the vegetarian meals with oodles of ghee and gongura chutney, moving on to taste the Mutton Biryani and some delicious meaty sides. 

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
VEG MEALS 
 a popular lunch choice at bheema’s, the veg meal comprises of a pappu, a vegetable of the day, sambar, rasam, perugu, buttermilk and dessert, usually a payasam. my top picks were the deliciously creamy spinach pappu, the flavourful sambar. the moolangi chutney was not as vibrant or vivacious as the gongura chutney. don’t forget to top your piping hot rice with ghee and the signature podi before you work your way through the dishes!
rs 205. (2.90 usd) 
8.5/10


CHILLI CHICKEN
although this chilli chicken has an incredible amount of chilli seeds, it doesn’t hit you right away when you first taste it. but as you devour the dish, the green chilli spice makes its presence felt on the palate. the chicken is moist and juicy. eat this dish with rice and oodles of ghee to help tame the chilli aggression. 
rs 260. (3.65 usd)
8.5/10


BHEEMA'S CHICKEN
this fried chicken preparation is a bheema’s signature. the chicken is coated and fried in a light batter and tossed in a masala which makes liberal use of green chilli and curry leaves. this fried chicken is cooked perfectly, crunchy and dry outside yet soft and juicy within. the curry leaves lends a toasty, herbaceous note to the dish.  
rs 270. (3.80 usd)
9/10


MUTTON BIRYANI
this biryani is gentle in its aromas, not a biryani you can smell from a mile away. the rice is cooked in the flavourful mutton broth that has given up all its meaty flavour to the supremely flavoursome rice. you can also taste the whole spices like cloves, cinnamon and star anise. the meat is cooked to a juicy, tender pink.
rs 285. (4 usd)
8.5/10


MUTTON PEPPER FRY
the meat is the star in this mutton pepper fry. it is slow cooked and braised for hours resulting in that tender, melt-in-the-mouth texture. the flesh is pink all the way through and the fat too has rendered well. the pepper does not obliterate the flavour of the mutton.  the curry leaves provide a nice respite in between tasting. the flavour of the meat and spices have come together beautifully in this dish! 
rs 340. (4.75 usd)
9/10

Title: Tasting 14 COASTAL DELICACIES At KARAVALLI Bengaluru |LOBSTER, CRAB, PRAWN, OCTOPUS, POMFRET & More!
Description:
#GourmetOnTheRoad #RestaurantsInBangalore #Seafood 

Best Seafood Dishes In Bengaluru, Coastal Restaurant At The Gateway Hotel Bengaluru, Top Rated Seafood Dishes at Karavalli. Aquafest 
 
In nearly three decades of its existence, Karavalli at The Gateway Hotel Bengaluru has distinguished itself as an establishment that serves the country's finest South West Coastal cuisine. This has made the speciality fine dining restaurant an absolute must-visit in the city with patrons highly recommending a meal here.

What patrons also await is a much loved, annual seafood festival that the restaurant has been hosting since its existence. 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits Karavalli to savour all the dishes on offer as part of this very special Aquafest menu. He meets with Executive Chef of The Gateway Hotel, Naren Thimmaiah to understand what makes this festival as popular. He then sits down to enjoy a whopping 14-dish meal.

BABY LOBSTER JIREM MIREM
chunky baby lobster meat marinated and cooked in a cumin (jirem) and fresh pepper (mirem) masala. you taste the byadgi chilli as opposed to the pepper in this warming masala. 
rs 1850. (25.80 usd)
9/10

GOAN OCTOPUS CHILLI FRY
i love the sweetness of the tomato in this preparation, the octopus however, has a bite that borders on being chewy. the flavours of this dish is one you would enjoy in a shack somewhere on the beaches of goa.
rs 1200. (16.75 usd)
7/10

KOONDAL PORICHATU
the batter-fried masala coated squid is cooked to springy perfection and the masala has penetrated all the way through. the fresh acidity of a squeeze of lime cradles that gentle spicing of the squid. this is the sort of dish that would make for a very happy bar snack.
rs 1200. (16.75 usd)
9/10

WHOLE SILVER POMFRET RECHEADO
this dish of whole fried silver pomfret is a taste of goa! liberally coated in the sweet, tart and hot goan recheado masala, both inside and out, you taste notes of the goan palm vinegar and the aggressive punch of chilli as you devour the dish. 
rs 1200. (16.75 usd)
8.5/10

TIGER PRAWN MALABAR STYLE
a signature dish at karavalli i keep returning for! these meaty tiger prawns are first fried to perfect scrumptiousness and then tossed in a vivacious masala of shallots, tomatoes and pepper.
rs 1800. (25.10 usd)
10/10
SEA CRAB GHEE ROAST
these meaty sea crabs, cooked in a ghee roast masala are divine! i love the mild sweetness of that crab meat (tastes just like the ocean!). the butteriness of that well rounded masala embraces the natural flavours of the crab.
rs 1450. (20.20 usd)
9/10
KOLI BARTHAD
a speciality here on the menu, this is a dish that hails from coorg. pieces of chicken are pan fried in a bunch of spices and kachampuli. the deeply roasted spices that have melded together as one.
rs 995. (13.88 usd)
8.5/10

MUTTON STEW
this is a textbook syrian christian stew with the mellow coconut base carrying just the subtlest hint of spicing. the meat is soft, you taste its nourishment in every strand. 
rs 1150. (16.05 usd)
10/10

PRAWN CALDEEN 
this goan-style curry is a pleasant melange of flavours. you taste the freshness of the coriander, the spice of the green chilli, raspy bite of the ginger and the creaminess of the coconut in the sauce. the prawns are juicy having absorbed all that goodness. 
rs 1450. (20.20 usd)
9/10
ALAPPUZHA MEEN CURRY
the deep, spice notes in this alleppey fish curry catches hold of your palate from the first bite. the seer, a meaty fish, is the right medium to convey and carry these bold flavours of coconut, ginger and raw mango. 
rs 1150. (16.05 usd)
9.5/10


DODOL
my favourite way to end a meal at karavalli is with the dodol, a goan dessert made with rice flour that has been well roasted with palm jaggery and loads of butter! it is rich and dark, each bite is lush, buttery yet dry. 
rs 475. (6.60 usd)
9/10
KASHI HALWA
the ghee glistens in this translucent kashi halwa. the ash gourd is flavoured with saffron, you also sense a hint of acidity in this dessert. 
rs 475. (6.60 usd)
7/10

Title: MARATHA STYLE NON VEGETARIAN Food | MARATA DARSHAN | Naati Koli Saaru, Mutton Chops & More!
Description:
#MilitaryHotelsInBangalore #NonVegetarianFood #GourmetOnTheRoad

Maratha Cuisine In Bengaluru. Military Style Food In Bangalore. Ragi Mudde and Mutton Chops Thali.

Gorge on mouthwatering military-style food, especially robust mutton dishes at Marata Darshan in Bengaluru. Established by Shantharaj Lad back in 1989, this humble eatery is known for its wholesome military style meals served for breakfast and lunch. Presently run by the father, mother and son trio, the reason behind the restaurant’s success are traditional recipes by the mother, Hemavathi Bai.

Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna meets the family in this episode of Gourmet On The Road. He then sit downs for a meal tasting the Mutton Chops Thali served with either rice and the restaurant’s signature Ragi Mudde, Koli Saaru, Mutton Kheema Curry and a bowl of Soppina Saaru. Title: Affordable, Fresh & Delicious SEAFOOD At MANGALORE PEARL | PRAWN GHEE ROAST | KANE FRY | CRAB & More
Description:
#Seafood #SeafoodRestaurantsInBangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad

Best Seafood Restaurants In Bangalore. Mangalorean Food In Bangalore. Authentic Mangalorean Food In Bengaluru. 

A favourite for Mangalorean fare in Bengaluru, Mangalore Pearl is always bustling with patrons who visit this spot for their taste of coastal Karnataka, more specifically the Mangalorean Catholic-style of seafood food.

Set up by Steven Pinto who left behind a lucrative career in the IT sector to pursue his dream of sharing the food he grew up with, this 15-year old restaurant rose to fame thanks to its spiced filled seafood dishes and Mangalorean classics.

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits the Ulsoor outlet and meets with the brother duo that run the restaurant. He discusses the procurement of fresh seafood, the variety of curries on offer and also witnesses the making of two most popular fries, the Bangude and the Kane Fry.

He then sits down to a feast, tasting a bevy of coastal dishes, from a Pomfret Curry, Crab Masala, Khoobey Mootlien, Chicken Roce Curry and more!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATINGS

RAGI MANNI 
the manni has a lush, creamy texture that takes over your palate! you taste the caramel notes of the jaggery. this mangalorean dessert resembles the Italian panacotta minus the cream. definitely a delicious way to end your meal here.
rs 60 (0.90 usd)
8/10

KHUBEY MOOTLIEN
this dish deserves attention when being savoured, especially when picking on the tiny yet sweet and mildly briny clam flesh. the rice dumpling has a sticky, slightly slimy texture that goes very well with the thick, velvety coconut based gravy. the flavour of the clams in this dish is reminiscent of the ocean.
rs 170 (2.40 usd)
8.5/10

CRAB MASALA
tossed in a semi-dry onion and tomato masala that complements the mildly sweet, flesh of this dotted sea crab don’t forget to suck on the crab meat!
rs 310 (4.30 usd)
8.5/10

POMFRET STEW CURRY
the spicing in this masala is mellow and refreshing and just right, allowing the flavours of the pristine, fresh pomfret to shine. this stew curry goes deliciously well with mangalore rice.
rs 480 (6.70 usd)
9/10

KANE TAWA FRY
this fish is as fresh as it gets! so delicates that the meat just flakes apart effortlessly. the pullimunchi masala gives off a warming note o f the byadgi chilli and also a slight tartness from vinegar. the fish has absorbed the masala, yet retains its unique flavour. be mindful of the tiny pin bones though!
rs 280. (4 usd)
9/10

BANGUDE FRY
the butterflied mackerel allows for the masala to penetrate the deep flavours of this fish. notwithstanding this, the mackerel asserts its strong flavour from the word go despite being fried in a spicy masala.
rs 120 (1.70 usd)
9/10

CHICKEN ROCE CURRY
a popular choice of chicken curry at mangalore pearl made with coconut milk, fried onions and gentle spices. best savoured with the soft, spongy sannas that disintegrate as it absorbs this flavourful curry. the chicken though, tastes better when in the company of the creamy curry.
rs 220. (3 usd)
8.5/10

PRAWN GHEE ROAST
soaking in oodles of ghee this is one of the best prawn ghee roasts i’ve tasted! the prawns are plump and fresh, being coated in all that roasted masala that does not overpower its sweet flavour. the neer dosa serves as the perfect combination to this dish. the beautiful balance of spice, toasty flavour notes of coconut oil, rich ghee and divine prawns will keep you coming back for this dish!
rs 295 (4.10 usd)
10/10

FRIED POTRADAY
this dish starts off as a rice cake steamed with spinach, coriander, cumin seeds and red chill that is then sliced, battered in a light spice mix and deep fried. it makes for an appetising start to a meal.
rs 120. (1.70 usd)
7.5/10

SOLKADI
this drink made of coconut milk, kokum juice, ginger, garlic and chilli certainly awakens the senses and the palate. a refresher with a bite.
rs 50 (0.70 usd)
7.5/10

Title: Tasting SOUTH CANARA VEGETARIAN THALI At NEW MODERN HOTEL Bengaluru | Making Of BADAM HALWA |Chiroti
Description:
#VegetarianMeals #RestaurantsInBangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad

Most Popular Vegetarian Restaurants In Bengaluru. Masala Dosa At New Modern Hotel VV Puram Bangalore. South Indian Vegetarian Meals 

Located at VV Puram in South Bengaluru, New Modern Hotel is one of those rare, iconic establishments that has stood the test of time retaining it’s old world charm be it in its space and ambiance or in its recipes and way of cooking, simple honest homestyle fare.

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers Editor, Kripal Amanna, visits the eatery to escape the hustle and bustle of the city meeting with 3 generations of the family that has been running the restaurant for over 60 years. He then gets special access into the kitchen and to a step-by-step making of the most popular sweetmeat on their menu, the Badam Halwa. Following this he tastes the Thatte Idli, a wholesome South Canara-style Thali and the ghee laden Badam Halwa and another favourite dessert in the region called Chiroti Milk.

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATINGS

THATTE IDLI
generously smeared with ghee and served with a side of sambar and chutney, the thatte idli here is soft, almost breaking under its own weight. the chutney is rich in coconut with a mild chilli flavour while the sambar is thick, one in which you taste the hing and jaggery.
rs 30. (0.40 usd)
8/10

VEG MEALS
this vegetarian meal at NMH is a wholesome, south canara-style thali that is sure to remind you of home. this plate comes to you with a poori/ chapathi, vegetable of the day, sambar, saagu, tilisaaru, mosaru, rice, papad, pickle and majjige. a complete meal that’s honestly priced and delicious!
rs 80. (1.15 usd)
8.5/10

CHIROTI MILK
this popular dessert in the region is a puri made of semolina and maida that is crumbled and topped with sugar, badam powder and hot milk. the result is a sort of dessert that can bring a smile to anyone’s face. you taste the rich badam milk and occasionally crunchy bits of the ‘indian’ puff pastry.
rs 42. (0.60 usd)
8.5/10

BADAM HALWA
lusciously velvety, this dessert fill every pore of your palate with joy. served in small portions because it is super rich (1 part badam, 2 parts khova, 3 parts sugar and 6 parts ghee!) you can taste the granular texture of the almond and the fragrant flavour of cardamom.
rs 50. (0.70 usd)
9/10

FILTER COFFEE
Strong, piping hot filter coffee. just the sort you need after a meal here. order this with a side of the badam halwa. 
rs 23. (0.30 usd)
8/10

Title: Exciting Street Food Trail VV Puram PT 2 | AVAREKALU VADA, OBBATTU, Badam Milk, FIRE PAAN & More
Description:
#ThindiBeedi #VegetarianFood #GourmetOnTheRoad
Street Food In Bengaluru. Best Street Food In Bangalore. VV Puram Food Street. Thindi Beedi. Vegetarian Street Food.

In part two, the final part of our street food trail at Thindi Beedi, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna tastes some of the more traditional and popular recommendations at VV Puram. He begins by tasting a super scrumptious Avarekalu Vada served piping hot, followed by a wholesome Avarebele Akki Rotti served with an saaru and crusty, Paddus. He then visits over 45 year old Guru Idlis to try their Mini Idlis. Rounding off the trail on a sweet note, he tastes two types of Holiges, a glass of nutritious Badam Milk and the super popular Gulcan Ice Cream. To help digest the 21-dishes he savours, he ends with a Fire Paan!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING 

SRI VASAVI VAISISTA THINDI
AVAREKALU VADA 
this vada is every fried food lovers delight! made using a mixture of water hyacinth bean, dill, gram flour and aromats like onion, ginger, garlic, chilli and coriander this is as delicious and nutritious as a vada can get. in short, hot, crunchy and mouthwatering!
Rs 20 for two vadas. (0.30 USD)
9/10

SRI VASAVI MANE THINDI
AVEREBELE AKKI ROTTI 
this dish is a full meal. the akki roti has a crunchy crust and a soft inside. the gravy however, is quite tame. the avarekalu in the rotti makes for a tasty textural relief.
Rs 40. (0.56 USD)
7.5/10

PADDU
an enriched dosa batter that is cooked on a tava speckled with spherical cavities. it has a slight sour twang coupled with the crunch of the onions and freshness of the dill. delicious when eaten with coconut, chana dal and green chilli chutney.
Rs 20. (0.30 USD)
8/10

SRI GURU DEV IDLI MANE
MINI IDLIS
porous, soft fluffy idlis. the chutneys however are a little watery. the green chutney with gram flour is diluted in flavours. the idli though is the hero of this dish! 
Rs 10 for 3. (0.15 USD)
8/10

IDLI MANE
PLAIN OBBATTU 
a flaky, sweet paratha stuffed with lentil, cardamom and jaggery. the liberally slathered buttery ghee and that mild jaggery sweetness make this a delicious holige.
Rs 20 (0.30 USD)
8.5/10

KAI OBBATTU
much more weightier, this version of the obbattu has a rich, sticky, sweet coconut filling that lends a great bite to this obbattu.
Rs 20 (0.30 USD)
8.5/10


MUMBAI BADAM MILK AND LASSI CENTER
BADAM MILK
a rich, thick and nourishing badam milk flavoured with pista, kesar and cardamom. the super thick cream on top tastes almost like khova. one can run a mile after drinking this!
Rs 40. (0.40 USD)
9/10

SHIVANNA GULCAN ICE CREAM CENTER
GULKAND ICE CREAM
a crowd pleaser of a dessert here at vv puram. a mixture of gulkand or rose jam and butter topped butterscotch ice cream and mixture of fruits. the fruit helps cut through the sweetness of the ice cream and jam.
Rs 100. (1.40 USD)
8/10

PAAN POINT
FIRE PAAN
this unique version of the popular digestive, paan left me speechless, quite literally! you can absurdly taste the fire for a fraction of a second, followed by the cool ice and a mish mash of flavours from all the components inside!
Rs 50. (0.70 USA)
7/10

Title: Bengaluru’s Popular VV PURAM FOOD STREET PT 1 | VB BAKERY, Mosaru Kodubale, Bajji Chaats Chai & More
Description:
#ThindiBeedi #VegetarianFood #GourmetOnTheRoad
Street Food In Bengaluru. Best Street Food In Bangalore. VV Puram Food Street. Thindi Beedi. Vegetarian Street Food.
Bangaloreans love eating out and one spot every one frequents is VV Puram for its delicious vegetarian street food that can leave you spoilt for choice!

In part one of this two-part street food trail at Thindi Beedi, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna begins his trail at the legendary VB Bakery to taste three recommended treats, starting with the signature KBC or Khara Butter Bun Congress, a butter jam bun and the honey cake. Following this, he makes a trip to Shree Swamy Bajji Center to taste five scrumptious bajjis! Next on the list is a unique, smokey Tandoori Chai, special chaats from Chandra Chaat Center and highly recommended street snack, the Mosaru Kodubale or the Curd Kodubale.
Stay tuned to the final part of this trail coming up, this one covers some traditional snacks and tiffin and something sweet to seal the deal!
GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATINGS
VB BAKERY
KHARA BUTTER AND CONGRESS KADLEKAI BUN 
the first flavour to hit your palate is the savouriness of the curry leaves. you taste the buttery goodness, followed by the chilli and the crunch of the peanuts! this could very well be the Iyengar version of the peanut butter sandwich!
Rs 26. (0.40 USD)
9/10

BUN BUTTER JAM
This special bun is made with milk powder and has some raisins in it too. slathered with a generous lashing of butter and mixed fruit jam, this dish is a slice of nostalgia packed in a bun! 
Rs 27. (0.40 USD)
8/10

HONEYCAKE
made with pure coorg honey, this honeycake is dense and sticky. the top is light, airy and spongy but the bottom is where the sugary attack of the honey hits you. 
Rs 28. (0.40 USD)
8/10

SHREE SWAMY BAJJI CENTER
OOTY MENASINAKAI BAJJI
the ooty pepper in itself does not have too much heat but that raw chilli powder sprinkled on top certainly has a kick to it. this bajji will be a treat on a rainy day!
Rs 10 for a bajji. (0.15 USD)
8/10

CAPSICUM BAJJI
a whole capsicum fried to scrumptiousness. the capsicum still retains its fresh crunch despite being fried. ticks all the boxes if you are considering a nice evening snack.
Rs 20 for a bajji. (0.30 USD)
8/10

ALU BONDA
delightful fried snack that is super hot and made fresh. an absolute steal for a tasty snack! 
Rs 10 for 3 bondas. (0.15 USD)
8/10

BANANA BAJJI
love how the raw, starchy banana tones down the spice in that chutney and chilli powder sprinkled on top. the bajji is deliciously crisp when eaten seconds after it is fried!
Rs 20 for 2 bajjis. (0.30 USD)
8.5/10

PINEAPPLE BAJJI
a large slice of pineapple battered fried and then sliced and topped with a chutney and a garnish of onions and carrots! a definite first for me. Rs 20 for a bajji. (0.30 USD)
7/10

NAMMA KITCHEN
TANDOORI CHAI
certainly a tasty tea spiced with cinnamon and ginger. what makes this a tandoori chai is that smokey flavour present in every sip! perfect for a nippy evening. 
Rs 20. (0.30 USD)
8/10

CHANDRA CHAAT CENTER AND PAV BHAJI
MASALA PURI
this masala puri isn’t too spicy as one would expect. what you really taste is the fragrant spicing in the masala base and the slight sweet pop of the peas. 
Rs 30. (0.40 USD)
7/10

DAHI PURI
a loaded dahi puri. one bite and the puri just oozes all the delicious dahi with the stuffing of the boiled potatoes. you can also taste the spice of the garam masala. 
Rs 40. (0.56 USD)
9/10

GULAB JAMUN
this gulab jamun made using a special recipe is soft, creamy and perfectly sweet. the richness from the khova makes you want to keep going back for seconds.
Rs 20. (0.30 USD)
8/10

ARYA VYSYA
MOSARU KODUBALE
the mosaru kodubale was a scrumptious discovery. the crunchy exterior gives way to the gooey, porous inside. there’s a hint of chilli and cumin flavour. 
9/10

Title: MUTTON PULAV, PEPPER CHICKEN, KHEEMA UNDE At New Govind Rao Military Hotel| 110-Year Military Hotel!

#NonVegetarian #RestaurantsInBangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad

New Govind Rao Military Hotel, Bangalore serves up popular local style non vegetarian fare, and has amassed a loyal following drawing from its 110 year-old legacy. KHEEMA UNDE

Rs 100.
7/10

 MUTTON LIVER FRY
The liver itself tastes fine, but with topped with that well roasted masala, this dish tastes robust and complete!

Description:
#BakeriesOfHyderabad #HyderabadFoodTrail #GourmetOnTheRoad

Best Bakeries Of Hyderabad. Popular Bakery In Old City Hyderabad. Tasting Muharram Special Hyderabadi Dum Ke Roat.


A huge part of Hyderabad’s dining culture is of course, snacking on popular bakes at some of the city’s most popular bakeries. This tradition of savouring biscuits with Irani Chai or even presenting biscuits as gifts when visiting someone’s home was what brought us to Subhan Bakery located at Old City, Hyderabad to taste some of their very special offerings in this episode of Gourmet On The Road.


Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna, meets with Mr Syed Imran, the owner of Subhan Bakery to taste a Muharram delicacy, the Dum Ke Roat made especially during the holy month of Muharram. He also tastes the Hyderabadi essential, Osmania Biscuits, and a cardamom flavoured Chand or Moon Biscuit.

SPECIAL DUM KA ROAT    
this rich cookie is a muharram specialty at subaan. it is soft and chewy on the inside. you taste the delicious richness of the ghee right away followed by the crunch of nuts. this is one decadent cookie!

Title: Feasting on NIHARI, BHEJA FRY, PAYA MASALA At HOTEL NAYAAB | TRADITIONAL HYDERABADI DELICACIES
Description:
#OldCityHyderabad #HyderabadFoodTrail #GourmetOnTheRoad

Hotel Nayaab Old City Hyderabad, Restaurants Of Old City Hyderabad, Muslim-Style Hyderabadi Cuisine

In this episode of Gourmet On The road we set out in search for some delicious Hyderabadi fare. This culinary conquest led us to the Old City, an area that boasts of some of the most iconic, traditional Hyderabadi eateries. 

Hotel Nayaab, an establishment over three decades old, located right at the entrance of bustling Chatta Bazaar, Nayapul Road, Charminar, is a favourite amongst locals and tourists. Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna catches up with Omer Aziz of Hotel Nayaab to understand the typical Hyderabadi fare served here. He explains how the Nihari, a broth that makes for the Paya Soup is slowly simmered over hours and also steps into the kitchen to discover the making of two extremely popular dishes.

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING

NIHARI  
this is a comforting dish perfect to be enjoyed on a nippy evening! you taste the nourishing goodness of the juices from meat bones and the warm spices. the thin veil of fat on top rounds off all flavours. the deep savouriness of fried onion and the fresh hit of coriander adds another layer to the nihari.
rs 100.
9/10

MALAI PAYA/ PAYA MASALA 
definitely an indulgent take on the austere paya! the gravy is enriched with thick cream. the trotter itself is melt-in-the-mouth. Perhaps not for the purist.
rs 240.
8/10

BHEJA MASALA 
this bheja preparation is as light as air! it melts away leaving behind the delicious, custardy flavour of the brain. the masala is unctuous, smoky yet delicate in flavour.
rs 160.
9/10

BHEJA PEPPER FRY
the gentle heat of the pepper creeps up the back of your throat. the bheja is cooked beautifully and the masala, heavy on pepper and coriander balances against the intense creamy bite of the brain.. 
rs 160.
9/10

MUTTON TALAHUA
the masala is reminiscent of an achari masala with its tart edge. it’s perfect to mop up with a piece of roti. the boneless mutton chunks are well cooked and have absorbed that masala.
rs 220.
8/10

DAL FRY 
this nourishing lentil curry is thick and rich. it is more of a south indian style dal that is slightly tart, tempered with curry leaves and mustard. 
rs 150.
8/10

MUTTON BIRYANI
every grain of rice is separate and has absorbed the flavour of the meat. the meat itself has its flavour and a bit of its bite intact. one can also taste the robustness of the spices that have gone into this biryani. the salan has a mild pickling flavour note that helps break the rich spice notes of the biryani. 
rs 200.
8/10

QUBANI KA MEETHA 
this dessert is a tad syrupy. the malai with its richness helps balance out the overwhelming sweetness. the nuttiness from the apricot kernels pack twice the flavour of almonds and breaks the monotony of flavours. 
rs 100.
8/10

Description:
#LunchOnHighway #Telangana #GourmetOnTheRoad

Popular Restaurants On The Bengaluru - Hyderabad Highway. Restaurants For Lunch On Highways. Food Pyramid 24X7 Restaurant.

Food Pyramid, located on the Bangalore-Hyderabad highway or NH44, is a delightful spot to stop over for a meal. It boasts a large rest area, perfect for kicking back after a long drive and of course, has delicious food options, with a large list of local fare to choose from! 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor Kripal Amanna stops by Kothakota, at Food Pyramid for an Telugu-style lunch. He starts his meal with a fiery Natukodi Pulusu or sour and spicy Chicken curry, served with a wholesome Raagi Sangati. He then moves on to a rustic preparation of Gongura Mutton, and finishes with a Kurnool Kunda Chicken Biryani.

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATINGS
NATUKODI PULUSU WITH RAAGI SANGATI 
the naati chicken is cooked to a tender texture in this hot, spicy, sour curry! you can feel the heat on the palate multiply with each bite!! the soft sangati, perfect to be drenched in this flavourful curry, makes for a wholesome accompaniment. 
rs 335.
9/10

GONGURA MUTTON CURRY
this is a rustic preparation that encapsulates the flavour of the region. the sour spinach or sorrel hits you right away. the meat is cooked nice and soft with generous bits of fat and has absorbed the sour punch of the gongura through and through.
rs 299.
8.5/10

KURNOOL KUNDA CHICKEN BIRYANI
this dish has a very smoky aroma, making it a tad overbearing. the rice is however, cooked beautifully with each grain separate. the chicken is soft and has absorbed all the flavor of the masala. the biryani tastes better with the accompanying salan. 
rs 260.
7/10

Title: NIMRAH CAFÉ | Hyderabad’s Most Popular IRANI CHAI & Osmania Biscuits |CHARMINAR|Making Of Irani Chai
Description:
Nimrah Cafe And Bakery, Popular Bakeries In Hyderabad. Most Famous Bakery In Hyderabad.

Nimrah Cafe and Bakery is a landmark establishment in Hyderabad. Since 1993, Nimrah Café has been serving up delicious biscuits, buns, snacks and of course, great chai!

In this episode, Food Lovers’ Kripal Amanna samples a selection of delicious biscuits studded with a variety of dry fruits and nuts. He starts with the Cherry Coconut Biscuit with it’s delicious coconut notes and the Osmania Biscuit with it’s crumbly salty, sweet flavour. He then moves on to the Star Cashew Biscuit and the Fruit Biscuit. The Bun and Rusk Toast that follow, provide a more wholesome, less indulgent pair of snacks. Lastly he tries the Pista Biscuit and the Coconut Dry Fruit Biscuit, both with the toasty flavours of nuts and dry fruit. Of course, he rounds off this tasting session with a cup of Hyderabad’s signature tea, the Irani Chai! 

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATINGS
CHERRY COCONUT BISCUIT
this cookie has a pleasant gooey inside with a crunchy outside. it prominent notes of delicious toasty coconut.
rs 6/ biscuit.
8/10

OSMANIA BISCUIT
this is a biscuit with a delicate crust. it is soft and crumbly with a salty sweet flavour. perfect to snack on with a cup of chai!
Rs 3/ biscuit.
9/10

STAR CASHEW BISCUIT 
warm and delicious, this cookie is as fresh as it gets! it is slightly chewy and nutty in taste.
rs 6/ biscuit.
8/10

FRUIT BISCUIT
studded with colourful tutti frutti or candied fruit, this biscuit has more of a sugary bite. 
rs 5/ biscuit.
7/10

BUN
this bun has a lovely crust to it which is the sign of a skilled baker! it’s fresh, soft, fluffy and so satisfying!
rs 7/ bun.
8/10

RUSK TOAST
the rusk is studded with tutti frutti and nuts which give it a sweet bite as well as texture. it’s dry and crunchy with a sticky, gooey inside. 
rs 5/ biscuit.
9/10

PISTA BISCUIT
this is one crumbly cookie that just about holds together before disintegrating in your mouth! it’s studded with the pistachio which gives it a signature green tint. 
rs 6/ biscuit.
9/10

COCONUT DRY FRUIT BISCUIT 
these cookies are light, porous, and carry the light toasty notes of coconut. they have a restrained sweetness to them, reason why you'll keep going back for another!
rs 6/ biscuit
9/10

IRANI CHAI
the potent decoction cooked and reduced down for hours makes this chai unlike any other! you first taste the mildly bitter, tannic notes of the brew that catches hold of your palate, followed by the creamy milk. the sugar plays the second fiddle. this tea makes the perfect complement to osmania biscuits.
rs 12.
10/10

Title: Making of Traditional PATTHAR KA GOSHT at Novotel Hyderabad Convention Centre | MUTTON KEBAB RECIPE
Description:
#PattharKaGosht #HyderabadiCuisine #GourmetOnTheRoad

How to make Patthar Ka Gosht. Patthar Ka Gosht recipe. Hyderabadi Patthar Ka Gosht. Mutton Kebab Recipe

Like many Hyderabadi dishes, Patthar Ka Gosht is a recipe that has royal origins. It is said to have been invented, when the royal chef of the Nizam, forgot his equipment while accompanying the Nizam on official matters. He therefore, improvised and used a marble slab to cook his kebabs. and thus, the Patthar Ka Gosht was born! 

Food Lovers’ Editor Kripal Amanna joins Chef Mohammed Iqbal, Sous Chef at the Novotel Hyderabad Convention Center, as he shows us what goes into the making of this iconic dish cooked over a hot granite slab! 

Here is an indicative recipe if you would like to try to recreate this dish at home. 

Patthar Ka Gosht Recipe 
(serves 4)

Ingredients:
500g mutton (boneless chunks flattened into 1cm thick slices)
1 tbsp ginger garlic paste
1 tsp raw papaya puree
2 tbsp lemon juice
1 tbsp deggi mirch (chilli powder)
1 tsp mustard oil 
1tsp garam masala powder
1 heaped tbsp rose petal powder
1 tbsp potli ka masala
1 tbsp pathar ka phool (stone flower) powder
½ tsp turmeric powder
1tsp cumin powder
1tsp coriander powder
Salt to taste
Refined oil as needed.
Ghee to finish

Method:
1.Mix the mutton slices with all the ingredients, except the refined oil and ghee.
3. Massage this masala into the meat and set aside for 45 minutes.
4. In place of the stone, heat a cast iron skillet or a heavy bottomed pan over medium flame.
5. Grease the pan with oil. 
6. Grill the meat until it forms a brown crust on both sides and is cooked through.
7. A few minutes before taking the meat off the pan, pour ghee over the top and allow to cook.
8. Serve hot.

Description:
#BiryaniLovers #HyderabadFoodTrail #GourmetOnTheRoad 

Andhra,Telangana, Rayalseema food at Ulavacharu, Hyderabad. Pulao and biryanis in Hyderabad. Pulao restaurants in Hyderabad. Raju Gari Pulao, Rayala Vari Kodi Pulao.

This hugely popular establishment in Hyderabad is famous for its unique takes on traditional recipes. Their specialties are their biryanis or rather, their pulaos, of which they make 18 varieties! And each of them has its own unique flavour and character.
Food Lovers' Editor, Kripal Amanna joins Ravitej Ravuri of StreetByte on an epic pulao tasting session. He tastes a couple of unconventional starters namely, the Bamboo Chicken, an appetiser of chicken cooked in a bamboo stalk in a tandoor, and the Bangla Kodi. From their wide menu of pulaos, he tries the unique Raju Gari Pulao, a vegetarian Guthivankaya Pulao with eggplant, as well as the Rayala Vary Kodi Pulao with gongura leaves. He rounds off the meal with an indulgent rose milk and a sweet pudding called Junnu made from colostrum. 

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING 

BAMBOO CHICKEN
this chicken is cooked in a fresh, tangy herb marinade and steamed in a bamboo shell. the masala has penetrated all the way into the chicken. the meat is juicy but a wee bit powdery in its texture. 
rs. 445
8/10

BANGLA KODI 
an interesting appetiser of chicken encased in a thick slice of potato that is marinated in a red spice paste and deep fried. almost resembles a mini taco! the slightly underdone potato adds a textural crunch.
rs. 399
8.5/10

RAJU GARI KODI PULAO 
this is unlike any biryani/ pulao i have ever tasted! the consistency is that of a khichdi or rice and gravy mixed together. the pulao is flavoured with pepper, whole spices and green chilli takes some getting used to, the chicken is here just to support the flavourful rice.
rs 335
9/10

GUTHIVANKAYA PULAO
a refreshing take on a vegetarian pulao or biryani. this masaledar pulao has an eggplant gravy ladled on the rice. the eggplant adds a meaty bite to the dish.
rs 285
8/10

RAYALA VARI KODI PULAO
cooked with a masala made of sorrel leaves/ sour spinach or gongura as it is popularly known in the region, this pulao is unique in its flavours. you taste the sour notes in the rich masala and chicken.
rs 345
8.5/10

RAJAHMUNDRY ROSE MILK
thick, rich milk infused with a sweet rose syrup. difficult to down an entire glass!
rs 125
8/10

JUNNU
this milk pudding is rich and creamy. visualise lightly sweetened khova in a custard form. 
rs 95
8/10

For a taste of Karnataka or for local non-vegetarian meals visit Naati Sogadu, Sahakar Nagar, Bengaluru. Non-Vegetarian Restaurants In Bangalore.

Heroing flavours of the land, this desi hotel, Naati Sogaadu serves homestyle fare and is especially known for its non-vegetarian offerings.

Title: Visiting 75-Year Old G PULLA REDDY SWEETS Kurnool|MOST POPULAR SWEET SHOP Andhra Pradesh & Telangana
Description:
#IndianSweets #HyderabadFoodTrail #GourmetOnTheRoad

G Pulla Reddy Pure Ghee Sweets Top Sweet Shop In Hyderabad and all of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. Famous Indian Sweets.

If you’re looking for great sweets in Andhra Pradesh, look no further than G Pulla Reddy Sweet Shops. The company now has a presence all over Andhra Pradesh and Telengana. Established in 1948, the original owner set up shop in Kurnool. He insisted on making sweets of the highest quality which meant using pure ghee!

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits the original establishment set up by G Pulla Reddy himself. Here he samples a smattering of their most popular offerings including, a delicious Khova Puri, the ghee laden Mysore Pak and Badusha, as well as the paper thin, melt-in-your-mouth Sugar Pootharekulu. 

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATINGS
KHOVA PURI
this puri is flaky with layers of dough stuffed with creamy khova or cooked milk solids. the buttery goodness of the ghee makes you want to keep going back for a bite.
rs 580/ kilo
 8.5/10

BADUSHA
a crusty maida cookie. the texture is crumbly on the outside and gooey inside. you can taste the doughy goodness in every mouthful.
rs 540/ kilo
8/10

SPECIAL MYSORE PAK 
this version of the mysore pak is unbelievably soft! just melts on the palate leaving the delicious aftertaste of ghee!
rs 580/ kilo
8/10

MYSORE PAK
the older, original version. harder in texture and lighter in colour. It has a crumbly bite. this mysore pak lingers on the bite. 
rs 580/ kilo
7/10

SONA PATTI 
also called the gatti mithai, this one’s an interesting indian sweetmeat made of germinated wheat sprout flour, sugar and ghee. Has the texture of a hard candy and a mellow toffee-like sweetness. What you really taste is the ghee.
rs 620/ kilo
7.5/10

there’s nothing quite like this sweet creation that resembles and feels exactly like paper! These thin sheets are made of rice flour and ghee is stuffed with sugar. it disappears the minute it hits your palate!
Rs 30/ piece
 9/10

this version of the paper sweet is lined with bits of jaggery. its taste has much more of an earthy sweetness. a delightful find at g pullareddy!

10/10

KHOVA
can taste light, toasty caramelised notes in the milk of the khova or reduced milk solids. a simply yet soul satisfying dessert.
rs 540/ kilo
9/10

KAJU BARFI
Looks similar to a kaju katli but much thicker. You taste the richness of kaju and the subtle hint of cardamom and other sweet spices. garnished with the signature varak or silver leaf.
rs 1200/ kilo
8.5/10

Title: BEST Andhra Breakfast |Chutneys Hyderabad|LONGEST 70MM DOSA|Babai Idli| CHIRANJEEVI DOSA| 6 CHUTNEYS
Description:
#HyderabadFoodTour #BreakfastInHyderabad #GourmetOnTheRoad

Most Popular South Indian Vegetarian Restaurant In Hyderabad, Chutneys. South Indian Breakfast spread in Hyderabad.

This restaurant in Hyderabad is abuzz with patrons who flock here to savour some delicious South Indian breakfast, especially their bounty of different ‘chutneys’ as the restaurant's name suggests. 

In this special collab episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna meets with Ravitej Ravuri of Streetbyte to discover a great breakfast! He tastes the blockbuster of a 70mm dosa, some incredibly soft Babai Idli, a spongy Chiranjeevi steamed dosa, their delicious chutneys and more.

Streetbyte Channel link - https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCqA2ZPcBYbWqmKU3iFX2KwA

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING

70MM DOSA 
This 70mm dosa is 4 feet long, thick in its texture with a slightly tart edge. Tasting this dosa with the six different chutneys, from the spicy and sweet ginger and jaggery, grainy lentil chutney to the sweet kobari chutney is a treat to the senses!
8/10

CHUTNEYS
each of these chutneys holds it own in its flavours. the kobari lausu is simple, you taste the coconut and a light sweetness. the coconut and peanut chutney has an endearing spicy edge while the putnalu chutney has that wholesome grainy texture from the lentils. The tomato and corn chutney dabbles in fusion! Another favourite here is the tangy, sweet and spicy allam bellam or ginger and jaggery chutney.
10/10

BABAI IDLI 
these steaming hot idlis topped with a dollop of butter are super soft! the white butter melts into the idli making it all the more crumbly! the chutneys give every bite a different dimension of flavour. 
10/10

GUNTUR IDLI 
smeared with a mixture of the guntur chilli podi mixed with ghee, this is a spicy idli! The chutneys help mellow the spice in the podi.  the Andhra style sambar is lusciously thick and great accompaniment.
8/10

CHIRANJEEVI DOSA
This thick dosa is steamed and uses absolutely no oil! This is a spongy dosa with a crunchy crust. It is served with a cheruku panakam or sugarcane syrup that is intensely sweet, perfect to be lapped up with this thick dosa.
9/10

MLA PESARATTU
A green gram pancake stuffed with upma. A unique dish.  you taste the crunch of the onion, cashew and the spice from the green chilli. grainy crunch of the pesarattu and the soft upma give this dish a contrast in its textures.
8.5/10

MANGO UTHAPPAM
A raw mango paste mixed with red chilli powder is smeared on top of this thick uthappam. you taste the tanginess that kicks in at the end of each bite. 
8/10

For the best Andhra / Telugu Food in Hyderabad visit The Spicy Venue at Jubilee Hills. Best Restaurants In Hyderabad. Most popular Andhra Vegetarian Thali.

The Spicy Venue, Hyderabad is a restaurant that comes highly recommended for its traditional fare from states of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. The signature Vegetarian Thali featuring some of the most loved Andhra dishes such as Ulavacharu, Pesara Pulusu and Pappu Chaaru is sure to give one the taste of food served in an Andhra home.

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna tastes this extensive thali together with some of the must try, traditional non-vegetarian preparations. He also meets owner, Mr Sampath who began the establishment nearly two decades ago and makes a quick kitchen tour to watch another popular dish, the MLA Potlam Biryani, a dish that Mr Sampath says draws inspiration from from the Japanese omurice and local MLA pesarattu. This one is a delicious fresh water shrimp  and mutton mince biryani in a spicy omelette blanket!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
MLA POTLAM BIRYANI
a unique surf and turf style biryani. the signature of this dish is the thin, veil-like omelette in which the fresh water shrimp and mutton mince biryani is wrapped!  the rice has a mellow spicing. the shrimp has a mild saline flavour yet is deliciously sweet.
rs 375.
9/10

VEGETARIAN THALI

Most Popular Biryani Restaurants In Namma Bengaluru. Best Restaurants For Spicy Andhra Biryani In Bangalore.

Nagarjuna, an establishment that was set up in the early 1980s serves two Andhra-style, dum biryanis, a Mutton and a Chicken while Meghana Foods, a relatively new eatery serves an array of biryani to choose from, the most popular of which is a spicy, Chicken Boneless Biryani.

#Breakfast #MysoreFoodTrail #GourmetOnTheRoad

Visit Gayathri Tiffin Room or popularly called GTR in Mysore for a variety of dosas or tiffin time snacks like idli ! Breakfast or Tiffin Spots In Mysuru.

Gayathri Tiffin Room, widely known as GTR in the city of Mysuru, is a destination loved for its tiffin items, especially a variety of dosas! This over half a century old establishment serves up tongue-tickling dosa, the favourite being the Gayatri Masala Dosa here, not the typical Mysore Masala with red chutney, but a thick roast with a soft underbelly. 

Customers who patronise this restaurant have grown in number over the years and often frequent the place for breakfast or tea-time tiffin.

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits the eatery for tiffin in the evening and savours three dosas, the GTR Masala Dose of course, along with an unusual Green Dosa and an Open Butter Masala Dose. He also tastes one of the best Kesari Baths he has ever eaten!

Description:
#Kodava #MysoreFoodTrail #GourmetOnTheRoad
Authentic Kodava Food In Mysore Only At Simply Kodavas!

Finding authentic Kodava food outside Coorg can be quite the task but for the citizens of Mysuru however, Simply Kodavas is the place to go! This family-run restaurant features traditional Kodava art and serves up classic Kodava dishes.

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor Kripal Amanna pays a visit to this restaurant and chats with the owner and his son about this distinct cuisine. He samples the quintessential Kodava Pandi Curry a flavourful Pork Chilli, both finished with kachampuli. He also tastes a robust chicken curry and couple of unconventional dishes namely, the Pork Biryani and Pork Kebab. He savours all of this with some traditional Kodava rice-based staples like Kadamputtu, Noolputtu and Paaputtu.

Pandi curry
you can taste roasted spices, fresh coriander, the tartness of the kachampuli and a peppery heat. A finger-lickingly good pork dish!

the fat in this is spicy and flavourful! pork melts in your mouth and the delicious fat coats your palate. You have the deep brown roasted spices, a slight tartness from the kachampuli or coorgi vinegar, and the spice of the green chilli that lingers on the palate. a satisfying preparation!
9/10

Title: Tasting A Vegetarian MYSORE THALI & Non-Vegetarian KARNATAKA THALI At La Uppu | Grand Mercure Mysore
Description:
#LocalFlavours #MysoreFoodTrail #GourmetOnTheRoad

Must-visit restaurant for the best, traditional vegetarian and non-vegetarian thalis in Mysore! Restaurants To Lunch At In Mysore.

Karnataka has some delicious fare on offer and these iconic dishes can be savoured as a whole in its Thalis. To experience these traditional flavours Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits La Uppu, the all-day dining restaurant at Grand Mercure Mysore for not just one, but two thalis for lunch.

He interacts with local chef, Vijay in the kitchen understanding what goes into some of the dishes on the thali. At the table he begins lunch with the Mysuru Thali, a vegetarian thali featuring dishes such as Bisi Bele Bath, Mysore Bonda, Chitranna, Thilisaaru, Mysore Pak and Godhi Halwa. He then tastes the non-vegetarian Karnataka Thali that comes with a Donne Biryani, Gorikayi Kara and Koli Saaru among other dishes.

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATINGS
Mysore Thali
MYSORE BONDA 
mildly seasoned bonda. dunk it into the thili saaru to perk up its flavours

THILI SAARU
there’s a puckering tartness in this rasam, gentle spice and slight, soothing sweetness in its flavours. 

BALEKAI FRY
raw banana fry with a nice masala coating. no-fuss, tasty, fried goodness.

BELE TAWE
Thick, creamy lentil preparation with chilli, mustard and curry leaves. the kind that would perhaps be served in a typical Mysuru kitchen.

GORIKAYI PALYA
Lightly tempered, this cluster bean preparation is delicious, savour it with the akki rotti.

BADNEKAYI GOJJU
loaded with onions, the flavours of the masala make this brinjal dish shine!

CHITRANA
a satisfying rice preparation, flavoured with tumeric, onions and lemon juice.

BISI BELE BATH
a tasty bisi bele bath! the rice is fortified with lentils and a gentle warmth from the red chilli. the ghee on top makes this dish all the more irresistible!

KOSAMBARI
the kosambari is quite generous in its use of grated coconut. perfect palate refresher in between tasting all the dishes on the thali.

MOSARANNA
the cool yoghurt and mild tempering makes the mosaranna the best way to end an all vegetarian meal.

MYSORE PAK
all the ghee makes this mysore pak melt in the mouth!

GODHI PAYASAM
the best part to this wheat payasam is that it isn’t very sweet. it’s a light dish for a dessert, not leaving you feeling too heavy!

The Mysore Thali is priced at Rs 999 +taxes per person.
9/10

Karnataka Thali

GORIKAYI PALYA
this version of the palya or veggie preparation is spicy and uses a mint, green coriander and chilli paste!

KOLI SAARU
a rich, thick gravy that is flavoured with methi or fenugreek. there’s also some chilli and whole spices that have been ground and added to the masala.

MUTTON DONNE BIRYANI
the rice in this biryani is very mellow in its flavours. you taste the signature donne masala or spicing but this isn’t overly powerful. the meat is soft and tender, cooked really well!

The Karnataka Thali is priced at Rs 999 +taxes per person.
8.5/10

Title: Popular Breakfasts Bengaluru Mysuru Highway|Bidadi THATTE IDLI|Shivalli KADUBU|Maddur Tiffany's VADA
Description:
#Breakfast #HighwayEateries #GourmetOnTheRoad

The best breakfast spots on the Bengaluru-Mysuru Highway: Bidadi Thatte Idli, MTR Shivalli Restaurant, Maddur Tiffany’s.

The Bengaluru Mysuru Highway is a busy one! And thanks to all that footfall, there’s definitely some great eateries that have popped up along the way. If you’re setting out early in the morning, these three eateries make for the ideal breakfast spots. 

Food Lovers’ Editor Kripal Amanna makes his first stop at Shri Renukambha Bidadi Thatte Idli, a small joint just off the highway in a town called Bidadi. The next stop on the highway is Shivalli, to sample their Rice Kadubu, a steamed rice-based dumpling served with chutney and sambar. The third and last stop is Maddur Tiffany’s. This famous eatery is popular for having invented the Maddur Vada, a delicious crispy, savoury, snack made with semolina, and flavoured with curry leaves, cashews and ghee!

9/10

7.5/10

UDDINA VADA
crispy and very lightly seasoned. 
7/10

Plate of Idli Vada

Maddur Tiffanys

Title: Malgudi Coffee Shop Mysore | CAFE WITH A CAUSE | Mysore Filter Coffee| Lemon Drizzle| Chocolate Cake
Description:
#CoffeeShop #Dessert #GourmetOnTheRoad

Looking for a scenic cafe in Mysuru? The Malgudi Coffee Shop located at Green Hotel (formerly the Chittaranjan Princess Palace) is the place to visit!

This cafe set in a covered courtyard, surrounded by nature and natural interiors is the perfect spot to unwind with a cup of coffee and some scrumptious cakes or sandwiches.

The unique aspect of this culinary enterprise is that it seeks to employ and empower women who come from less privileged backgrounds, offering them a means of livelihood. All treats on the cafe’s menu is all made by the staff who run the show here! Their delicious coffee is also sourced from local farmers, supporting fair trade in the area. 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna, visits the coffee shop, interacts with a member of the staff and orders himself some of the must-tries on the menu. He tastes a highly recommended Lemon Drizzle Cake, Walnut and Date Cake, and gooey Chocolate Cake together with a cup of strong Mysore Filter Coffee.

LEMON DRIZZLE CAKE 
buttery with the citrusy edge of the lemon. slightly crumbly texture. an old fashioned cake that's comforting and delicately flavoured.
7.5/10

this cake slices clean and holds together. one can taste the full-on nutty flavours of the walnut and the natural sugars of the date.
7.5/10

7.5/10

this coffee has a strong, heady aroma and some terrific body! you get the fullness of the coffee in the first sip. it works well when relished with sweet cakes. 
8/10

Title: Local-Style Non-Vegetarian Meals At TEGU MESS In Mysuru | IDLI | PEPPER CHICKEN | MUTTON CURRY
Description:
#BestRestaurantsInMysore #NonVegetarian #GourmetOnTheRoad
When in Mysore, head to Tegu Mess for local-style non-vegetarian fare! This hole-in-the-wall eatery began as an establishment to cater to the needs of students in the area nearly 50 years ago! 

Known especially for its wholesome, hearty, meat dishes, each item on offer has its own unique masala ground in-house by the family. Open through the day for breakfast, lunch and dinner, the fare here is sure to remind one of home.

Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits this humble eatery and meets second generation owner, Mr. Tegoji Rao and his son Shyam. He takes a look at the open kitchen, right next to the dining area and samples the Idlis with Gravy which is offered during breakfast hours. He also tries a nourishing Paya soup, a flavourful Pepper Chicken, a gently spiced Mutton Curry and much more as part of his lunch meal.

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
IDLI WITH GRAVY
Steaming hot and fluffy idlis. can be savoured with a chicken gravy or a robust mutton gravy that packs heaps of flavour. 
8/10
Rs 30

PAYA
Has a nourishing, delicate flavour with a hint of pepper and fresh herby zing of coriander. the gelatinous trotter just melts in your mouth! 
8.5/10
Rs. 130

MUTTON CHOPS
A light, delicate stew cooked with mild spices allowing the meat flavour to be most dominant. The mutton is soft and peels effortlessly off the bone!
9/10
Rs. 130.

PEPPER CHICKEN
This is a delicious gravy. notes of pepper and fenugreek give it a deep flavour. the chicken is lushly flavoured with that masala, and is tender and juicy in every bite.
9/10 
Rs. 130.

GHEE RICE
A staple here made with long grain rice. it’s aromatic on its own but can also be paired with the delicious meaty sides!
7.5/10
Rs. 60.

CHILLI CHICKEN
Loaded with tomatoes and coriander this gravy has a gentle, roasted red chilli heat. it is very different from the green chilli heat that one is used to. the curry also has a certain smokiness to it. 
7/10
Rs. 130.

MUTTON LIVER
Made in green masala made that is loaded with fresh coriander. works well with the earthy, meaty, irony notes of the liver. the liver has a slight bite but yields quickly.  
9/10
Rs. 130.

MUTTON CURRY
A superb curry! The mellow spicing allows the meat to shine. all the flavour of the meat is in the gravy. the sort of dish your grandmother would cook for you.
9/10
Rs. 140.
