Title: Tasting 28 dishes! KERALA SADHYA at Vembanad, Bangalore|Vegetarian Malayalee Food|4 TYPES OF PAYASAM
Description:
#Onam #VegetarianFood #GourmetOnTheRoad

The Kerala sadhya meal is an essential part of Malayalee cuisine. Traditionally served at festive occasions like Onam, Vishu, weddings and the likes, the sadhya on average consists of 25-28 dishes! 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor Kripal Amanna, samples the sadhya at Vembanad, the Keralan Hotel at The Paul. He savours this lavish meal of 28 dishes, each with its own unique character and flavour. The meal celebrates the use of vegetables, fruits, various lentils, spices, yogurt and of course coconut in various forms! He wraps up the meal with 4 varieties of payasams, a traditional dessert from Kerala. 

GOURMET ON THE ROAD
NEI PARIPPU
very mildly flavoured. this lentil dish is meant to be eaten at the beginning of a sadhya.

SAMBAR 
slightly tangy with the nourishing feel of the vegetables. quite a satisfying sambar! 

INJI PULI
the sour hit of the tamarind and warm heat of the ginger in this pickle awakens your palate!

ULLI THEEYAL
the delicious savouriness from the onions plays off the sweetness from the jaggery. 

KOOTU CURRY
there’s the earthy texture of the yam with bite of the bengal gram and the slight crunch of the coconut. these veggies are coated in an aromatic, roasted masala. 

BEANS MEZHUKUPURRATI
this poriyal of sorts has a nice crunch of the beans with the mild sweetness and gentle crunch from the onions. 

OLAN
the coconut milk in this soothes and refreshes your palate. best eaten in between tasting the spicy dishes.

VENDAKYA MORRU CURRY
this yoghurt based gravy has a pleasant crunch from the sauteed okra and the savoury pop of the mustard seeds.

AVIAL
a lovely union of veggies. this avial has the gentle flavour of yoghurt, sweetness of the grated coconut and the crunch of the vegetables. you can taste that drizzle of coconut oil used to finish the dish.

CABBAGE THORAN
this cabbage thoran has a prominent sweetness from the copious amounts of fresh grated coconut. It’s mild tempering allows the cabbage to shine!

KAALAN 
the unctuous ripeness of the banana imparts a surprising sweetness to this dish. delicious!

RASAM
you can taste the tartness of the tamarind and tomato and the gentle heat of the peppercorn at the back of your throat in this rasam.

PACCHA MORRU
this buttermilk is thick unlike regular buttermilk. savour this combination of the buttermilk with the rice with kondattam or yoghurt-soaked, sundried and fried chilli!

PARIPPU PAYASAM 
the sweetness of this lentil payasam pairs well with the fruity flavours of the banana. the pappadam adds weight and body to your bite.

SEMIYA PAYASAM
this semiya payasam has the toasty notes of the fried cashews and the sweet jammy pop of the sauteed raisins.

PAAL ADA
a traditional malayalee dessert made with rice flakes, has a delicious, mild caramel flavour. 

JACKFRUIT PAYASAM
this payasam has the intense, pungent sweet flavour of ripe jackfruit. you also taste the lingering note of ground cumin with each bite.

SADHYA
This vegetarian meal gives one a delicious taste of Kerala, each dish unique and pleasing to the palate. a highly-recommended experience to savour!
10/10
This traditional sadhya is priced at Rs 1350 +taxes per person.

Title: Making Of Artisan INDIAN CHOCOLATES In MYSURU | Tasting NAVILUNA Chocolates | Jamun | Gondhoraj
Description:
#ChocolateMaking #MysoreFoodTrail #GourmetOnTheRoad

Naviluna Artisan Chocolate in Mysuru is all about celebrating Indian chocolate, and artisan or handcrafted Indian chocolate at that!

Using certified single origin Indian cacao beans from the South of India, Naviluna conjures up chocolate bars with unusual, unheard of and unique flavour combinations. In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits the factory where this chocolate is produced in small batches, meeting with Founder & Head Chef, David Belo. He understands what it takes to be bean to bar chocolate makers, giving viewers an in-depth understanding of the chocolate making process. He also tastes some of the more popular flavours of chocolate on offer here!

Visit https://earthloaf.co.in/ for more details on Naviluna Artisan Chocolate.
Tel: 098806 29172
GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATINGS

JUNIPER & CHAMOMILE 
these initially disparate flavours come together with the help of that boldly flavoured unapologetic chocolate. the flavour is led by juniper with subtle notes of chamomile. fig and rose petal added in small amounts impart a hint of sweetness and round off the flavours in this bar. 
Rs. 330/ 60g bar
8.5/10

AMERICAN BARREL AGED 
this chocolate has a long and warm finish, a character that comes owing to the fermentation of the cocoa in a whiskey barrel.
Rs. 330/ 60g bar
8.5/10

GONDORAJ LEBU 
the dehydrated flecks of gondhoraj rind emit a fragrant tartness as you bite into this chocolate. a refreshing fragrance that you actually taste! A unique chocolate flavour.
Rs. 330/ 60g bar
10/10

JAMUN & ROSEMARY
a monsoon special, this chocolate bar is studded with jamun and a sprig of rosemary. the jamun feels jammy on the palate, and balances out against the dominant flavour tone of the rosemary.
Rs. 330/ 60g bar
9/10

Title: Melt-In-The-Mouth Mylari Dosa | Hotel Original VINAYAKA MYLARI Mysuru | Exclusive Kitchen Tour
Description:
#Dose #MysoreFoodTrail #GourmetOnTheRoad
Some say it is a sin to visit Mysuru and skip out on eating the famous Mylari Dosa. But what is it about this dish that demands such reverence? Food Lovers pays a visit to Hotel Original Vinayaka Mylari to find out! 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor Kripal Amanna gets a close look at the making of these soft, melt-in-the-mouth dosas and discovers that they are cooked on a massive iron tawa over a searing hot wood fire! He samples the Idlis here (One of the three items in total on the menu here) and of course, the famous Mylari Masala Dosa. He also ends his meal with a sticky, jammy Kashi Halwa. 

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
Idli 
These woodfire steamed idlis are soft, fluffy, aromatic and slightly tart. saagu is robustly flavoured,  with a coriander accent. the vegetables still have their crunch intact.
9/10
Rs. 30 

Masala dosa  
This dosa is unbelievably soft and fragile. Holds together just enough to contain the vegetable saagu. After the initial crunch, the dosa dissolves in the mouth! The chutney adds a touch of freshness and spice. 
10/10
Rs. 40 

Kashi Halwa 
it's not overly sweet and is cooked down just right to a jammy consistency with an endearing stickiness
8/10
Rs. 25 

Address Tag- Hotel Original Vinayaka Mylari, Shop No, 79, Nazarbad Main Rd, Doora, Mysuru, Karnataka 570010

Title: PAN ASIAN Lunch At BIG WONG XL | Chinese Dim Sum | Japanese Sushi | Cambodian Lamb Curry | Stir Fry
Description:
#AsianCuisine #LunchInBangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad
Big Wong XL, a Pan Asian restaurant serving up interesting dimsum and sushi, is just a stone’s throw away from the Food Lovers office, in 5th Block Koramangala. 

Exuding a laid back vibe, with contemporary decor together with oriental accents, this eatery features an extensive Asian menu, from Indonesian curries to Japanese Ramen Bowls and everything in between!

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor Kripal Ammana decides to check out Big Wong XL for some steamed dim sums, a variety of sushi as well as a couple of appetisers and a recommended Cambodian Style Lamb Curry. 

He books his table using Eatigo, a restaurant booking app now available in Bengaluru, through which he avails of 50% discount on the bill.  To avail of attractive discounts at interesting restaurants, download the Eatigo app at https://bit.ly/343K1XZ

Note: Although we have been invited by Eatigo to use the app in this episode, this is an independent review of the restaurant and its food as in all Gourmet On The Road episodes.

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATINGS
RAINBOW SUSHI 
This one’s a colourful seafood sushi but the pieces topped with tuna is where the flavour is!
7/10
Rs. 650 for 8 pieces.

CALIFORNIA ROLL
the california roll is stuffed with crab stick, avocado, and mayo. the salty pop of the tobiko (flying fish roe) livens up its flavours. eat it with a touch of wasabi!
8/10
Rs. 650 for 8 pieces.

VEG TEMPURA 
well wrapped sushi with the right balance of rice and filling. there’s a pleasing crunch to the fried vegetable tempura. 
7/10
Rs. 550 for 8 pieces.

ASPARAGUS TEMPURA
with this sushi, you first experience the crunch of the asparagus followed by the creaminess of the mayo. the perfectly seasoned, vinegar rice is the ideal vehicle to carry these flavours and textures. 
8/10
Rs. 550 for 8 pieces.

CRYSTAL VEG DIMSUM
a delightful ‘money bag’ dumpling stuffed with peppers and mushrooms. the skin is translucent and skillfully made. definitely a dimsum to try if you like robust, spicy flavours.
7.5/10
Rs 220 for 4 pieces.

VEG THAI HERBS DIMSUM
plump, flavourful dumpling. the filling is soft barring the bite of the water chestnuts. The accompanying chilli peanut sauce provides a spicy kick!
8/10
Rs. 220 for 4 pieces.

CHICKEN CHILLI FLAKE DIMSUM
served with a cheung fun sauce, this dumpling has a filling that does not hold back in its flavours but the wrapper however, feels a little doughy on the palate.
6/10
Rs 290 for 4 pieces.

PAK CHOY WRAPPED CHICKEN DUMPLING
well marinated chicken with great umami flavours and the herbaceous crunch of the wrapper/ pak choy. a delicious dumpling!
8.5/10
Rs 290 for 4 pieces.

THAI STYLE COCONUT PRAWN
there’s an appetising sweetness from the coconut milk, and a mellow warmth from the spicy chilli glaze. the curry leaves give it an unexpected herbaceous lift. The prawns are cooked perfectly and embrace the unctuous thickness of the sauce!
9/10
380 small/ 650 sharing.

CAMBODIAN STYLE LAMB CURRY WITH JASMINE STICKY RICE 
this delicious curry is fortified with coconut and shrimp paste. the lamb is tender, flavoured with the aromats in the curry.
9/10
Rs 500.

CRISPY SPINACH AND CORN 
the veggies are dusted in cornstarch and flash fried to help retain their crunch. the spinach is left whole as opposed to being shredded, this allows you to still taste its flavour. a simple yet tasty appetiser.
7/10
Rs 220.

ADDRESS Big Wong XL; KHB Colony, 5th Block, Koramangala, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560 095

Title: MYSURU’S favourite Andhra-Style BIRYANI At HOTEL RRR | Chilli Chicken |Mutton Pepper Fry | Biryani
Description:
#Biryani #MysoreFoodTrail #GourmetOnTheRoad
This biryani establishment has been in existence for 40 odd years and the citizens of Mysuru swear by their biryani! 

Hotel RRR serves up classic Andhra-style fare with a menu that is limited to about 15 items only! They are most popularly known for their biryani and Andhra style starters that do not skimp on flavour. From robust whole spiced preparations, to an almost numbing but heavenly chilli kick to moist, aromatic biryani, this restaurant serves it all!

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor Kripal Amanna starts his meal here with the Chilli Chicken and Mutton Pepper Fry. He also savours both the Chicken and Mutton Biryani here.

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
Chilli chicken
The chicken is tender and juicy, having soaked up that fiery chilli gravy. A squeeze of lemon helps tone down the spice slightly. 
8.5/10
Rs. 181.

Mutton pepper fry
This masala is well-roasted, with toasty notes of onion and pepper. The meat has its bite intact. there’s bits of organ meat, and the kidney especially has a nice, briny, meaty flavour that goes well with the masala. 
9/10 
Rs. 190.

Chicken biryani 
Fragrant biryani studded with flecks of tomato and chilli slices. every grain of the basmati rice has soaked in the spice and flavour of the chicken. the slightly tart gravy on the side helps transform the flavours of this mellow biryani.
8.5/10 
Rs. 176.

Mutton biryani
Has similar spicing to the chicken biryani but feels a little more moist thanks to the juices of  the mutton! every bite is flavourful. You can taste the flavour of the tender meat and the fat that has rendered into the rice. 
9.5/10
Rs. 195.

Title: MYSORE PAK TRAIL IN MYSURU | Guru Sweet Mart | Shree Mahalakshmi Sweets | 5 Varieties Of Mysore Pak
Description:
#IndianSweets #Desserts #GourmetOnTheRoad
No visit to Mysore is complete without tasting the city’s most popular sweetmeat, the Mysore Pak! This concoction, born in the royal palaces of Mysore, takes only 4 ingredients to make, namely, gram flour, sugar, turmeric, and plenty of ghee! 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor Kripal Amanna samples various versions of the Mysore Pak across the city. The first Mysore Pak he samples is at Guru Sweet Mart. This sweet shop is run by the fifth generation of the family descended from Kakkasura Madappa, the chef at the royal palace, widely regarded as the inventor of the Mysore Pak. He then moves on to Shree Mahalakshmi Sweets, a sweet shop that specializes in varieties of Mysore Pak. Here he samples the Milk Mysore Pak, the Badam (Almond) Mysore Pak and the Kaju (Cashew) Mysore Pak. 

GURU SWEETS 
Vanaspati Mysore pak
made with vanaspati or vegetable oil. It has a hard, crumbly texture.
7/10
Rs 280/ kg

Special Mysore pak
made with pure ghee. Has a luscious, dissolve-in-the-mouth texture. You can feel the rich ghee coat your palate!
10/10
Rs. 400/ kg

SHREE MAHALAKSHMI SWEETS

Ghee mysore pak
It’s soft to the touch. Beautiful, luscious melt in the mouth quality! 
9/10
Rs. 483/ kg 

Milk mysore pak
Texture-wise, very similar to the ghee mysore pak. You have the flavour of khova or milk solids running through every bite.
8/10
Rs. 504/Kilo 

Badam mysore pak
You definitely taste the almond. Almost feels like a drier badam halwa. You have the grainy bite from the almonds, but this still is a buttery, luscious mysore pak!
10/10
Rs. 670/Kilo 

Kaju mysore pak
you can taste the slight nuttiness of cashew and slight graininess in texture. This mysore pak has more of a bite. 
9/10
Rs. 650/Kilo 

Vanaspati mysore pak
This mysore pak is hard and crumbly. it doesn't have the richness of the ghee but it certainly has the flavour of the besan and sugar. 
7/10
Rs. 294/Kilo

Description:
#HomeDining #Communal #GourmetOnTheRoad
Bengaluru Oota Company is a unique dining experience run by two lady entrepreneurs Divya Prabhakar and Vishal Shetty. Divya is a Gowda, and Vishal is from the Bunt community of Mangalore. They bring together their respective cuisines in a marriage of flavours, represented in their customizable tasting menus. 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, we learn how the two women started this enterprise. Food Lovers’ Editor Kripal Amanna sits down to sample their menu for the day which includes a Kane Rava Fry, Pelata Gatti (steamed jackfruit dumplings) with Kori Ajadina, a Bannur Mamsa Pulav. He rounds off the meal in true South Indian fashion with curd rice, rasam and a badam halwa. 

KOSAMBARI 
This cucumber based traditional salad has just the right amount of tempering to give it that savoury lift. A great start to a meal here. 
7/10

GARLIC SANDIGE 
scrumptious crunch with a strong garlick-y flavour.

9/10

9/10

PELATA GATTI 
similar in texture to an idli but with the mellow sweetness that emanates from flecks of ripe jackfruit. A happy discovery! 
9/10

7/10

cool and refreshing with the sweet pop of the pomegranate seeds. lightly tempered with that roasted curry leaf flavor. the pineapple in the mensakai made for sweet and sour  combination with the curd rice.

8/10

8.5/10

8/10

Title: BEST BREAKFAST In Malleshwaram AT VEENA STORES | SOFT FLUFFY IDLI | Chow Chow Bath | Sweet Pongal
Description:
#Idli #Breakfast #GourmetOnTheRoad

This tiny shop in Malleshwaram is popular for their fluffy idlis and crunchy vadas. Originally a condiment store in 1977, Veena stores has amassed a loyal customer base over three decades of service. 

Food Lovers’ Editor Kripal Amanna finds people of all ages, crowding around the tiny store to savour a delicious breakfast from Veena Stores. He samples some of the more popular items on the menu such as the Idli Vada, the Chow Chow Bath and a unique Sweet Pongal. 

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
IDLI 
the idlis have an inviting fragrance. soft but with just enough texture. the chutney packs a punch with coriander, chilli, and curry leaves. exactly what you need with the soft idlis.  
9/10
Rs 45

VADA
vada is crisp, and crunchy, with a porous inside. very mildly seasoned with tiny flecks of coconut. definitely needs the chutney for that flavour boost.
8/10

KHARA BATH 
soft, creamy, and flavourful, even without the onions and garlic. this khara bath packs all the flavour of the tomatoes, curry leaves, and chillies. its taste lingers on your palate. 
8.5/10

KESARI BATH
the kesari bath itself is not too sweet. the plump raisin gives it a burst of sweetness and the cashews add a toasty flavour!
8/10
Rs 35 for a plate of chow chow bath

KHARA PONGAL
A mellow-tasting pongal made of rice, with a certain creaminess that comes perhaps from lentils. Elevated with the sharp bite of whole peppercorns and the lingering flavour of cumin, and comes alive on the palate with the chutney.
7/10

JAGGERY PONGAL
The jaggery is very evident in this short-grained rice dish, as is the edible camphor that immediately engulfs the palate. A touch of lentils add some creamy graininess to the bite.
8.5/10
Rs 35 for a plate of sweet and khara pongal

COFFEE
the coffee is nice, thick, and strong. always the best end to a tiffin breakfast. 
Rs. 
7/10

Title: Tasting & Watching The Making Of Mysuru’s Most Popular MUTTON PULAV At Hotel Hanumanthu|Mysore Trail
Description:
#MysoreFoodTrail #MuttonPulav #GourmetOnTheRoad

The iconic Hanumanthu Hotel in Mysuru is famous for its mutton pulav that patrons relish from six am each morning! The restaurant, now looked after by the second and third generation, father-son duo of, Parmesh and Vishal  cooks all its food on firewood.

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, we get an exclusive insider access to the kitchens of this legendary establishment and a closer look at how their iconic mutton pulav is made. Aside from the generous serving of Mutton Pulav, Food Lovers’ Editor Kripal Amanna samples some Mutton Boti and a plate of Mutton Chops. 

This restaurant, part of Mysore’s rich culinary history is a must-visit!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
mutton pulav
the gentle masala spicing makes this a fragrant biryani. perfectly cooked pieces of mutton, with a slight bite. the organ meat and fat of the mutton intensifies the meaty flavours in this biryani. 
10/10
Rs. 200 for full plate. Rs 160 for half a plate.

mutton chops 
The gravy carries the flavour of the fat and meat. This style of preparation highlights the flavour of the meat through and through.
9/10
Rs.120 

mutton boti 
The liver, intestines and other offal meat are flavourful, perfectly tender, not leathery or rubbery! The gravy is thick, almost creamy and unctuous. The masala does not overpower the meat. 
8/10
Rs 120

Title: Tasting Muslim-Style MUTTON DUM BIRYANI At Chichaba’s Taj | Bheja Fry | Barrah Chops | Seekh Kebab
Description:
An offshoot of the restaurant that claims to be the only muslim restaurant in Bangalore to have been around since 1935, Chichaba’s Taj is known for serving up traditional muslim-style dum biriyani, kebabs and curries

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor Kripal Ammana visits the crowd favourite at Frazer Town, Bengaluru, to quell his craving for a good biryani, and along the way also tastes some of the highly recommended kebabs, paya and a peppery bheja fry!

MUTTON SEEKH KEBAB
The right proportion of meat to fat makes this succulent kebab. The outer crust envelopes a flavourful mutton mince. This kebab is gentle on the palate despite its fiery red colour. Best eaten hot off the sigri! 
Rs.160.
7/10

MUTTON BHEJA FRY
Its unctuous bite coats the palate with its creamy texture. It's delicious, loaded with pepper, roasted onions, curry leaves and chillies. A must-try here!
Rs. 190
9/10

MUTTON PAYA
The paya or trotter is gelatinous and has rendered well into the aromatic broth. There’s a mild meatiness to this nourishing soup. 
Rs. 200
8/10

BARRAH CHOPS 
The meat peels away from the bone but still retains its bite. This dish is cooked to textbook perfection with the right amount of spicing that allows the meat to shine through. 
Rs. 400.
9/10

MUTTON DUM BIRYANI
This biriyani is aromatic with smoky undertones and gently spiced with whole spices. The mutton pieces are moist and succulent with pockets of fat! The baigan ka salan accompaniment with its tartness, adds a whole new dimension, making the biryani livelier!
Rs. 260.
8.5/10

CHICKEN DUM BIRYANI
Each grain of rice is separate. It has a nice gentle aroma, a hint of tartness from the tomatoes and fresh flavour of herbs. A mild biriyani that will not necessarily jolt your taste buds.
Rs. 200
7/10

CHICHABAS FRIED CHICKEN
Well marinated, succulent fried chicken that’s not dry. It has a pleasant spice marinade and gentle flavouring.
Rs. 200
7.5/10

Address - Chichabas Taj; 50, Madhavaraya Mudaliar Road, Frazer Town, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560005;

Title: SOFTEST Idlis & Crunchiest VADAS at Brahmins’ Coffee Bar|Delicious South Indian Breakfast |Bengaluru
Description:
#Breakfast #Bangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad
This pillar in Bengaluru’s culinary landscape has always had only four items on its menu! For 5 decades Brahmin’s Coffee Bar has been serving up the softest idlis, crunchy vadas, and of course, thick, strong coffee in South Bengaluru. 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor Kripal Amanna visits the famous coffee bar and samples everything on the menu (all four items that is), which consists of the Idli Vada, the Khara Bath, and the Kesari Bath. He also learns of the history of the restaurant and why this family-run establishment has resolved to stick to the only four-item menu they started with.

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING

Idli and Vada 
the idli is unbelievably soft, pillowy, and melts in your mouth with no effort! this is in contrast to the perfect crunch of the vada. the inside of the vada is almost cloud-like, speckled with slivers of coconut, chillies, and curry leaves. the chutney is spicy and slightly minty. this dish, especially the idli is a revelation! 
Rs 16 for one Idli
Rs 23 for one Vada
10/10

Khara Bath
this khara bath literally melts in your mouth. it is studded with all sorts of aromatics, fried lentils, carrots and peas for texture. with the signature chutney, this dish is divine! 
Rs 23.1
8/10

Kesari Bath
laden with ghee, raisins, nuts, and pineapple, and studded with cloves. the sweetness balanced with the acidity of the pineapple and the toasty notes of the cashew. the astringent flavours of the clove readies your palate for the next bite. every bite is delightful.
Rs 23.
9/10

Coffee
a coffee, nice, strong and thick coffee. just the way it should be!
Rs 16.
9/10

Title: KOSHY’S BEST BREAKFAST DISHES| Mutton Cutlet, Appam Stew, English Brekkie... Exclusive KITCHEN TOUR
Description:
#Breakfast #KoshysParadeCafe #GourmetOnTheRoad
 Koshy’s is a landmark establishment in Bengaluru that has been around since the 1950s, popular for its old world charm and vintage decor. 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor Kripal Amanna, meets with Mr. Prem Koshy, third generation co-owner of this hallowed institution to discover its surprisingly humble origins. 

He savours some of the most popular breakfast items from their expansive menu, including the homemade Baked Beans on Toast, Chicken Liver on Toast, Club Sandwich and of course, their signature Appam and Stew, a signature dish that is served only on Sunday!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD 
BAKED BEANS ON TOAST
Homemade baked beans generously slathered on a thick slice of Koshy’s bread. The earthy flavours of the beans and tangy tomato, make this dish very comforting. 
Rs. 130
7/10

MUSHROOM ON TOAST
A simple dish of mushrooms sauteed in some garlic and pepper, spread over buttered toast. The earthiness of the mushroom is what’s most prominent. A must-try for every mushroom lover. 
Rs. 130
7.5/10

TOMATO AND CHEESE ON TOAST
A beautiful plate popping with contrasting colours of the sauteed tomatoes and cheese. The jammy flavours of the tomatoes are delicious. Acidic and salty flavours, yum!
Rs. 130
8/10

VEGETABLE CUTLET
An old fashioned cutlet made from a medley of veggies, peas, carrots and potatoes, spiced delicately. There's a certain creaminess that takes over the palate.
Rs. 75
8/10

MUTTON CUTLET 
Hot and crisp to the touch. A delicious mutton cutlet, the crumbed exterior holds that flavourful spiced mutton mince. A textbook mutton cutlet. Old fashioned, like mum would make.
Rs.100
9/10
 
MR. K's BIG EASY ENGLISH BREAKFAST
Tawa toast slathered with baked beans and fried sunny side up eggs, crisp, plump pork sausage, fries, and a side of veggies. Layered with flavours, this is definitely an indulgent breakfast. 
Rs. 450 
7.5/10

SPANISH OMELETTE.
This old-fashioned omelette is a big, protein-packed meal in itself, especially with the fries. This is a loaded omelette. It's cheesy; it has the meaty bite of the chicken, a salty hit from the bacon, and a crunch from the peppers.
Rs.300
9/10

MR K'S GINGER FRUIT PUNCH
You can taste an assortment of fruits like papaya, apple, banana, and grape. You get the mellow spike of ginger and its wellness boost. Quite a filling drink. 
Rs. 75
8/10

CHICKEN LIVER TOAST 
A must-try dish for liver lovers! There’s very little that gets in the way of the rich deep flavour of the liver. The peppers pick up the flavour. The thick soft bread has absorbed liver gravy.
Rs.130
9/10

CLUB SANDWICH
Fried egg, slice of ham. roast lamb, chicken, tomatoes, onions, and some lettuce all encased in that soft bread from Koshy's bakery. You get the flavour of the roast meat, the pungent bite of onions. There’s the creaminess of the egg enveloping it. 
Rs. 190
8.5/10


APPAM AND MUTTON STEW 
Traditionally only served on a Sunday. The mellow, creamy coconut milk has a hint of whole spices. The meat has soaked in the flavours of the stew but the flavour of the meat itself shines through. 
Rs.170
10/10

COFFEE
Nice and strong with a robust hit. Just the thing you need to pick you up after a big heavy breakfast here.
Rs. 39
8/10

Title: Mumbai Vada Pav & Maharashtrian Street Food In Namma Bengaluru |Rajvardhan Foods |Dabeli |Misal Pav
Description:
#StreetFood #MumbaiStreetFood #GourmetOnTheRoad

Nothing quite like Maharashtrian street fare and Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna who spent his early in the city of Mumbai absolutely agrees!

In this Gourmet On The Road episode, he visits Rajvardhan Foods, to take a trip back to Mumbai, tasting an authentic Vada Pav, spicy Misal Pav, Poori Bhaji with some lusciously thick shrikhand and some upvaas chi faraal or fasting foods such as Thalipeeth and Sabudana Vada. 

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING

VADA PAV
The pav is perfect in its taste and texture. the plump batata vada, with a thin casing is stuffed with an appetising potato mix. The garlic chutney and customary fried chilli makes every bite an explosion of flavours! 
Rs 35
8.5/10

KUTCHI DABELI 
a riot of flavours and textures. sweet, spicy, tangy potato patty, topped with the crunch of peanuts and fruity pop of the pomegranate seeds. the pav is toasted to perfect scrumptiousness. the fried sev adds another layer of texture. 
Rs 50
7/10

KANDA POHA
maharashtrian breakfast special made with beaten rice. tempered with onions, mustard, chilli, peanuts and topped with generous amounts of sev. a very simple flavoured dish that needs that twist of lemon to amp up flavours. the thick, slightly sweet yoghurt with the poha is delicious! 
Rs 65
7/10

SHRIKHAND POORI BHAJI 
fluffy pooris but the bhaji is a little low on flavour. best way to savour this is with the lusciously thick, sweet, cardamom flavoured shrikhand.
Rs 115
7/10

KOLHAPURI MISAL PAV
spicy rassa cooked with moth beans and topped with crunchy sev and mixture. a hearty dish to be enjoyed with the pav. the lemon helps tone down the heat. 
Rs 90
7.5/10

SABUDANA KHICHDI
a wholesome dish prepared with minimal fuss. Simply seasoned with flecks of chilli and ajwain seeds.
Rs 90
8/10

SABUDANA VADA
crunchy outside and soft inside. generous flecks of green chilli. minimally seasoned. enjoy this with mint chutney.
Rs 55
8.5/10

ONION THALIPEETH
the almost burnt onions gives this filling pancakes a strong onion-y flavour and bite. 
Rs 90
7/10

UPVAAS THAALIPEETH
made with tapioca flour and rajgira this is a high on nutrition pancake. it’s slightly dry. the butter and the sweet and bitter lemon pickle helps add flavour to this fasting snack.
Rs 95
6.5/10

CHAAS/ MASALA BUTTERMILK
just the drink you need to help you settle your stomach after eating all the spicy street fare served here!
Rs 25
6/10

the quintessential triangular MTR masala dose served with a tuppa da batlu. Perfectly roasted crust that glistens, stuffed tempered mashed potatoes with a side of thick, spicy chutney.
this dosa is a ritual for many here and when you taste it you certainly understand why!

this dose has a spicy green chutney smeared inside for that flavour burst in every bite. a simple dose done well.

Title: BIG FAT MEDDITERANEAN Lunch At Fava Bistro | Salads | Mezze | Burgers |Peri Peri Chicken |Bangalore
Description:
#Lunch #Mezze #GourmetOnTheRoad
Fava Bistro, a laidback Mediterranean restaurant in the suburb of Koramangla is Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna’s go-to spot for lunch, on the rare work day that he is not shooting or producing a Gourmet On The Road segment. 

Unfortunately, however, Fava Bistro is set to soon close doors. In this episode, he shares a final lunch at the bistro, tasting dishes he would typically order including a selection of mezzes, a filling wrap, a faultless burger, and a fruity salad!

He also briefly touches upon the challenges involved in running a restaurant.

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
Organic chickpea hummus
Spiced with paprika, light and creamy. the tahini or sesame paste balances the prominent chickpea flavour. the pita with hummus makes for a great bite. 
Rs 200
8/10

Multigrain fava bistro hamburger with grilled bacon 
A loaded burger that you should dig into when you're really hungry.  multigrain bun, juicy patty, bacon, gherkins, coleslaw, caramelized onions and salty cheddar make this a super delicious burger! can't fault this one!
Rs 395
10/10

Mango caesar salad 
Dressed just enough enough to moisten the salad and your palate. the mango, the Mallika mango in this case  is nice and sweet. eating this salad will not leave you feeling guilty!
Rs 295
8/10

Lamb kebab and avocado wrap

Title: The Perfect South Indian Breakfast At VIDYARTHI BHAVAN | Bengaluru’s Iconic MASALA DOSA & TIFFIN
Description:
#Breakfast #RestaurantsInBangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad

Bringing its patrons exceptional benne masala dosa, soaked in ghee, heavenly kesari bhath and filter coffee since 1943, Vidyarthi Bhavan is a landmark in Bangalore that is simple yet inviting. 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits this highly endorsed eatery. He converses with third generation owner Arun Adiga, understanding what keeps patrons coming back. He also relishes a full breakfast of all the items on the menu, tasting from the iconic dosas to poori saagu and more!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
Idli Vada
A delightful plate of pillowy soft idlis and traditional uddina vada bathed in a tasty, hot sambar. The chutney, although a little runny, is enhanced with a punch of spice and a delicious tempering. 
Rs 14 for one Idli and Rs 26 for vada.
8/10

Poori Saagu
This poori saagu is a humble yet delicious dish at VB. A medley of beans, carrots, brinjal, and sweet pumpkin all harmoniously brought together. The pooris are light and fluffy as you would expect. The chutney adds a flavorful punch. 
Rs 36.
8/10

Khara bath
Spicy and savoury, this semolina concoction with veggies like carrots, onions and the simple tempering has a pleasing texture. A dish that needs no accompaniment.
Rs 26.
8/10

Kesari Bath
This bath is laden with copious amounts of ghee, and tiny morsels of pineapple to give it that sweet, tart flavor. The intense flavour of clove cuts through the richness, making this an irresistible bite. 
Rs 26.
8/10

Saagu masala dosa
This dosa is roasted perfectly with a crackly exterior and a soft interior. That slight tartness of the batter is present in every bite. The delicious saagu is a wholesome change from the typical potato stuffing. 
Rs 50.
9/10

Masala dosa
A traditional masala dosa in every sense, served with chutney. The dosa is roasted to a nice deep brown crisp around the edges, yet soft and fluffy within. The flavourful potato palya is gently tempered.
Rs 46.
10/10

Filter coffee
Strong, robust coffee topped with a frothy cream. Pull your coffee to cool it down and end your meal in an authentic way. 
Rs 16.
9/10

Vidyarthi Bhavan, 32, Gandhi Bazaar Main Road, Basavanagudi, Bangalore 560 004; tel +91 080 2667 7588

Title: Non Vegetarian FEAST At RANGANNA MILITARY HOTEL|Famous Mutton Pulao, Kheema Gojju, Mudde |Bangalore
Description:
#MilitaryHotel #RestaurantsInBangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad


Drop in at Ranganna Military Hotel for breakfast, lunch or dinner to chow down on rustic meaty dishes full of flavour. 


Established way back in 1964, this eatery swears by its food and so do its patrons. Presently run by a husband-wife duo and their sons, the USP of the restaurant lies in the functioning of its kitchen. 


In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers Editor, Kripal Amanna visits the 60-year-old establishment to explore its kitchen with third generation Co-owner, Sendil Kumar. He discovers that the prep here begins as early as 7am, and every dish is prepared using secret recipes and local ingredients!

He also relishes a meaty spread for lunch, tasting from a hearty mutton leg broth, to steaming hot mutton pulao, kheema gojju, ragi mudde and more!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
Bannur Mutton chops
Mutton has a decent amount of bite. Most of the fat from the meat has rendered into the gravy enhancing the meaty flavours of this dish.
Rs 150
9/10

Bangude fry
Love the masala coating on this deep fried mackerel! The crunch, spice from the batter and prominent fish flavours make this a tasty fish fry!
Rs 150
8/10

Mutton head
a strong, deep flavoured dish, definitely for a hardcore carnivore to savour! Not my cup of tea though. 
Rs 125
7/10

Chicken leg masala
spicy leg of chicken cooked with the skin on. The gravy is robust and rich and the meat is cooked right down to the bone yet juicy!
Rs 80
9/10

Raagi mudde and saaru
Wholesome, filling mudde served with a spicy saaru or meat gravy.
Rs 36
7/10

Goat leg soup
A hearty broth that can make a sick man walk! Mellow in flavours, one can taste the intense flavours of the bones that’s extracted into the broth.
Rs 150
8/10

mutton pulao 
An aromatic pulao, where the meat is cooked with the short grain jeeraga samba rice. The rice is intense in its meaty flavour and studded with flecks of coriander and chilli. 
Rs 190
9/10

Mutton Kheema Gojju
Coarse mince, with flecks of fat, fresh peas and coriander. the kheema is coarsely ground, soaking up the masala. the peas pop in the mouth and the fat adds a burst of savouriness.
10/10
Rs 130

Kheema unde 
Very different from the gojju, the meat here is more finely ground and comes together as a ball or unde. The springy texture gives this meatball a chewy bite. The gravy, is lighter, with flavours of coriander. 
Rs 190
7/10

Title: Eating An Enormous Breakfast At HOLE IN THE WALL CAFÉ|Bangalore’s MOST Popular Eggs Breakfast Spot!
Description:
#AllDayBreakFast #Cafes #GourmetOnTheRoad

Popularly known for its breakfast options, mouthwatering egg creations (an omelette pizza too!), fluffy pancakes, loaded burgers and loaded toasts, The Hole In The Wall Café is perfect for lazy mornings and mid day brunches when in the city of Bengaluru!

In this episode of Hole In The Wall, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna meets proud owner, Nathan Harris, and shares  exclusive details on how the café  actually started out as a literal “hole in the wall”.
 
He also tucks into a large breakfast spread, tasting everything from a scrumptious English Breakfast, perfectly cooked Skillet Eggs, an all-time favourite Chicken Liver on Toast and sweet decadent waffles and pancakes!
  
The Hole In The Wall Café, No 4, 8th Main Road, Koramangala 4th Block, Koramangala, Bangalore 560 047; tel + 91 80 4094 9490

LOCATION TAG - https://g.page/THITWC?share


GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING

English breakfast
a hearty breakfast platter of eggs, juicy bacon, cooked just right and juicy, crunchy bacon! Not a big fan of the texture and flavour of the chicken sausage, the mash however, was seasoned well. 
Rs 320
8/10

Skillet eggs with chicken pepperoni and cheese
perfectly cooked eggs with the yolk still runny, savoury chicken pepperoni and slivers of chilli make for a creamy, meaty, spicy mouthful. easy to miss out on the flavour of the cheese, so make sure to order with extra cheese!
Rs 175
7/10

Meaty beef cheeseburger 
the juicy tenderloin patty, topped with fried egg, lettuce, tomato and cheese makes this a rustic burger that will leave you satisfied! The crumbly bun however,struggles to hold the burger together.
Rs 265
8/10

Chicken Liver On Toast
Love the savoury, deep flavour of the liver and its soft yielding texture. Cooked simply with lightly caramelised onions this is a dish every liver lover must try!
Rs 170
9/10

Veggie pizza Omelette
An interesting discovery, this pizza with an ‘eggy’ twist is tangy, savoury and has a nice crunch, thanks to the veggies. Order this dish when out with a bunch of friends.
Rs 165
7/10

Guava Juice
Surprisingly available all year round here, this pink guava juice is nourishingly tasty. The grainy texture of the guava is a great indicator of its freshness! 
Rs 75
8/10

Triple Chocolate pancakes
Chocolate nirvana! The chocolate pancakes, chocolate sauce and chocolate shavings ensure that every bite is decadent and super chocolatey!
Rs 220
8/10

Apple pie waffles
Two thick slices of perfectly cooked waffle topped with caramelised, cinnamon apples, caramel sauce and ice cream. The doughy texture of the waffle makes you want to keep eating! Look out for the slightly burnt edges, they are the best bits!
Rs 240
9/10

Title: Exploring Authentic Tamil-Brahmin Vegetarian Banana Leaf Meal At Iyer Mess In Bengaluru|Malleshwaram
Description:
#SouthIndianMeals #Bangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad

Serving authentic Tamil-Brahmin style meals for close to 60 years now, Iyer Mess is a go-to spot for lunch at Malleshwaram, Bengaluru. 

Founded in 1959, the mess is located in the home of owners, Venkatesh and Kamala Iyer.

The couple who have carried forward the tradition of serving homestyle vegetarian fare, use recipes handed down by Mr Iyer’s father to maintain taste and style of cooking.

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers Editor, Kripal Amanna visits the well-known mess to explore its kitchen and taste the ‘veg homely meal’.

The kitchen starts as early as 5:00 am every morning, preparing a standard banana leaf meal, comprising of Rice, Sambar, Rasam, Poriyal, Kootu, Pickle, Yoghurt, Vada and Appalam. On Sundays the menu features a special additions of Payasam and Mor Kuzambu.

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
Rs 70 for a vegetarian meal

Kose/ Cabbage Poriyal
A fresh, crunchy medley of cabbage and flecks of coconut, simply seasoned with mustard. 8/10


Kumbalakai/ Sweet Pumpkin Kootu
A mildly tempered, delicious preparation. Can taste the sweetness of the pumpkin, a tasty combination with the chapati.
9/10

Paruppu Vada
deep fried yet wholesome because of the lentil or paruppu in the vada. Flecks of onion impart hints of sweetness and the green chillies give it that spicy kick.
8/10


Chapati
Soft and light, a homestyle chapati.
7/10

Thayir Sadam/Curd Rice
thick and creamy, homemade curd. the milk for the curd is cooked on a coal stove!
9/10

Pickle
Spicy, bitter accompaniment called oorukka in Tamil.
7/10

Moolangi/ Radish Sambar
Big in flavour, the spicy, fiery kick from the chilli is very prominent in this sambar. The radish is cooked just right!
10/10

Rasam
a bit mellow. not as robustly flavoured as one would expect.
6/10

Appalam
Crunchy, deep fried, perfect when eaten with rice and rasam or sambar.
8/10

ADDRESS - Iyer Mess, No 4/3, West Park Road Between 7th and 8th Cross, Malleshwaram West, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560003; tel: 098860 78290

Title: Tasting the BEST Chicken and Mutton BIRYANI In Vellore! Making of Famous JOTHIE BIRIYANI
Description:
#Biryani #BiryaniInIndia #GourmetOnTheRoad

Gorge on mouthwatering biryani at Jothie Biriyani in Vellore, a 37-year-old establishment that has stood the test of time in the city.

This humble eatery has held onto a traditional recipe and way of making, for nearly four decades. Skilled cooks recreate this recipe by layering meat, rice and a rich, flavourful stock to make some of the most deliciously moist biryani. 

Large deghs fired using tamarind wood charcoal are used to make batches of Mutton and Chicken biryani at different times in day.

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits the kitchen to understand what goes into making this extraordinary dish!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
Mutton biryani
Fingerlicking rice! taste it just by itself and you are hit with a savoury kick of the meat that gets to your palate. the meat makes its presence felt even without it being your mouth! such a find. 
Rs 120
10/10

Chicken biryani 
Mildly coloured rice, flavours of the stock layered into it while cooking takes over the palate! flavours of the chicken biryani is in the rice and not the meat. just eat the rice to be totally happy and totally satisfied! the enne katrikai has a crunch,  sour edge, but this biryani rice needs no accompaniment. not even the meat! it's moist light leaving you wanting another bite. 
Rs 100
10/10

Chicken varuval
An appetising preparation. flavoured with onion, tomato also the curry leaf.skin on the chicken also gives it that flavour burst. 
Rs 90.
6/10

Title: The Perfect FAMILY BREAKFAST Stop | Sai Sangeet, Vaniyambadi | South Indian VEGETARIAN | TamilNadu
Description:
#Breakfast #HighwayFoodSpots #GourmetOnTheRoad

Sai Sangeet located between Vaniyambadi - Ambur NH 48, On Bangalore-Chennai highway is a delightful spot to stop over for breakfast!

More than any typical highway eatery, this restaurant has an interesting store out front that sells everything from windchimes, to clay pots and pans and also has animals and birds for entertainment!

The fare here is South Indian, with typical, Tamil Nadu breakfast dishes such as the podi uthappam, idli vada and ragi poori. 

Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna relishes some delicious highly recommended.
 breakfast staples in this episode of Gourmet On The Road also sharing a quick review on each dish!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING

Idli & chutneys

light and fluffy idli with a perfect wobble. a beautiful combination with the sweetness of coconut chutney. The podi with idli hits you right in the throat!
Rs 25.
8/10

Vada & chutneys
Nourishing vada with the bite of the lentil intact. vada is crisp, studded with onions chillies and peppercorns. crunchy on the outside, soft and coarse within. a seriously delicious vada!  
Rs 35.
10/10

Ragi poori
only place where I've tasted a ragi poori. can feel the weight and the bite of the ragi millet. filling and nourishing, two of these with some lightly spiced sagu and chutney and you're good to go!
Rs 65.
7/10

Podi uthappam
a specialty here. podi is completely smeared on the soft, fluffy texture of the dosa. the crunch of the podi and spices together with chutney rounds off all the sharp flavours. the sambar is a nourishing accompaniment. 
Rs 75.
10/10

Black jaggery halwa/ karupatti halwa
nice and warm on the palate. Toasty, intense jaggery flavours. copious amount of ghee makes this a super-rich halwa. a halwa you can't finish on your own!
Rs 70.
8/10

Milk and date halwa 
can taste the milk solids and flecks of date in the halwa. not too sweet, not too rich. A dessert I can finish entirely on my own. 
Rs 40.
9/10

Filter coffee
nice, thick and strong! don't forget to pull your coffee to cool it down and for that extra froth. 
Rs 30.
8/10

Title: Exploring the Vaniyambadi BIRYANI at 40-year AHMEDIA HOTEL| Mutton Biryani | Chicken | Quail Masala
Description:
#Biryani #TamilNadu #GourmetOnTheRoad 

Established in 1975, Ahmedia Hotel, a name highly familiar with the locals of Vaniyambadi is the quintessential non-vegetarian lunch stopover in town!

Especially known for its aromatic Biryani made using long grain basmati rice, unlike the typical jeeraga samba rice used in biryanis elsewhere in Tamilnadu, this restaurant claims that its biryani is what brings patrons back each time. 

Aside from the biryani, the mutton and quail preparations here are what one should definitely indulge in here. In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits the kitchen to discover what makes this biryani great and also orders a full lunch meal complete with piping hot Mutton Biryani, Mutton Chukka, Chicken Chukka, Teetar Pepper Masala, Chicken Kebab and more to savour the whole experience of dining here.

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
Mutton chukka
meat is roasted superbly well. not your typical Chettinad/ Kongu chukka. very mild and gentle, allows you to enjoy the flavours of the meat. deep brown on the outside and moist and pink on the inside. 
Rs 150.
8/10

Chicken chukka
crisped curry leaves add an extra dimension to the dish. excellent dish for a chicken lover!
8/10

Quail pepper dry
Cooked well although quail is tough to get right. Prominent pepper flavours together with the characteristic crispy curry leaves makes this an intense dish.
Rs 130
9/10


Quail phaal/masala
thick gravy with the quail having soaked in all the masala. delicious! a dish to definitely order here! all you need is a piece if parota to mop up all the goodness. 
Rs 150.
10/10


Bheja/brain pepper fry
in-your-face pepper hit with underlying flavours of curry leaves, onion and tomato.  Can be enjoyed both with roti and biryani.
Rs 140
8/10


Vanjaram fish fry 
Fish tastes fine but doesn't really make the cut. slightly overcooked. the masala hasn't penetrated inside. I prefer the meat dishes here. 
Rs 160.
5/10


Chicken kebab
Tastes like a regular kebab. A tad bit dry. if you love your kebab, this dish is worth trying. 
Rs 140.
6/10


Mutton Biryani
certainly an aromatic biryani! made with the long grain basmati. very delicate in it's flavours. pink juicy pieces of mutton, you can taste the pure flavour of the meat. no heavy spices weighing down the meat. this is a delicious biryani!
Rs 200.
10/10

Title: Desi Gourmet OMELETTES! Streetfood Eggs Taken To A Whole New Level| Egg Factor! Bangalore Food Tour!
Description:
#Eggs #StreetFoodInBangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad

Egg Factor – Street House, a street kiosk whips ups gourmet-style omelettes that are a far cry from the regular masala or cheese versions.

Using ingredients such as chicken, prawn, grilled fish, goat brain and even fruits such as pineapples or strawberries, ex-cruise line chef, Kumar is dishing up fancy, exotic and unheard of toppings and fillings to go with the humble omelette, in a street shop setting.

In this Gourmet On The Road video, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna discovers what inspired this well-travelled, ex-cruise line chef’s vision, the incidents that led to the creation of offbeat toppings and fillings, the delectable omelettes you can try here and more!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING

Chicken and Cheese Omelette
A loaded omelette! chicken is well marinated. The crunchy veggies complement the gooey savouriness of the cheese. Can definitely feel the chilli kick in the seasoning!
Rs 150.
8/10

Pepper Prawn Omelette
You smell the inviting aromas of freshly ground spices and fresh herbs. This makes all the difference! the prawns are torched, cooked just right, can taste the sweetness. The use of desi eggs gives this omelette a wholesome touch!
Rs 200
8/10

Goat Brain Omelette
Luscious, creamy, custardy! The heavy masalas balance the rich flavours of the brain. The lush buttery texture of the brain with the fluffy egg is a delightful mouthful.
Rs 200
10/10

Pineapple And Cheese Omelette
A sweet, hot and sour medley on the palate! The garlic and chilli in the pineapple is a surprising touch. a tart zingy acidity and a chilli heat in the back of your throat. A savoury fruit omelette. This is definitely a first for me!
Rs 130
6/10

Title: Exploring Traditions & Tasting the VEGETARIAN LUNCH THALI At Mavalli Tiffin Rooms | MTR | Bangalore
Description:
#VegetarianRestaurants #IconicEateriesInBangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad

One of Bengaluru’s most iconic restaurants for traditional South Indian breakfast and meals, Mavalli Tiffin Rooms or MTR is a culinary institution.
 
Nearly 100 years old, located in a quaint double-storey building with halls packed full of patrons, both old and new, Mavalli Tiffin Rooms, Lalbagh is part of the history of Bengaluru.
 
The eatery today is known for its rich culinary traditions, that has struck a chord with people not just in the country, but across the world! 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor visits the iconic eatery to lunch with Hema Malini Maiya, Managing Partner. He explores the nuances of what makes MTR so special over a traditional lunch.

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
Lunch Thali - Rs 270

Black grape juice
No lunch at mtr has begun without this refreshing drink, that is served no matter grape season or not!
7/10

Kosambari
Fresh, crunchy salad. Typically to be eaten at the start of the meal.
7/10

Raw banana palya/ balekai palya
tasty fibre. coconut adds a nice texture. made with a south canara masala, that is very gentle. Looks spicy but isn’t!
8/10

Poori Sagu
Fluffy pooris best eaten with the sweet and tangy saagu and thick chutney. the savoury and slight sweetness from the potatoes are balanced with the spice hit from the chutney.  
8/10

Sabbakki kadle bele payasam
Perfectly sweet dessert. has some chana dal that adds texture and breaks the gluten and the sweetness. helps you refresh your palate in between all the food.
8/10

Mini masala dosa
dosa has a slight tartness from the batter. can taste the masala in every bite. the chutney adds flavour and spice. the slightly grainy bite of fried gram in the chutney makes it the perfect accompaniment to the dosa.
10/10

Rave vade
a delicious, crunchy fritter. this accompaniment on the thali is different everyday.
6/10

Bisibelebath
a flavourful bisibelebath. the bite of the vegetables is what makes this dish. it is robustly spiced. Best eaten with the raita.
10/10

Kara pongal with hunase hannu gojju
A Thursday special. This flavourful dish sings on your palate. the tangy tamarind chutney helps cut through the spice from the ginger and peppercorns in the dish. 
9/10

White rice and bendekai huli with ghee
typical south Canara Style huli/ sambar. super tasty! Slightly tart in flavour, you can taste the spices and the crunch of the vegetable. Best eaten with ghee to round off all its flavours.
9/10

Rice and rasam 
piping hot rasam/ saaru! can taste the spices that are well balanced. sourness from tomato and tamarind is balanced with a slight sweetness from the jaggery. The spice comes from the red byadgi chilli. great when eaten with the appala and uppinakayi or pickle.
9/10

Curd rice 
lightly seasoned. curd rice helps settle your tummy. makes for a lovely end to the rice courses. 
7/10 

Ice cream and fruit mixture 
this ice cream, made in house and with very little fat - almost like a rich sorbet -  is only available at mtr and is called the american ice cream. served with a ‘french fruit mixture’ as they call it. 
8/10

Gulab jamoon
Flat, oblong jamoon. Light, not cloyingly sweet, a bit of camphor traditionally added for flavour.
8/10

Beeda or pan 
Stuffed with fennel, gulkand and betel nut to refresh your mouth. a perfect digestive. rounds up a perfectly satisfying and happy lunch here. 
7/10

Title: Lunch At SHIVAJI MILITARY HOTEL |Bangalore’s most popular Mutton, Chicken Donne Biryani|Best Biryani
Description:
#DonneBiryani #MilitaryHotelsInBangalore #GourmetOnTheRoad

An age-old, iconic establishment in the city of Bengaluru, Shivaji Military Hotel is renowned for its Maratha cuisine.

The crowd favourite, “donne-style” biryani here is cooked on dum using coal and robustly flavoured with stock, chunks of meat and a secret masala blend all made in-house. The biryani can be enjoyed with other meat heavy preparations like Mutton Dry, Chicken Kalmi, Liver Fry and more.

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits this bustling eatery to discover what makes it popular with the locals while he indulges in a full-fledged meal!

GOTR RATING
Chicken Dry
the chicken is smothered in masala, making every bite flavourful. Chicken cooked just right. 
Rs 160
8/10

Mutton Dry
great quality meat. cooked dry with fat trimmings that imparts a deep savouriness, a meaty bite. So good!
Rs 190
9/10

Chicken Leg/ Kalmi Masala
plump, spicy chicken thighs. it's juicy, succulent inside and has a peppery bite.
Rs 160
8/10

Mutton Donne Biryani
piping hot biryani with gentle inviting aromas. the rice has all the flavours of the biryani, is cooked perfectly well and even has a bite to it. the meat is soft, juicy, fatty, all things you want in a piece of meat! a seriously tasty biryani!
Rs 220
10/10

Mutton Liver
cooked in a green chilli, coriander and mint masala that has a freshness to it. meaty piece of liver. a tad dry for my liking.
Rs 150
6/10

Chicken Donne Biryani
pleasantly surprised with the flavours for a chicken biryani. lightly spiced with a chilli kick that you feel at the back of your throat. chicken with the rice makes for a lovely mouthful. the pachadi (yoghurt salad) helps cool off the heat.
Rs 180
8/10

Chilli Chicken
not your typical chinese-style chilli chicken. this maratha chilli chicken uses tons of green chilli. if you love your food spicy then this dish is for you.
Rs 160
7/10

Title: A ‘CHEESY’ Spin on Tandoori Chicken Made Without A Tandoor! | Easy Recipes| Scamorza Stuffed Chicken
Description:
#TandooriChicken #Recipes #FoodLoversRecipes
A contemporary spin to good ol’ tandoori chicken, the scamorza filled tandoori chicken breast at Lazy Suzy, Bangalore is a coming together of interesting flavours that perfectly mimic the essence of the popular Indian delicacy!

Chef Udayshankar Shenoy of Lazy Suzy recreates the flavours of tandoori chicken with this recipe that boasts of various delicious elements. And it isn’t cooked in a tandoor!
 
He begins by stuffing a tandoori spiced chicken breast with scamorza cheese, this adds the the most important smoked flavour to the dish. Once pan-fried, and finished in the oven, the breast is served on a bed of chokha or Indian spiced potatoes and a tomato butter sauce.
 
Recipe by Chef Udayshankar Shenoy, Lazy Suzy, Bangalore

Description:
#ChettinadCuisine #Salem #GourmetOnTheRoad

Hotel Rajaganapathy, a tiny eatery located at Arthanari Nagar, Salem is frequented by locals for its non-vegetarian meals and Chettinad style meat fries. 

Carrying forward its 40-year old legacy is owner, Vaidyanathan, a gentleman who has been working the stove since he was a 7-year-old.

In this episode of Gourmet Of On The Road, Food Lovers Editor, tastes a lavish non-vegetarian meal with a variety of dishes as interacts with the owner and his sons to find what makes this spot special!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
Mutton Chukka
Roasted with a bunch of spices and cooked on the bone with the marrow rendered into the gravy.  The meat definitely has a bite to it. Rs 200. 9/10

Natti chicken fry
pieces of shredded country chicken roasted in a dry masala with loads of curry leaves. Rs 200. 7/10

Mutton boti
boti cooked to perfection, almost melts in the mouth. Rs 150. 8/10

Pigeon roast 
Intense, gamey flavours. The curry masala made using hard spices complements the meat. 
Have to wrestle with tiny bones to get to the meat! Rs 200. 9/10

Natti Chicken biryani
The flavour in this biryani runs deep. the country chicken has a chewy texture but the flavourful rice makes up for this. pairs well with the special, rich chicken gravy. Rs 200. 9/10

Country chicken pepper chukka
very distinctive, peppery taste. Rs 200. 7/10

Chicken chintamani fry
Simple preparation of chicken tossed with shallots and red chillies. A bit on the salty side. Rs 150. 5/10

Title: CHETTINAD non-veg Lunch at Salem’s most popular SELVI MESS |Biryani |Mutton|Turkey Chukka |Prawn Fry
Description:
#ChettinadCuisine #Salem #GourmetOnTheRoad 

Selvi Mess, in Salem, Tamil Nadu, known for its Chettinad-style fare dishes out specials in true country style. Although a tiny eatery, this spot is unmissable to the traveller’s eye owing to the clamour coming from a full house of diners. In nearly 35 years of its existence, the iconic mess called a ‘mess’ has amassed a devoted audience, turning into the perfect pit stop for a delicious meal!

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna tastes a full meal of the most highly recommended dishes here including a piping hot Catla Fry, robust Mutton Chukka and the signature Turkey Chukka, the special for the day. 

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
Prawn fry 
A semi dry preparation of tiny prawns cooked in roasted spices and onions. the tiny prawns add flavour and punch to the dish.
Rs. 210  
9/10

Turkey chukka
Cooked just right although turkey is a tough meat to nail. The deeply roasted masala adds an extra dimension to the dish.
Rs. 200
8/10

Mutton chukka
A true blue Chettinad preparation made with tiny bits of meat cooked on the bone. You can taste the signature spice mix and pepper with every bite. 
Rs 200
10 /10

Goat Head Curry
Delicious! The meat and fat melts in your mouth with each morsel.  
Rs 180
8 /10

Country chicken chukka
Naati style chicken cooked with the skin, deep flavour. Rs 215
7/10

Mutton biryani
Served with a customary egg, this biryani is made with the short grain jeerga samba rice. This style of making a biryani uses copious amounts of tomato that lends a tart flavour to the dish.
Rs 210
8/10

Mutton gravy
The mutton gravy is a delicious side to the biryani. The spices are raw and coarse, with the fat perfectly rendered into the gravy.
 8/10

Catla fry
Caught in the Mettur dam, a specialty of the region. Lightly coated in masala and deep fried, it makes for a scrumptious, mildly spicy dish..
Rs 110
9 /10

Rice & Rasam 
The unlimited rice and rasam are perfect to be eaten with the robust meat fries. The tangy rasam is a great wash down to a non-vegetarian meal! 
Rs. 100
 8/10

Selvi Mess, No 212, Opp New Bus stand, Arthanari Nagar, Swarnapuri, Salem,

Title: Tasting SEVEN Kinds Of HALEEM |Haleem Festival|Turkey|Jackfruit|Prawn| Duck Haleem |Ramadan Special
Description:
#RamadanFeast #Haleem #GourmetOnTheRoad

Haleem, a delicacy especially during the month of Ramadan is a filling, wholesome meal  packed with essential nutrients. Made with ingredients like lentils, spices and broken wheat, along with spices, ghee, dry fruits, and saffron, the haleem is said to be easy on the stomach but also full of nourishment that helps restore energy. 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers Editor, Kripal Amanna indulges in seven variations of the haleem at Punjab Bistro to celebrate this holy month in full swing! From a Vegetable Haleem made with over five kinds of veggies, Raw Jackfruit Haleem, to Prawn, Duck and even Turkey Haleem, this haleem festival has something for everyone! 

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATINGS

Vegetable Haleem
Great choice for vegetarians on the lookout to try haleem, its texture mimics a meat haleem! The fried veggies as a garnish adds a beautiful crunch.
Rs 275 for a full portion. 8/10

Kathal Haleem
meaty bite for a vegetarian haleem. can taste the subtle sweetness of the raw jackfruit.
Rs 295 for a full portion. 7/10

Prawn haleem
Light in its flavours. Definitely needed the birista and coriander for added depth. The spicy prawn chutney accompaniment is overpowering.  
Rs 475 for a full portion. 6/10

Chicken haleem
mellow flavours with a bit of an underlying tartness. a great combination with the sheermal.
Rs 340 for a full portion. 8/10

Turkey haleem
light in colour but deep and bright in flavours! the fried turkey is a little salty perfect to cut through the monotony of flavours. Rs 575 for a full portion. 9/10

Duck haleem
The haleem for duck lovers. deep flavours of the duck are balanced when eaten with birista and coriander. Personally, a bit strong for my liking. Rs 450 for a full portion. 6/10

Mutton haleem
Classic, textbook haleem. Its rich, meaty savouriness shines in every bite. piece of ghee fried mutton on top makes for a wonderful bonus! Rs 400 for a full portion. 10/10

Description:
#Breakfast #SouthIndianBreakfast #GourmetOnTheRoad 

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna visits the Krishnagiri outpost of Sree Saravana Bhavan that has spawned several other restaurants trying to imitate its menu under its name. 

Savouring some of Tamil Nadu’s breakfast staples, the idli vada, masala dosa including a fiery podi dosa, catch Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna’s full review in this video.

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING

Idli Vada
Soft, almost-pillowy idlis served with an assortment of chutneys, leaving you spoilt for choice. Vadas are perfectly crunchy. Rs 60. 10/10 


Pongal
Lightly spiced, mellow pongal that is delicately tempered with ghee and studded with cashews. The peppercorns help cut through the richness! Rs 62. 8/10

Masala Dosa
A thin, crisp dosa, surprisingly light on oil! Each bite with the spiced mash potato is super satisfying! Rs 71. 9/10

Podi dosa
You can taste the fire of the podi. This spirited condiment is a Tamil Nadu staple made with lentils, chillies and garlic. Rs 76. 7/10

Idiyappam
A simple dish but delicious! The steamed rice flour noodles are best when lapped up with the sweet coconut milk flavoured with cardamom. Rs 55. 10/10

Filter coffee
Dark, deep-roasted coffee topped with a frothy foam. Rs 25. 8/10

Description:
#RamadanFoodTrail #FrazerTown #GourmetOnTheRoad

Frazer town located in the heart of Bangalore is nothing less than a food lovers heaven! 

With streets like Mosque Road and MM Road lined with restaurants and eateries dishing out some of the most delicious non vegetarian fare, this spot in the city is a must-visit.

In this episode of Gourmet On The Road, Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna takes off on this busy street, during the month of Ramadan together with a friend to taste and review much loved dishes such as the Haleem, Kheema Samosa, a delectable Nalli Nihari and more! 

Gourmet On The Road Ratings
MUTTON KHEEMA MINI SAMOSA 
a speciality at Albert, he thin skin is fried to a crisp with a moist kheema filling. Delicious! Rs 480 a kilo. 10 /10

BRAIN PUFF
piping hot, flaky puff stuffed with a custardy mutton brain that dissolves in your mouth!  Rs 35 per puff. 
9/10

KHEEMA NAAN
prominent taste of onions and a meaty savouriness makes the kheema naan a tasty, filling indulgence! Rs120 6/10

KHOVA NAAN 
the filling of the khova or reduced milk solids shine in this dessert puff that isn’t overly sweet. Rs100 7/10

HYDERABADI MUTTON HALEEM 
A wholesome dish, this haleem is velvety, gooey and is crowned with fried onions, mint and lemon juice. The twang of the lemon and texture from the onion helps cut through the richness. Rs 250 8/10

QUBANI KI MEETHA
This Hyderabadi speciality is a rich and pulpy apricot dessert laced with a  hint of saffron. The sugary goodness makes the perfect accompaniment to the haleem. Rs 190. 7/10

PAYA WITH NAAN
This gelatinous, warm and nourishing stew made with lamb trotters is to be enjoyed steaming hot with some naan! Rs150. 8/10

NALLI NIHARI
The slow cooked, rich nihari is superbly flavourful. You can tell that the gravy has been cooked for hours to intensify the deliciousness! Rs 350. 10/10

KARACHI NAAN 
The Karachi naan is a light yet dry making it the right accompaniment to soak up all the gravy and its unctuous goodness. Rs 45 for 2. 9/10

Title: Make This Delectable Bengali Patali Gur Mousse Today! | Indian Dessert Recipe | Jaggery Sweet Treats
Description:
Nothing captures the essence of a community the way its food does. Food Lovers brings to you recipes and traditional cuisine handed down through generations while sharing fond memories and cherished emotions of its maker. 

In this episode of Recipes & Traditions, Ms Ajantha Purkayastha, a social worker, reminisces enjoying delicious desserts made with jaggery and thickened milk or pancakes topped with melted jaggery, growing up. 

She also shares how she wanted her love for gur to pass on to her kids. To make sure the custom of enjoying jaggery continues, she concocted a dish that made use of jaggery in a more inspired-by-the-West way. She calls it the Patali Gur Mousse, that is light, perfectly sweet and might we also add, eggless!

Watch this video to make your own!

Title: Home Cooked Christian Food At MARYBAI’S Mangalore| MEATY DELIGHTS!|PORK BAFAT|FISH FRIES|Food Lovers
Description:
#NonVegetarian #MangaloreanCuisine #GourmetOnTheRoad

If one is looking for a simple yet sumptuous home-cooked meal, Marybai’s in Valencia, Mangalore is the place to visit! 

Located in a small home, this eatery has been making its patrons happy with authentic Mangalore Christian cuisine since 1984, when Marybai, the founder set up the restaurant.

Dishes that have been coined to be delicacies at Marybai’s are its meat preparations such as pork chilli, chicken pepper, beef bafat and pork bafat. These dishes are meant to be eaten with a humble thali to enjoy a complete experience here.

Food Lovers’ Editor, Kripal Amanna, digs into this delicious spread together with some local, tasty fish fries!

GOURMET ON THE ROAD RATING
BOILED RICE AND PICKLE MEALS 
A nourishing, home cooked meal worth its price. Rs 40. 7/10

SARDINE FISH CURRY 
A curry with a tart edge, made with the humble boothai or sardine. Perfect when eaten with boiled rice. 7/10

CHICKEN PEPPER 
This dry preparation is loaded with coriander and pepper. Rs 70 9/10

PORK PEPPER 
Fat has rendered down beautifully. meat is unctuous with a smokey flavour. A must-try here! Rs 80 10/10

BEEF BAFAT  
The meat and masala sing in unison. Very unique in its style and preparation. Rs 90 9/10

PORK BAFAT

Title: Sriracha Brings UNEXPLORED EAST ASIAN CUISINE To Bengaluru | Sriracha Bengaluru | Food Lovers
Description:
#Sriracha #AsianCusine #NewRestaurants
Chef Vikas Seth, Culinary Director of Sriracha traces the path taken by their team of chefs across the Orient, making stops at Thailand, Malaysia, Japan, Indonesia, Vietnam, China, Cambodia and Singapore. 

The result is a menu with creations that blend the age-old East Asian traditions with the new.

Diners can savour an array of dishes from across, beginning with robust grills made live with choices of turmeric and red chili king prawns with plum and pineapple salsa or scallops with togarashi dust;  Taiwanese hamburgers or baos and charcoal seafood or roasted pumpkin and water chestnut dumplings.

The restaurant continues the tradition of som tam made tableside, alongside introducing charcoal Khmer barbecue for the first time in India. Other Cambodian specials include, lemongrass poached shrimp fresh spring roll and fish amok trey, a traditional Cambodian dish steamed in a cup made from banana leaves.

The menu comprises popular desserts such as the banana cake with homemade coconut ice cream and Sumatra dark chocolate mousse.

To add to the personalised experience, the restaurant also makes its own sriracha!

Sriracha, 608, 12th Main Road, 7th Cross, HAL 2nd Stage, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560 038; tel +91 80 4220 0081

Title: 500 Year Old Groundnut Fair In Bengaluru | Kadalekai Parishe | Basavangudi | Bangalore | Food Lovers
Description:
#Bangalore #India #GroundnutFestival
Held annually on the last Monday of Karthika Masa, (an auspicious month in the Hindu calendar dedicated to Lord Shiva) the Kadalekai Parishe is a tribute to Lord Basava. Farmers from across Karnataka and states of Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh offer their annual harvest of groundnuts at the Bull Temple in Basavanagudi.

Mounds of peanuts adorn the lanes of this neighbourhood for two days, as multitudes of locals purchase peanuts - raw, dried, boiled, roasted, salted, spiced, fried and sugar coated - at bargains.

A range of snacks such as bajji, bonda, batthaas, bendu and coloured sodas are also on sale, alongside stalls selling bangles, traditional toys and clay trinkets and plastic and glass dolls. 

Kadalekai Parishe, Bull Temple Road, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560 004

Title: Discover Khmer Barbecue At Sriracha | Khmer Cuisine | Cambodia | Food Lovers
Description:
#Khmer #Barbecue #AsianCuisine

Inspired by his travels to Cambodia, Chef Vikas Seth is bringing Khmer cuisine to Sriracha and adding his own spin to it with the Khmer barbecue table. 

This immersive dining experience engaging all senses, has the chef cooking tableside.

Title: Preparing a Traditional Lasagna
Description:
Italian Chef Giuseppe Lioce shares the recipe for a traditional home-style lasagna.

Show more for the full recipe.


A comforting family recipe for this staple dish from northern Italy, that layers the creaminess of béchamel sauce and the tangy flavours of bolognese with al dente sheets of pasta.

Ingredients

For pasta

100 gms semolina flour
10 ml egg white
2 egg yolks
Salt to taste

For béchamel sauce

500 ml milk
100 gm roux
200 gm parmesan cheese
A pinch of nutmeg

For bolognese sauce

100 gms beef mince
300 gms tomato sauce
50 gms carrot
50 gms celery
50 gms leek
50 gms onion
3 gms rosemary
100 ml red wine
10 ml olive oil
2-3 sprigs of basil
1 bay leaf
Salt to taste

Method

For the pasta

To make the pasta dough, knead together mix semolina flour, egg yolk, egg white and salt.
When the dough is ready, leave it to rest for 30 minutes to an hour.
Now roll the pasta dough to sheets to 5 mm thickness.
Blanch the pasta in boiling water and keep aside.
 
For béchamel sauce

Make a béchamel sauce by adding the milk to the roux, made with butter and flour.
Add parmesan cheese and a pinch of nutmeg into the sauce.
 
For bolognese sauce

In a pan add olive oil and sauté the carrots, leeks, celery and onions.
Add rosemary to the vegetables.
Once the vegetables are cooked, add beef in to the pan and cook through.
Add red wine and allow the beef to simmer for a while.
Add the tomato sauce, basil and bayleaf and cook on a low flame for 2 hours.
Keep stirring the sauce at regular intervals.
When the bolognese has thickened, check for seasoning add salt to taste.
